sessions.title: From Event Streams to Enterprise AI with Cloudera Anywhere Cloud
sessions.abstract: Distributed edge assets, remote sensors, and transactional systems often leave operational data isolated from enterprise AI platforms. This session demonstrates how global organizations break down these operational boundaries using Cloudera Anywhere Cloud. Discover an event-driven architectural blueprint that standardizes real-time streaming, unifies hybrid pipelines, and routes live activity directly into downstream analytics and AI agents. Learn how a single operational standard across hybrid environments simplifies data sovereignty and enables real-time enterprise automation.

sessions.title: Edge-to-Action: Streaming On-Prem Data to Power Agentic AI
sessions.abstract: To build production-ready autonomous agents, AI requires continuous, real-time context. Deploying Cloudera’s services directly on-premises unlocks critical edge streaming telemetry, ingesting high-frequency data into Apache Iceberg tables on Cloudera’s Open Data Lakehouse on AWS. Learn how grounding generative AI models with streaming telemetry and dynamic operational context enables real-time anomaly detection. Discover how autonomous multi-agent workflows leverage streaming RAG and Model Context Protocol tools to execute closed-loop business actions from alerting operational teams to dispatching automated remediations without creating processing bottlenecks on primary databases.

sessions.title: What's new with the AWS Sustainability service
sessions.abstract: If you've ever wanted to know more about the environmental impact of your cloud usage, this session is for you.  In this lightning talk, learn about the latest features of the AWS Sustainability service, including expanded impact areas beyond carbon, increased data granularity, and programmatic access via APIs. We walk through how to use the service to track progress against your sustainability goals and integrate environmental data into your existing workflows and reporting processes. Whether you're just getting started or already reporting on cloud emissions, this session has you covered.

sessions.title: AWS AI from chips to agents: The end-to-end production AI foundation
sessions.abstract: The AI experiment is over. Now it has to work. This session walks through the AWS AI Platform end-to-end, starting at the chip layer with AWS Trainium and AWS Graviton delivering up to 40% better price performance. From there, model inference and customization through Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Then production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every layer co-designed so workloads move across the stack without rearchitecting. You will leave knowing which service handles which job, where the layers connect to accelerate production timelines, and how to keep your architecture open as your AI strategy evolves.

sessions.title: Using AI for Impact: Achieving Sustainability and ROI on AWS
sessions.abstract: AI is accelerating sustainability at unprecedented speed, but only if the infrastructure behind it keeps pace. Learn how customers leverage AI for autonomous building control, emission factor mapping, supply chain carbon accounting, disclosure drafting, and transforming procurement data into sustainability intelligence using natural language. Then explore how AWS makes AI infrastructure more sustainable through hardware design decisions that minimize embodied carbon, custom silicon optimized for energy efficiency, and ML-driven data center optimization. Leave with a clear understanding of the AWS services powering these solutions, how AWS is building a more sustainable infrastructure, and how to get started.

sessions.title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
sessions.abstract: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.

sessions.title: From chips to applications: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier
sessions.abstract: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack — chips, servers, software, and the models built on top — each layer making the next faster, cheaper, and more capable. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. Leave with understanding of how each layer of innovation compounds and where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.

sessions.title: Best practices to build, connect and optimize agents on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Ship agents fast. Connect to anything. Optimize continuously. In this session, learn best practices for the full agent lifecycle on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build: go from local to production with microVM isolation, persistent memory, and any framework. Connect: access MCP servers, knowledge bases, and APIs through Gateway with automatic authentication. Optimize: trace every model call with OpenTelemetry-compatible observability and run continuous evaluations. Walk away with architectural patterns and implementation strategies to ship your first agent in minutes, not months.

sessions.title: Scalable LLM inference, easy on the ops: CrowdStrike on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: When adversaries move in seconds, security has to move faster. CrowdStrike shares how they built scalable, real-time LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker to power threat detection at massive scale, where sub-second latency is a hard requirement. Learn how dedicated, configurable endpoints gave them full control over performance, while SageMaker AI's managed infrastructure removed the operational overhead. Walk away with a blueprint for running latency-critical workloads on SageMaker Managed Inference, without running the stack yourself.

sessions.title: The age of vertical models: training to deployment on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Purpose-built domain models are delivering breakthrough results. Intercom's Fin AI agent resolves over 2 million customer issues per week, powered by vertical foundation models that achieve superior accuracy at a fraction of the cost and latency of general-purpose alternatives. Learn how Intercom's ML team trained, evaluated, and deployed domain-specific models on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and how vertical models are unlocking new levels of performance on real production workloads. Walk away with a blueprint for building and serving your own vertical FM at scale.

sessions.title: Accelerate Domain Specific AI Development with SageMaker AI and Forge
sessions.abstract: SageMaker AI & Forge accelerates AI solution development on AWS. In this session, you will learn about Forge capabilities and how you can use these to create custom evaluations for your use case, effectively incorporate your data into your AI solution, and select the best model for your needs.

sessions.title: From Cost to Compliance: Scaling Scalable GenAI with Amazon Nova
sessions.abstract: Enterprises putting generative AI into production face three converging pressures: controlling inference cost at scale, meeting compliance and data-residency requirements, and migrating off incumbent models without losing accuracy  or quality. Amazon Nova is purpose-built for this reality. In this session, learn how organizations across regulated  and cost-sensitive industries are standardizing on Amazon Nova to run high-volume GenAI workloads at a fraction of the  cost while meeting strict compliance requirements.

sessions.title: Build Voice AI experiences with Amazon Polly and Transcribe
sessions.abstract: Give your applications a voice and ears. This session shows how Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech. See how to build real-time voice agents, and multilingual experiences, with practical patterns for latency, accuracy, and scale.

sessions.title: Building conversational AI with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
sessions.abstract: We'll explore how bidirectional audio streaming enables natural, low-latency dialogue, with expressive voices across multiple languages. See how new capabilities like cross-modal voice-and-text switching, asynchronous tool calling for multi-step tasks, and a large context window let you build voice agents, customer service automation, and conversational apps.

sessions.title: Agentic commerce: Use AI agents with AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: Managing software procurement across dozens of tools, teams, and accounts is slow and error-prone. In this lightning talk, we use AI agents to automate the buyer journey on AWS Marketplace to discover and evaluate products, accept discounted offers instantly, enforce governance, achieve operational excellence, request refunds and cancellations, and gain unified visibility into spend and cost management. Compress procurement from weeks to minutes while maintaining governance and financial controls.

sessions.title: What's new in Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: AI moves fast: new models, new economics, new governance capabilities. Attend this breakout to learn about the latest innovations across Amazon Bedrock. We cover the newest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and more, the latest inference advances, and updates across security, governance, and cost. Whether you are new to Bedrock or want to keep up with the latest updates, this session offers a little bit for everyone. Leave knowing what is available today and where to focus next.

sessions.title: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI
sessions.abstract:
Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it.
What you'll learn
⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots
⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve
⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments
⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps

sessions.title: Hands-On Workshop: Build & Deploy AI Agents with Cloudera Agent Studio
sessions.abstract: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera Agent Studio. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will build multi-agent workflows without code, develop agentic chatbots for data access, learn Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration with AWS tools including Amazon Bedrock and PuppyGraph, and explore the latest Cloudera AI and Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments.

sessions.title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike
sessions.abstract: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments.

sessions.title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS
sessions.abstract: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps.

sessions.title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect
sessions.abstract: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation.

sessions.title: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery
sessions.abstract: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare.

sessions.title: Own Your Harness: Control Cost & Risk in Enterprise-Wide AI Adoption
sessions.abstract: The fastest way to lose control of AI is to let agents multiply without a harness. This talk walks through Presidio's journey from scattered pilots to enterprise-wide adoption, built on a custom orchestration layer that treats cost, identity, and policy as first-class concerns. Attendees will get an inside look at the architectural decisions, guardrails, and economic models that let us scale AI use predictably across the business. If you're weighing governance (cost and risk) against velocity, this is the playbook you want from day one.

sessions.title: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy
sessions.abstract: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at Resolve AI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions.

sessions.title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps
sessions.abstract: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment.

sessions.title: Machines on Call for Humans: Agents to run and fix your prod
sessions.abstract: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans.

sessions.title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.

sessions.title: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One
sessions.abstract: Every AI application touching real people can fail in ways that cause harm. In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.

sessions.title: Building a governance foundation for your agent platform
sessions.abstract: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.

sessions.title: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
sessions.abstract: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics—powering interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving—but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. In this builders session, we deploy and optimize a real-time video world model on AWS Trainium using AWS Neuron Agentic Development skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel optimization through natural-language interaction. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. Walk away with practical patterns for using agentic tools to achieve optimized, real-time inference on purpose-built AI silicon.

sessions.title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
sessions.abstract: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. Leave with practical skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents at scale.

sessions.title: Run coding agents at scale with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Developers want to run Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this session, learn how AgentCore runtime hosts coding agents with microVM isolation, persistent filesystems, and Bedrock model access. Build code review agents, PR automation, and repo consolidation workflows, then deploy to AgentCore for production. Run agents in parallel, wake them on GitHub events, and let them work while you sleep.

sessions.title: Build a knowledge assistant that scales across your company on Bedrock
sessions.abstract: In this builders session, build a multi-tenant knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases, a fully managed vector store. Learn how to implement secure tenant isolation, ingest documents through the API, and use the Agentic Retrieval API to return multi-hop, cited answers. Along the way, tackle the hard parts: concurrency-aware ingestion, zero cross-tenant leakage under load, and an architecture that scales to thousands of tenants on a single knowledge base. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse for enterprise search.

sessions.title: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
sessions.abstract: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.

sessions.title: Serving LLMs on Trainium: From vLLM Neuron to EKS at Scale
sessions.abstract: This chalk talk gives a full-stack view of scaling LLM serving on AWS Trainium. We start with vLLM Neuron, the open-source plugin that brings vLLM to Trainium with features like continuous batching, speculative decoding, and multimodal support. We then show how advanced serving architectures — disaggregated inference, prefix-cache-aware routing, and vision encoder disaggregation (EPD) — run on Trainium and scale to production with frameworks like AIBrix and llm-d. Underneath the serving layer, see how EKS keeps it resilient at scale through topology-aware allocation, multi-node scheduling, and fault recovery. You'll leave able to take an LLM from a single instance to a resilient production fleet on Trainium.

sessions.title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning enables your model to follow instructions, but teaching it to reason requires reinforcement learning. RL workflows demand iterative loops that multiply compute costs — making AWS Trainium's purpose-built price performance critical. In this chalk talk, we explore what techniques like RLHF and GRPO bring to the table and how to run them on Trainium with the AWS Neuron software stack, Torchtitan, HuggingFace TRL, vLLM, and native PyTorch. We compare co-located vs. disaggregated RL architectures. You'll leave ready to implement cost-effective RL loops that train agents to reason.

sessions.title: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
sessions.abstract: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

sessions.title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
sessions.abstract: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

sessions.title: Get started on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: New to Bedrock, or considering it for your next workload? In this hands-on workshop you go from your first API call to a working application in a single sitting. You choose a model, ground it with Managed Knowledge Bases, apply Guardrails, pick a service tier, then deploy and monitor what you built. Along the way you learn the core building blocks and how they fit together. You leave with an application you built yourself and a repeatable path your team can follow to build the next one.

sessions.title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

sessions.title: AI that delivers ROI: Aligning workloads to tech and business needs
sessions.abstract: Every AI dollar should align to an expected business outcome. As AI use cases scale across the enterprise, this session covers the design decisions and the metrics that tie them to technical and business requirements. Learn how workload type and adoption maturity shape which metrics matter most, and how to track value from direct outputs like cost reduction to indirect outputs like faster time to decision. Explore best practices for aligning chips, training, inference, customization, and agents to business value, and how baselines, cost-per-outcome metrics, and waste guardrails keep unit costs and business impact moving together.

sessions.title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
sessions.abstract: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

sessions.title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

sessions.title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
sessions.abstract: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

sessions.title: Serving World Model at scale with AWS Trainium and Native PyTorch
sessions.abstract: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads at scale. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave equipped to take world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

sessions.title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
sessions.abstract: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

sessions.title: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: AI agents doing real work, like financial advising, coding, customer operations, reason across turns, call tools, and recover when steps fail mid-conversation. Prompting won't get you there; building multi-turn RL from scratch takes weeks. We'll whiteboard how SageMaker AI's managed MTRL connects your Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent under 10 lines of code - handling rollouts, trajectories, and checkpointing, auto-cataloged in SageMaker catalog. We'll cover reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute keeping GPUs from idling, and smaller specialized models outperforming larger ones at lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case for mapping the path.

sessions.title: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. Experience how purpose-built chips changes the inference economics equation as you deploy Frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and learn how the Neuron software stack integrates with familiar open-source frameworks - no rewrites required - to achieve superior tokenomics. Leave with actionable skills to run performant, cost-effective model inference at production scale on AWS Trainium.

sessions.title: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
sessions.abstract: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. You leave knowing how to extend the security patterns your organization already trusts to cover AI workloads on Bedrock.

sessions.title: Optimizing model performance with agentic loops on AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: Extracting peak performance from AI accelerators requires optimization at multiple levels — from framework configuration to individual kernels — and the complexity grows with every new workload. Agentic loops replace this manual work with autonomous profiling, diagnosis, and code generation, iterating toward performance targets without human intervention. In this session, we demonstrate this workflow on AWS Trainium, purpose-built to deliver better price-performance for AI workloads. Explore how these loops identify bottlenecks, how persistent memory prevents repeated failures, and how long-running campaigns uncover optimizations for different inference shapes. Walk away with practical patterns for agentic optimization on purpose-built silicon.

sessions.title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
sessions.abstract: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in a classifier that routes requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, semantic caching to cut redundant calls, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.

sessions.title: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
sessions.abstract: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

sessions.title: Agentic fairness: Practical methods to detect bias in AI-driven decisions
sessions.abstract: AI agents increasingly make real-world decisions: approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts. Yet most fairness testing still checks whether chatbots use offensive language, a gap that creates business and regulatory risk. This session shows how to assess whether your agentic AI systems treat people equitably across chosen demographic attributes. Through hands-on examples in financial services, customer support, and commerce, you'll move from language-level toxicity checks to decision-level fairness audits. Learn to identify disparate treatment, choose the right fairness metrics, and build testing frameworks that catch bias in the outcomes that affect people's lives.

sessions.title: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
sessions.abstract: Advisors across mission-driven organizations — financial counselors at credit unions, benefits navigators at nonprofits, program coordinators matching people to services — juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and time-consuming plan generation while those they serve go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See an open-source advisor plugin demonstrated end to end: domain-specific skills, MCP data connectors, and a personalized action plan generated in real time. Then deploy the agent to a production runtime with guardrails and observability. Leave with sample code, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building advisor agents that scale personalized guidance.

sessions.title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

sessions.title: Build provable AI agents with Automated Reasoning checks
sessions.abstract: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

sessions.title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
sessions.abstract: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

sessions.title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
sessions.abstract: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.

sessions.title: Do more with open weight models on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Agentic and coding workloads are multiplying token consumption, and paying frontier prices on every call adds up fast. This chalk talk shows how open weight models on Amazon Bedrock let you scale that growth affordably without giving up quality or security. We walk through multi-model strategies for agentic and code generation workloads, the unit economics of open weight versus frontier, and how Bedrock's zero operator access design keeps security strong regardless of where a model came from. You leave with a practical path to cost-efficient inference at scale.

sessions.title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
sessions.abstract: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training from data preparation through distributed configuration to model test practices with interactive chat — showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. Walk away ready to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.

sessions.title: Build conversational AI agents (support, assistants, copilot) with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Conversational agents live or die on the details: staying responsive in real time, remembering what the user said three turns ago, and taking action instead of just answering. In this session, learn how to build production conversational AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, whether it's a customer support agent, an in-product copilot, or a virtual assistant for banking or travel. We cover low-latency streaming on Runtime, multi-turn and cross-session context with Memory, taking action through Gateway-connected tools, keeping responses safe and on-policy, and handing off to a human when needed. A live demo builds a support agent end to end.

sessions.title: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
sessions.abstract: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.

sessions.title: Build a governed enterprise AI/ML platform on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Enterprises struggle with fragmented ML tooling, inconsistent governance, and limited model health visibility. This session demonstrates a unified platform on Amazon SageMaker AI addressing these challenges across regulated industries. We cover multi-account architecture with environment-isolated domains, SageMaker AI Studio and MLflow/Model Registry as the central governance checkpoint with approval workflows, and CI/CD-driven model promotion with validation gates. We extend this to LLM fine-tuning — adapter versioning, evaluation benchmarks, and human-in-the-loop sign-off within the same registry-driven pipeline. Finally, we close the loop with model monitoring for drift, inference logging, and automated alerting. Leave with a reference architecture and decision frameworks.

sessions.title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.

sessions.title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
sessions.abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass every health check yet corrupt your results. In this hands-on builders session, you diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults before your jobs do. You leave with a failure-signature runbook and a triage method distilled from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

sessions.title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
sessions.abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall every active generation — and letting each phase scale on its own terms. It isn't free: KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still win. The difference is your traffic. In this hands-on builders session, you run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn the decision framework — input length, prefix reuse, latency SLO — and leave with runnable configurations.

sessions.title: Deploy Agentic AI on AWS AI Infrastructure for Production Agents
sessions.abstract: Autonomous agents demand multi-step reasoning, tool calling, and long-running sessions. In this chalk talk, we'll show how you can deploy self-managed agentic AI infrastructure on Amazon EC2 to solve its core scaling problem: agent turns are bursty — GPU-bound while reasoning, CPU-bound while orchestrating. We'll discuss when to use disaggregated inference to optimize for prefill and decode, KV cache management for multi-turn sessions, autoscaling for bursty traffic, and CPU-based compute for orchestration. We'll close with guardrails, cost controls, and reference architectures for multi-model agentic RAG and policy-based routing to managed endpoints.

sessions.title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
sessions.abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, and survive the failures that compound with scale. In this workshop, you walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances — compute, network, and storage; the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks — and stand up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer: measure, attribute, fix with the tool that sees inside. Leave with dashboards you built yourself and a goodput methodology for your training clusters.

sessions.title: Governed ModelOps: From customization to deployment with SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

sessions.title: Build production AI assistant with Hugging Face Libraries and models
sessions.abstract: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant—but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this Chalk Talk, we architect a production-ready solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. Walk away understanding how Native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium let you own your AI stack and scale.

sessions.title: Web grounding on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Learn about the ways in which customers can ground their AI applications in current web information with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

sessions.title: Build an automated evaluation pipeline for AI agents
sessions.abstract: Stand up a continuous evaluation pipeline for your generative AI applications. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build an end-to-end evals infrastructure using Amazon Bedrock and open-source tooling. We cover designing evaluation datasets, implementing automated scoring (LLM-as-judge and programmatic metrics), tracking model performance over time, and triggering alerts on quality regressions. Leave with a working pipeline you can adapt for your organization's models and prompts.

sessions.title: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
sessions.abstract: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 SonicLearn how to build and deploy a voice agent using Nova 2 Sonic, Strands BidiAgent, AgentCore, and customized Skills. The session covers both bidirectional streaming architecture (Nova Sonic) and cascading architectures using Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Polly. Attendees will learn reference architectures, implementation patterns, deployment steps, and best practices for building scalable, production-ready voice agents using AI coding tools.

sessions.title: Full-stack data agents using Box MCP and AWS
sessions.abstract: Run production AI agents for contract extraction on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that simultaneously connects to Box's content intelligence using Box MCP (via AWS Marketplace) and AWS database services. In this session, you build a custom MCP server exposing Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DocumentDB, and Amazon DynamoDB, then configure AgentCore Gateway for multi-MCP routing with namespace prefixing and parallel execution. The AI agent performs these 5-hop reasoning in one turn: extract PDF terms from Box, query amendment history in DocumentDB, check real-time risk in DynamoDB, correlate PO spend in Aurora, and generate an auditable compliance determination. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Designing  AI Agents with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Voice AI
sessions.abstract: Multimodal AI agents need to understand more than text and interact through more than a screen. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll explore how Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings connects knowledge across text, documents, images, video, and audio, including semantic search over spoken content and sound, while voice AI enables natural conversational interaction. We’ll examine cross-modal retrieval, audio and video segmentation, multimodal context, conversational orchestration, latency, and grounding tradeoffs for building responsive agents that can listen, understand, retrieve, and converse across modalities.

sessions.title: Accelerate intelligent document processing with Amazon Textract
sessions.abstract: Building custom extraction pipelines on foundation models is powerful but expensive to maintain. Textract Intelligence gives you the same GenAI flexibility as a managed service: custom-field extraction, document classification, splitting, and summarization, all backed by purpose-built OCR instead of a vision model guessing at pixels. In this session we compare approaches head-to-head on accuracy, latency, and cost, then show how 40-language support and trustworthy confidence scores close the gaps that push teams to DIY solutions.

sessions.title: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe
sessions.abstract: We'll use Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe to add natural speech and accurate transcription to your applications. With Polly, you'll build expressive, emotionally engaged voices using its generative and long-form engines, covering streaming audio, speech marks for word-level timing, and newscaster styles. With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.

sessions.title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
sessions.abstract: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Build agentic observability workflows with AI tools from AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Accelerate Domain-Specific AI with Amazon SageMaker AI and Forge
sessions.abstract: Forge accelerates AI solution development on AWS. In this session, learn about Forge's capabilities and how to use them to create custom evaluations for your use case, incorporate your data into your AI solution, and select the right model for your needs.

sessions.title: World Models & Physical AI: The Next Frontier in Intelligent Systems
sessions.abstract: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.

sessions.title: Model customization for industrial use cases on Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Off-the-shelf models fall short on what makes an industrial business distinctive: proprietary design languages, private process data, and physical tasks no public model has seen. See how two manufacturers closed that gap on Amazon SageMaker AI. GlobalFoundries customized a model to generate design rule check code in a proprietary semiconductor verification language, trained on Sagemaker Serverless and Hyperpod.

sessions.title: Which customization path? A decision framework for fine-tuning on AWS
sessions.abstract: Off the shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice, which technique, which service, which tradeoffs. In this chalk talk, we work through the decision framework live. When Supervised Fine Tuning is enough, when DPO or RLAIF earns its added cost, and when RLVR or multi-turn RL is the right call, and what data each demands. We will learn how to choose across SageMaker Serverless Customization, Training Jobs, HyperPod, and Bedrock Custom Model Import based on traffic, budget, and control needs. Bring a real use case and we'll place it on the map.

sessions.title: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
sessions.abstract: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.

sessions.title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
sessions.abstract: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated decision framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to combine both for unified security, governance, and models that move between services without rearchitecting. We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.

sessions.title: Innovating with agentic AI inside Amazon, powered by AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Amazon runs thousands of AI agents internally, built on the same AgentCore platform available to every AWS customer. Teams across the company have replaced manual workflows with agents that act autonomously, cutting process times from weeks to hours and eliminating thousands of lines of custom orchestration code. This session brings together the Amazon builders behind these transformations to share the AgentCore capabilities that made it possible, the failure modes they hit at scale, and the design patterns that separate agents that demo well from agents that survive production. Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.

sessions.title: How ISVs ship agent products to customers faster with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Every customer now expects AI agents in your software product. But shipping agents to thousands of customers means solving multi-tenancy, per-customer isolation, identity delegation, and cost attribution before you write a single line of agent logic. That is months of plumbing, not product. In this session, hear how Twilio and Typeform built agent products on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore - serving millions of end users without building custom infrastructure. Learn how they eliminated months of infrastructure work, stayed framework-neutral, and focused engineering on what their customers actually pay for — the agent experience, not the plumbing underneath.

sessions.title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.

sessions.title: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.

sessions.title: Deploy agents fast with Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI (1P)
sessions.abstract: Standing up an enterprise agent usually means weeks of plumbing: sandboxed compute, authentication, persistent memory, and observability. Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI, collapses that into three API calls. See how the OpenAI harness executes long-running tasks quickly and steers them reliably, with agent identity, auditability, and AgentCore compute built in. We connect agents to your existing AWS services and run a multi-step enterprise workflow end to end. You leave knowing how to ship a secure, memory-aware agent in days instead of months.

sessions.title: A developer's guide to model migrations on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: A new model drops every few weeks, and the pressure to upgrade is constant. But newer is not always better for your workload, and every migration carries cost and risk. This breakout gives you a decision framework for model upgrades on Amazon Bedrock: how to tell whether a new model actually helps your use case, what to benchmark beyond headline scores, how to estimate migration effort and cost, and when staying on your current model is the right call. Leave with a repeatable way to evaluate the next model, so you upgrade on evidence, not hype.

sessions.title: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
sessions.abstract: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS, has a remote path to your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. You leave ready to have the conversation that gets your AI workload approved.

sessions.title: From token-maxxing to value-maxxing with Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Agentic workloads changed the economics of AI overnight. A single task can burn millions of tokens, and the metrics that proved adoption no longer prove value. This session covers best practices for connecting AI spend on Amazon Bedrock to the outcomes it actually produces. Learn how to attribute spend to teams and workloads, tier models by the outcomes they drive, connect technical signals like latency, quality, groundedness, and token cost to business results, and build portfolio dashboards that surface dollars at risk with recommended remediation. Leave with a repeatable approach for deciding which workloads to scale, improve, or retire.

sessions.title: The agent fabric: shipping your software into the agentic economy
sessions.abstract: Your customers' AI agents won't stop at your product boundary. They expect your data, workflows, and agents to be reachable. If you're not, someone else will be. This workshop teaches the agent fabric pattern for making software products interoperable in the agentic economy: cross-organization agent discovery, cross-account identity, and the A2A protocol. Register specialist agents in AWS Agent Registry so a customer's coordinator can discover your capabilities, build that coordinator with the Strands Agents SDK, and wire cross-account trust and observability with AgentCore Identity and Observability. Leave with the pattern for shipping your product into the agentic economy.

sessions.title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.

sessions.title: Agents that train themselves: autonomous reinforcement learning on AWS
sessions.abstract: What if an agent could design reward functions, launch reinforcement learning, evaluate policies in simulated environments, and iterate autonomously until convergence? This session demonstrates a Strands agent orchestrating the full RL loop on SageMaker: generating rewards from a natural language objective, evaluating against quantitative success criteria, diagnosing failure modes, adjusting hyperparameters, and repeating without human intervention. We cover tool interfaces for each pipeline stage, how the agent decides when to iterate vs. stop, evaluation design for automated pass/fail, and how this pattern extends to any domain requiring iterative experimentation from robots to game playing and control systems.

sessions.title: Serverless Model Customization with SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Go from dataset to a customized foundation model in hours, without provisioning infrastructure. In this hands-on workshop, fine-tune LLMs using Amazon SageMaker AI's serverless model customization APIs — no infrastructure to provision, no GPUs to manage. Progress through four techniques: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for task-specific behaviors, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for alignment, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for reasoning,  RLAIF for scalable feedback, and Multi-Turn reinforcement learning for agentic fine tuning. Prepare datasets, launch training jobs, register assets in the SageMaker AI Registry, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy to a real-time endpoint. Walk away ready to customize models at scale on day one.

sessions.title: Build End-to-End AI Pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Modern AI pipelines demand unified frameworks for petabyte-scale data prep, large-model training, and low-latency serving. In this hands-on workshop, build a complete data processing → distributed training → model serving pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, fine-tuning and serving an LLM end-to-end. Experience HyperPod's native distributed computing integration with managed orchestration, embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Leave with a working serving endpoint, production patterns, and a resilient platform that eliminates the infrastructure toil of running distributed AI workloads at scale.

sessions.title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands-on workshop, use Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations — reducing search time from weeks to days, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results with NVIDIA AIPerf. Then, configure capacity-aware instance pools with priority-based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI-compatible APIs. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready deployment patterns you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Build agents on OSS models with blazing fast inference on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Stop paying frontier-model prices for agentic workloads. In this hands-on session, build production-ready AI agents powered by open-source models like Qwen3 and Gemma4 running entirely on Amazon SageMaker AI. You'll deploy models with optimized serving, connect them to multi-turn tool-use workflows through OpenAI-compatible APIs, and enable real-time bi-directional streaming for responsive agent interactions. Leave with a working cost-optimized agent stack you fully control — fast inference, zero vendor lock-in, and patterns for scaling agentic workloads on your own terms.

sessions.title: End-to-end foundation model pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS
sessions.abstract: Train, deploy, and serve a foundation model end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with on Kubernetes. In this hands-on workshop, prepare training data at scale leveraging high speed storage, launch distributed fine-tuning across multi-node GPU clusters with auto-healing and checkpointless recovery that maximizes goodput, and transition seamlessly to production inference on the same cluster— eliminating re-platforming. Throughout, monitor cluster health and inference latency. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready patterns you can deploy immediately.

sessions.title: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
sessions.abstract: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.

sessions.title: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
sessions.abstract: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week

sessions.title: Build a cost optimization playbook for your AI workload
sessions.abstract: Bring a representative prompt set from your own workload and optimize it live. In this builders session, you apply prompt caching, configure Intelligent Prompt Routing, and right-size model choice for the best price-performance, measuring token cost before and after each change. You see exactly which levers move the needle for your traffic and which do not. You leave with a cost optimization playbook tuned to what you actually run, along with the numbers to justify each decision to your team.

sessions.title: Right-size your AI spend on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Pilot budgets rarely survive scale. Token volumes surge, teams add models, and spend turns unpredictable fast. This session shows how to right-size AI spend on Bedrock: evaluate models for the right price-performance, apply Reserved capacity for steady workloads, use EDP drawdown, and attribute cost at the team level. You build a budget plan that maps each workload to the right pricing model and capacity strategy. You leave with a spend plan you can put in front of finance with confidence.

sessions.title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
sessions.abstract: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

sessions.title: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.

sessions.title: Build and Run Coding Agents at Scale with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

sessions.title: Scale AI productivity securely across your enterprise with Bedrock
sessions.abstract: AI productivity pilots are easy; scaling them across an enterprise is not. In this breakout, learn how to build a reference architecture and operating model for AI productivity on Amazon Bedrock, so your teams get consistent, secure access to models, company data, and tools instead of a patchwork of disconnected AI assistants. See how to put the essentials in place, including identity and access, data boundaries, Guardrails, evaluation, and cost controls, then share reusable capabilities across teams while preserving provider choice. Leave with a blueprint for moving from scattered experiments to secure, governed adoption.

sessions.title: Defense-in-depth AI safety with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sessions.abstract: Generative and agentic applications face a wide threat surface: prompt injection, harmful content, sensitive data leakage, and off-topic drift. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides safeguards for user prompts, foundation models, and agent actions. In this hands-on workshop, you apply a layered defense with checks that filter unwanted content, redact sensitive data, block prompt attacks, and catch hallucinations. You use the InvokeGuardrailChecks API to evaluate inputs and outputs against custom thresholds, then enforce safeguards across accounts for every model invocation. You leave with a blueprint for layered AI safety you can apply in your own environment.

sessions.title: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents
sessions.abstract: Building AI agents used to mean writing a good prompt. Now it spans context, harness, and loop engineering. But every layer comes back to the model: each prompt, tool call, and loop step is another hit on the inference engine. This chalk talk traces that evolution on Amazon Bedrock, using AgentCore and frameworks like Strands, and shows the inference impact of each layer with best practices to get them right, from versioning prompts and grounding context to engineering a reliable harness and designing loops that know when to stop. Leave knowing how each layer shapes cost, latency, and reliability.

sessions.title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

sessions.title: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Great models start with great data.
