In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Generate synthetic data to fill coverage gaps, then prepare datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, and RLAIF. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.

sessions.title: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
sessions.abstract: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.

sessions.title: Run agents at scale using AgentCore
sessions.abstract: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios to architect solutions together.

sessions.title: Route, cache or batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale. Some need your best model, some can reuse work you already paid for, and some can wait. This chalk talk whiteboards a clear decision framework for the models running on Bedrock: how Intelligent Prompt Routing sends each request to the right model, when prompt caching saves more on repeated context, and where batch inference fits for work that is not latency-sensitive. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a routing and caching strategy that matches how your workloads actually behave.

sessions.title: Bring your own model to Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: You fine-tuned a model on proprietary data or for a domain-specific task, and want to run it fully managed. With Custom Model Import, you import model weights in Hugging Face Safetensors format and run inference on Amazon Bedrock via InvokeModel. Supported architectures include Llama, Mistral, Mixtral, Qwen, Flan, and GPTBigCode. Once imported, your model runs on on-demand throughput with access to advanced API features including structured outputs, tool calling, and log probabilities. This chalk talk covers the import workflow end to end: permissions, architecture validation, serving, and post-import capabilities. Bring your model plans and your questions.

sessions.title: How to pick the right agent framework to build your agents
sessions.abstract: LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Strands, Claude Agent SDK - every framework makes different tradeoffs in control, orchestration, and complexity. In this session, we compare the major agent frameworks head to head: where each fits, where each struggles, and how to match one to your workload. We then show how any of them runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the same runtime, memory, identity, and observability, so your framework choice stays reversible. Includes a live demo running the same agent task across multiple frameworks on shared infrastructure.

sessions.title: Optimizing agents in production: evals, A/B tests, and traces
sessions.abstract: Your agent works in the demo, then does something baffling in production—and you have no idea why. In this hands-on workshop, you build a complete optimization loop for a live agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You capture traces to debug reasoning chains, token usage, and latency, then run built-in and code-defined evaluators against sampled production traffic to score quality. You set monitors that alert on regressions, run A/B experiments comparing prompts and models with traffic splitting, and configure automated rollback. You leave with a working evaluation harness and a data-driven way to ship improvements. Bring a laptop, we'll work together.

sessions.title: First principles at LLM scale: Architecting Forge
sessions.abstract: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we assumed the hardest problems would be ML problems. They weren't. They were classical problems Amazon's been solving for years, at a new scale. Same Well-Architected principles, evolved techniques. We will deep-dive into three workloads from the team behind Forge. First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. Leave with lessons for your own AI platform.

sessions.title: Evaluate, select, optimize and find your best model
sessions.abstract: Most teams pick a model on instinct. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build a structured evaluation pipeline for your own use case, run it against multiple model candidates (frontier and open-weight), and learn exactly when customization is worth the investment vs. when prompt engineering or RAG is enough. You'll leave with a working evaluation harness, a decision framework for technique selection (SFT vs. RFT vs. CPT), and a trained model you can take home.

sessions.title: Train and deploy large-scale models with governance at every step
sessions.abstract: Training a large-scale model is the easy part. Getting it into production with the right data flowing in, governance enforced, and multiple deployment paths ready is where most teams stall. This chalk talk works through how to build one training pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, bring in enterprise data that amplifies model value while respecting data protection policies, and deploy the same model into Amazon Bedrock for inference or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agent orchestration. Governance follows the model at every step. No bolted-on compliance. You leave with an architecture you can build against immediately.

sessions.title: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

sessions.title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Optimize the Agent Harness
sessions.abstract: An agent’s performance depends on far more than its model or system prompt. Tools, instructions, context management, memory, orchestration, and runtime policies form an agent harness that can determine whether the same model succeeds or fails. This session introduces harness optimization: a systematic, evaluation-driven approach to improving the complete agent system. Learn how to identify high-leverage changes, design controlled experiments, optimize for quality, latency, and cost, and avoid overfitting to benchmarks. Leave with a repeatable method for turning agent development into an engineering discipline.

sessions.title: Inside Bedrock's inference engine: architecture to capacity planning
sessions.abstract: When demand spikes, inference has to keep up. This session goes under the hood of Bedrock's high-performance inference engine, built for scale, security, and reliability. See how pooling, cross-region routing, and automatic spillover keep capacity available. Then learn how to match your workload to the right service tier: Reservations for guaranteed capacity with an availability SLA, Priority for production traffic that needs consistent performance, Standard for general workloads, and Flex for cost-sensitive batch jobs. Learn to read your own demand shape and design inference that stays fast and reliable under real load.

sessions.title: One agent, any robot: building physical AI with Strands Robots
sessions.abstract: Physical AI puts agents in the real world. This chalk talk builds a robotics agent with the Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands — a MuJoCo simulation by default, real hardware with one code parameter change. We'll whiteboard the loop around the embodied agent: perception, a vision-language-action policy (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), and low-level control. We'll cover the the edge-to-cloud intelligence split, the peer-to-peer mesh and AWS IoT bridge coordinating a fleet, and sim-to-real transfer.

sessions.title: Don’t trust the model: automated reasoning as agent guardrails
sessions.abstract: Your agent is only as safe as the constraints it can’t bypass. This chalk talk covers how to enforce hard invariants on LLM-driven agents using formal policy languages — Cedar for stateless authorization, Dogwood for temporal reasoning over action history, and human-in-the-loop for the decisions machines shouldn’t make alone. We’ll dig into the Strands Agents intervention system, the neurosymbolic architecture that lets probabilistic and deterministic reasoning coexist, and where the open problems are.

sessions.title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

sessions.title: Govern models and agents on any cloud with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sessions.abstract: Your models and agents run across Bedrock, Azure, GCP, and self-hosted infrastructure, and each one needs safety controls and an audit trail. Rebuilding those per cloud does not scale. This chalk talk shows how Bedrock Guardrails gives you one control plane for content filtering, PII redaction, prompt attack detection, and automated reasoning checks, wherever inference runs. Apply a pre-configured guardrail with ApplyGuardrail or run resource-less checks inline with InvokeGuardrailChecks, both decoupled from model invocation, with per-step scoring for agentic workflows. You leave with one set of safety checks and one audit trail across every environment.

sessions.title: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Agents are not just chat. They are multi-step, tool-calling, retrieval-augmented workloads that stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. You leave with working code for all three patterns that you can adapt to your own agents.

sessions.title: Right-size your AI spend on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: AI spend scales fast, and you can't right-size what you can't see. In this code talk, first build cost visibility on Bedrock live: CUR 2.0, Cost Explorer, EDP integration, attribution by IAM principal, and tag-based allocation, assembled into a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models in near real time. Then turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved capacity, pick models for the right price-performance, and set budgets that hold. Leave with working code and a repeatable way to right-size AI spend you can put in front of finance.

sessions.title: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.

sessions.title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation from Amazon's AI-Native Development
sessions.abstract: AI agents running on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at unprecedented velocity and scale. Discover how autonomous agents write, test, and deploy code around the clock through spec-driven development, while always-on agents process millions of transactions, unify fragmented data, and deliver measurable cost savings without human intervention. Leaders from multiple Amazon business units share the architectures, patterns, and governance models powering this shift, from AI-native development that eliminates idle time to agentic systems that compound value in production on AWS. Leave with a playbook for sustained transformation through autonomous AI.

sessions.title: The Art of the Impossible: How Amazon Shapes What's Possible with AWS
sessions.abstract: Across Amazon, teams are solving challenges once considered impossible: from deploying AI agents that autonomously resolve millions of customer interactions, to creating viewing experiences that transcend the limitations of the physical world, to delivering real-time insights in milliseconds. In this session, hear from a variety of Amazon businesses as they share how AWS services like Amazon Bedrock, Amazon AgentCore, and Amazon SageMaker transform ambitious ideas into production-ready solutions at unprecedented scale. Learn the architectural patterns and AI-native practices that enable Amazon builders to achieve what was previously unimaginable, and how you can too.

sessions.title: The Road to 10x velocity
sessions.abstract: This is a real-world case study documenting the journey toward 10x engineering velocity using Kiro. Prime Video Financial Systems started at 3x with AI-assisted sprints, then evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery — where agents pick up tasks, implement, raise CRs, address feedback, and merge 24/7 without human intervention. Each step compounds: parallel execution, zero idle time, and engineers freed to focus on design and review. It's an honest, in-progress story showing builders the concrete methodology — structured specs plus persistent Kiro sessions — and the architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.

sessions.title: Build a modern multi-warehouse architecture with Amazon Redshift
sessions.abstract: Managing a large-scale Amazon Redshift deployment across multiple business units requires a deliberate architecture. This session walks through a scalable multi-warehouse strategy, separating workloads by team, enabling cross-cluster data sharing, federated permissions, and right-sizing serverless and provisioned capacity so you scale with the business.

sessions.title: What's new in Amazon SageMaker Platform
sessions.abstract: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance,  and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to  production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL  analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers  enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team  needs.

sessions.title: Accelerate analytics and AI with an open lakehouse architecture on Apache Iceberg
sessions.abstract: Stop choosing between your data lake and data warehouse.  Join this session to explore how to build a  unified, open, and secure data lakehouse architecture, on Apache Iceberg. Learn how the lakehouse breaks down data  silos and opens your data estate offering flexibility to use your preferred  query engines and tools that accelerate time to insights. Learn about recent  launches that improve data interoperability and performance, and enable large  language models (LLMs) and AI agents to interact with your data. Discover  robust security features, including consistent fine-grained access controls, attribute-based access control, and tag-based access control that help  democratize data without compromises.

sessions.title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
sessions.abstract: Landing streaming data into Apache  Iceberg at scale is a complex undertaking. In this chalk talk, we dissect practical reference architectures for real-time ingestion into Iceberg tables, covering  Kafka to Flink, Kinesis to Firehose, and managed pipelines through Amazon S3  Tables. Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how  to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these  pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.

sessions.title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
sessions.abstract: Batch  jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a  stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment  an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive  rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail  independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and  analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive  agentic AI on AWS.

sessions.title: Accelerate lakehouse analytics with Apache Iceberg materialized views
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS store pre-computed query results as Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 or Amazon S3 Tables. These views are not only open, as in compute once and consume from any Iceberg-compatible engine – they accelerate your lakehouse analytics while reducing costs. Join this hands-on session to experience how Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS simplify medallion architectures, lakehouse migrations, accelerate BI query transactions and complex joins.

sessions.title: What's new in Amazon Redshift
sessions.abstract: Cut costs, query faster, and unify your warehouse and data lake without trade-offs. In this session, learn how new Graviton-powered RG instances deliver better price-performance, a built-in data lake engine lets you read and write Apache Iceberg tables in place, multi-warehouse architecture gives teams independent scale with shared data, and Redshift Serverless improvements let you get insights on your data without managing infrastructure. Whether you're consolidating on open table formats or building the analytics backbone for AI agents, walk away knowing exactly how to put these capabilities to work.

sessions.title: Build scalable streaming and messaging applications with Amazon Kinesis and AmazonMSK
sessions.abstract: Messaging  and streaming should be simple, elastic, and cost-efficient, no matter how  your workloads change. In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon  Kinesis Data Streams are making it easier and more affordable to build messaging  and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying  about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3  and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can  focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to  see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less, and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.

sessions.title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and  messaging
sessions.abstract: Organizations are  accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there  depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput  ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven  delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn  how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind  agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer  for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the  instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with  live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region  resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct  landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking

sessions.title: Retrieval at Agent Scale: What breaks and how to fix it
sessions.abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory across sessions, and demand verified answers before taking action. Traditional search architectures weren't built for this, and at agent scale, latency budgets compress, relevance requirements compound, and retrieval failures cascade into hallucinated outputs. In this session, we walk you through how the shift from human search to agent retrieval is reshaping infrastructure requirements and how the latest capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service help you address these unique challenges. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, why it matters, and how to get started.

sessions.title: What's new in AWS Data Processing
sessions.abstract: Explore the latest advancements in AWS Analytics designed to transform your data processing landscape. This session unveils powerful new capabilities across key services, including Amazon EMR for scalable big data processing, AWS Glue for seamless data integration, Amazon Athena for optimized querying, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) for complex workflow orchestration. Discover how these innovations can supercharge performance, optimize costs, and streamline your entire data ecosystem. Whether you're looking to enhance scalability, improve data integration, accelerate queries, or refine workflow management, join us to gain actionable insights that will position your organization at the forefront of data processing innovation.

sessions.title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.abstract: Your metadata is scattered across warehouses, lakes, ML pipelines, and BI tools. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all your data assets, enforces consistent governance, and makes every table, model, and feature discoverable across engines and teams. See how to register, enrich, and share metadata at scale, enable cross-account discovery, and give AI agents the context they need to query your data accurately.

sessions.title: Accelerating data analytics on Apache Iceberg with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Every analytics query starts with how your data is stored. In this session, learn how Amazon S3 Tables deliver purpose-built Iceberg table storage that accelerates query performance, reduces storage costs, and eliminates table maintenance overhead. See how to pair S3 Tables with Athena, Redshift, and EMR to get faster results at lower cost, automate compaction and snapshot management, and simplify your lakehouse without changing your query engine or workflow.

sessions.title: Mastering Amazon Athena: advanced optimization and cost-saving strategies
sessions.abstract: Dive deep into Amazon Athena's most powerful capabilities in this interactive chalk talk for experienced practitioners. We'll explore cost-saving techniques—CTAS for materializing expensive query results, partition projection to eliminate metadata lookups, and EXPLAIN-based tuning to minimize bytes scanned. Discuss workgroup budgets, provisioned capacity for predictable pricing, and query result reuse to avoid redundant scans. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

sessions.title: From prompt to pipeline: Agentic data engineering
sessions.abstract: Data engineers spend weeks building pipelines describable in a single sentence. AI agents change this by autonomously discovering data, building transformations, and orchestrating workflows via natural language. Explore how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gives agents standardized access to AWS analytics services. See a live demo of an agent composing across AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, and MWAA Serverless to build a pipeline from a single prompt. Leave with patterns and tools to start building.

sessions.title: Boost Apache Spark performance and reduce costs with AWS Analytics
sessions.abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore best practices for building high-performing, cost-efficient Spark applications using AWS analytics data processing services. We'll discuss the AWS performance-optimized runtime for Apache Spark—delivering up to 4.5x faster execution across Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue—meaning faster jobs and lower compute spend. Explore flexible deployment models—long-running clusters, on-demand elasticity with EMR Serverless, Kubernetes integration with EMR on EKS, and Graviton instances for up to 30% cost reduction. We'll also highlight how Glue's auto scaling, Flex execution class, and Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines while optimizing costs.

sessions.title: 10 tips to boost Apache Iceberg performance on Amazon Redshift
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg gives you flexibility and these 10 Amazon Redshift tips give you speed. In this  chalk talk, you'll learn practical tuning strategies for Apache Iceberg on  Amazon Redshift, including partition pruning, compaction, file sizing, sort  order optimization, predicate pushdown, materialized views over Iceberg, RG  data lake engine benefits, and metadata management. Walk away with an  actionable checklist to improve your Iceberg query performance.

sessions.title: Protect your analytics workloads with cross-region resilience
sessions.abstract: Explore best  practices for designing active-active and active-passive architectures for AWS analytics services including AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift and AWS Lake Formation based on your  RTO and RPO requirements. Learn how to build cross-region resilience when  Apache Iceberg tables become an integral part of your architecture, including catalog  replication and metadata synchronization. Explore real-world architectural patterns and  trade-offs for choosing the right resilience strategy.

sessions.title: Right-size your observability: maximize signal, minimize spend
sessions.abstract: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. In this chalk talk, we'll tackle your problems head-on with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Bring your toughest scenarios. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. If you're building AI agents, ask how to trace LLM calls, track per-invocation cost, and debug multi-agent workflows. And for any workload, ask how to stack cost levers like right-sizing, tiered storage, and writable warm to maximize savings.

sessions.title: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

sessions.title: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

sessions.title: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic pipeline for Amazon Redshift
sessions.abstract: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language—but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions about preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic pipeline for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution, including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns, and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

sessions.title: Build event-driven applications with AWS Streaming and Messaging
sessions.abstract: Dive deep into AWS messaging services in this hands-on workshop where you'll build a real-world, event-driven application. Learn to architect sophisticated event-driven systems using Amazon SQS, SNS, MSK, and Amazon MQ. Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

sessions.title: Build conversational AI agents for query federation with Amazon Athena
sessions.abstract: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for faster conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and multi-cloud data stores – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

sessions.title: Getting Started with Apache Iceberg: The AI-Ready open lakehouse advantage
sessions.abstract: In the agentic AI era, the same modern lakehouse is also your AI-ready foundation: the quality, openness, and organization of your data is what separates successful AI outcomes. Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 Tables gives you that true portability and engine interoperability to build your AI-ready data foundation. Welcome to this hands-on workshop, where you will build an open lakehouse on AWS to serve analysts and agents both, while tackling real-world data challenges including a medallion architecture, table maintenance, change data capture and GDPR compliance.

sessions.title: Give your AI agents business context with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.abstract: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. In this builders' session, learn how to turn the AWS Glue Data Catalog into a trust layer for AI agents. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build orchestration agents for AWS Glue ETL
sessions.abstract: What happens when you give an AI agent the keys to your ETL infrastructure? In this builder session, you'll build an agentic workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that accepts natural language instructions and autonomously orchestrates ETL jobs on AWS Glue. Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

sessions.title: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
sessions.abstract: Ready to tear down data silos? Join this hands-on workshop to transform your data landscape using the Amazon SageMaker lakehouse architecture. We will dive into unifying data lakes, data warehouses, and federated sources using seamless zero-ETL integrations. You'll get practical experience building a secure, governed single source of truth, implementing real-time analytics, and optimizing query performance. If you are a data engineer, ML practitioner, or solutions architect, this session will give you the blueprint needed to build a scalable, modern data infrastructure.

sessions.title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
sessions.abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Redshift Graviton instances deliver up to 35% better price-performance, accelerating workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

sessions.title: Govern your AI agents with data quality, lineage, and business  context
sessions.abstract: AI agents generate SQL, surface insights, and take action on your data. Without governance guardrails, they hallucinate column meanings, query stale tables, and return wrong answers with high confidence. In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. Walk away with practical patterns for governing AI-assisted analytics the same way you govern human analysts.

sessions.title: Observe, investigate, act: smarter ops with Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: AI agents are becoming your best investigators, triaging alerts, correlating telemetry, and performing root-cause analysis across metrics, logs, and traces in seconds. Agents are a critical workload to observe: you need LLM trace monitoring, per-call cost attribution, and multi-agent workflow debugging to keep token spend and accuracy under control. Whether you're scaling an existing observability platform or modernizing your stack, Amazon OpenSearch Service addresses both sides. In this session, we present capabilities including native OpenTelemetry ingestion, MCP-based agent skills for natural-language issue investigation, and an optimized log-analytics engine delivering 4× price-performance at petabyte scale. Learn how to put AI agents to work on your observability data and how to keep them accountable in production.

sessions.title: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
sessions.abstract: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and  Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the  notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk,  we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS  replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to  minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60  minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.

sessions.title: Simplify multi-tenant data platform architectures
sessions.abstract: Organizations building multi-tenant data platforms stitch together  custom IAM, Lake Formation, and ETL—spending hours on boarding each tenant  while lacking lineage and governed sharing. In this chalk talk, explore how Amazon SageMaker collapses that complexity into managed primitives. Dive into tenant  isolation with domain units, medallion pipelines, and cross-tenant  publish/subscribe. Build a working platform, automate on boarding, and leave  with a repeatable architecture.

sessions.title: Self-healing data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
sessions.abstract: Join this session to experience the magic of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive into an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes, are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines.

sessions.title: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
sessions.abstract: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop session, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

sessions.title: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.

sessions.title: Build agentic AI applications with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS
sessions.abstract: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

sessions.title: Master Apache Iceberg migration on AWS
sessions.abstract: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

sessions.title: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
sessions.abstract: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across multiple clouds, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

sessions.title: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights
sessions.abstract: Learn how to build a modern, streaming analytics solution for real-time data processing and power it with agentic AI capabilities to analyze events and extract patterns for actionable responses. This session will provide a hands-in experience on building a streaming solution using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for complex event processing, and Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock Agent Core to take immediate action. Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

sessions.title: Modernize legacy applications into serverless event-driven systems
sessions.abstract: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your modernization. We show how to reverse-engineer architecture and dependencies from existing code, then generate a serverless, event-driven target. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices in weeks, and make their applications agent-ready in the process.

sessions.title: Serverlesspresso: Build an event-driven app from the ground up
sessions.abstract: Build a fully event-driven, serverless coffee-ordering web application using AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and Lambda durable functions. Design scalable, fault-tolerant architectures as you simulate customers placing orders and baristas managing them in real time. Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building real-time applications with event-driven architectures
sessions.abstract: Build real-time features using AWS AppSync Events in this hands-on builders' session. Working in small groups with guidance from AWS experts, you'll implement in-app notifications and live updates, configure WebSocket connections, and design data persistence strategies. Using provided code samples, you'll gain practical experience creating responsive, event-driven applications that push updates to connected clients instantly. By the end of this 60-minute session, you'll have working real-time patterns you can apply directly to your own applications. Bring your laptop and come ready to code!

sessions.title: API Gateway unleashed
sessions.abstract: Gain essential hands-on skills to create, deploy, and manage APIs efficiently with Amazon API Gateway. Learn message transformation, request validation, and security best practices. Master deploying APIs using Infrastructure as Code and integrating with AWS serverless services. Dive into monitoring and debugging to ensure your APIs perform optimally, and explore building and testing WebSocket backends. Whether you're creating REST APIs or real-time communication layers, this workshop equips you with the knowledge to streamline application development and enhance API management. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building enterprise-scale event buses with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.abstract: Discover how Amazon EventBridge simplifies enterprise-scale event routing across accounts and teams. In this hands-on builders' session, configure an event bus with routing policies, schema discovery, and access controls that let platform teams govern event flows while application teams ship independently. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-account event routing patterns and test event delivery at scale. Bring your laptop and come ready to build!

sessions.title: Build secure APIs faster with Amazon API Gateway and Kiro CLI
sessions.abstract: Secure your APIs with confidence and build them faster. In this builders' session, dive into Amazon API Gateway authorization strategies including Amazon Cognito user pools, Amazon Verified Permissions, Lambda custom authorizers, IAM authorizers, and machine-to-machine scenarios. Through hands-on exercises, implement each strategy and understand their trade-offs. Once secured, ship faster—use Kiro CLI, OpenAPI, and MCP servers to go from spec to deployed API in minutes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.abstract: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, explore how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure. We discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events.

sessions.title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
sessions.abstract: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
sessions.abstract: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: How event driven architectures go wrong and how to fix them
sessions.abstract: Event-driven architectures promise decoupling and scalability, but production systems reveal hard-won lessons. In this chalk talk, we dissect the most expensive anti-patterns teams encounter such as unbounded fan-out, missing dead-letter queues, chatty event schemas that drive up costs, and orchestration gaps that silently drop work. We whiteboard fixes using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Step Functions, and proven enterprise integration patterns, then walk through designs that keep event-driven systems reliable, cost-effective, and observable at scale.

sessions.title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.abstract: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.

sessions.title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.abstract: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

sessions.title: Coding event-driven retry patterns that prevent outages
sessions.abstract: In this code talk, you'll instrument an event-driven integration layer with the patterns that contain failure: exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, poison-pill isolation, and replay-from-archive - all live, in code. See how jittered retries prevent thundering herds, how circuit breakers protect healthy services from impaired ones, and how idempotency makes every replay safe. By the end, you'll have hands-on patterns for EventBridge and Step Functions that shrink your blast radius from total outage to graceful degradation.

sessions.title: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
sessions.abstract: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.

sessions.title: Orchestrating AI agents with AWS serverless services
sessions.abstract: Production AI agents need orchestration that handles non-deterministic behavior, multi-hour workflows, human approvals, and multi-agent coordination. Learn how AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda durable functions provide the reliability layer that agents demand. We cover patterns for durable execution, human-in-the-loop controls, event-driven agent communication, and the scale-to-zero economics that make serverless the natural home for agentic workloads.

sessions.title: Beyond Batch: Modernize with Event-Driven Architecture & Serverless
sessions.abstract: In this builders' session, transform a batch-oriented data processing pipeline into a real-time, event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AWS Step Functions. Working hands-on in small groups, you'll decompose a monolithic batch process into discrete event-driven steps, implement file-processing triggers, and design fan-out patterns for parallel execution. Learn when to keep batch and when to go event-driven, and leave with a working modernization pattern. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

sessions.title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
sessions.abstract: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.

sessions.title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
sessions.abstract: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

sessions.title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost
sessions.abstract: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow.  Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs.

sessions.title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
sessions.abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Replay, request-response, ordering, and high throughput increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Through a real CQRS architecture, we build a practical decision framework for when to choose messaging, streaming, or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.

sessions.title: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
sessions.abstract: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.

sessions.title: One agent to thousands: Architecting an enterprise agentic platform
sessions.abstract: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same anti-pattern that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms: duplicated infrastructure, inconsistent security, ungovernable sprawl. The core insight: agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance. This tension drives every platform decision — dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, and defense layers that compose without coupling. Attendees leave with a decision framework for architecting enterprise agent platforms at scale.

sessions.title: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
sessions.abstract: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. Over-decomposed architectures create distributed monoliths, event spaghetti, and operational nightmares that cost more and move slower than the monolith they replaced. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.

sessions.title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
sessions.abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

sessions.title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
sessions.abstract:
Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
sessions.abstract:
Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
sessions.abstract:
Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to.
Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
sessions.abstract:
Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
sessions.abstract:
When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
sessions.abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
sessions.abstract:
AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
sessions.abstract:
Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
sessions.abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
sessions.abstract: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.

sessions.title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
sessions.abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

sessions.title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
sessions.abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

sessions.title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
sessions.abstract: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.

sessions.title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
sessions.abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
sessions.abstract: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

sessions.title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
sessions.abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

sessions.title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
sessions.abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

sessions.title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
sessions.abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

sessions.title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
sessions.abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

sessions.title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
sessions.abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

sessions.title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
sessions.abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

sessions.title: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
sessions.abstract: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.

sessions.title: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
sessions.abstract: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.

sessions.title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
sessions.abstract: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

sessions.title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
sessions.abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate.
