Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

sessions.title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
sessions.abstract:
Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
sessions.abstract: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
sessions.abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.

sessions.title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
sessions.abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
sessions.abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.

sessions.title: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
sessions.abstract: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.

sessions.title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
sessions.abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

sessions.title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
sessions.abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

sessions.title: The AI-Native Advantage: Deploying Agentic CX in Weeks, Not Months
sessions.abstract: Enterprises have long accepted months of integration work and vendor complexity as the cost of delivering connected customer experiences. This session challenges that assumption. Hear how one enterprise replaced fragile, multi-vendor architectures with an AI-native solution and deployed agentic customer experiences in weeks - not months - with no compromises on speed, scale, or results. If your CX roadmap is still dictated by what your stack can stitch together, this is what becomes possible when you build on a foundation designed for the future.

sessions.title: From Cost Center to Revenue Driver: AI-Powered, Proactive CX
sessions.abstract: You've cut handle time. You've increased deflection. You've optimized every metric designed to make customer interactions cheaper. And your customers still leave. The metrics you optimized for were built for a world where every interaction was a cost. This session flips the script - stop measuring what you avoided, start measuring what you created, and turn service into a growth lever and not a cost center.

sessions.title: How A Customer Met Surge Hiring in Hours, Not Weeks
sessions.abstract: You expanded fast, but your hiring didn't keep up. What started as seasonal growth has become a scramble of manual screening, scheduling delays, and fragile workarounds that can't keep pace with your brand — forcing the impossible choice between speed and quality. Hear how Universal Studios replaced weeks-long hiring with Amazon Connect Talent, putting AI teammates to work running science-backed candidate assessments and AI-led interviews that take candidates from application to same-day offer — evaluated on the substance of their answers. Built on AWS with Amazon's proven hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent ensures recruiters stay in control of every decision.

sessions.title: Agentic Integration: How AI Agents Replace Static CRM Connectors
sessions.abstract: Every enterprise has dozens of integrations connecting their CRM, ticketing, and backend systems to their customer experience platform, and every one of them is static, brittle, and expensive to maintain. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon Connect Customer, powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP), shifts integration from point-to-point connectors to intelligent, agentic orchestration. The AI agent reasons across multiple systems in real time, assembling unified customer context that no single system holds alone. We whiteboard the architecture: how MCP connections work, how each new system compounds the intelligence available to every interaction, and how to evaluate which integrations to migrate first. Bring your integration pain (Salesforce, ServiceNow, homegrown systems) and we'll design the agentic alternative on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice.

sessions.title: No-Code Workspaces and AI-Generated Workflows for Customer Engagement Teams
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, you build the complete agent and business user experience in Amazon Connect Customer. First, you create persona-specific workspaces using the no-code UI builder, customizing page layouts, applications, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors each see only the information, tools, and guidance they need. Then, you create AI-powered guided workflows using natural language: describe the experience you want, and AI generates the step-by-step workflow automatically. You test and validate end-to-end in the Agent Workspace, seeing how custom layouts and AI-built guides work together to accelerate resolution. Walk away with persona-tailored workspaces and working guided workflows built in minutes instead of days.

sessions.title: Beyond English: Architecture Patterns for Multilingual AI Voice Agents
sessions.abstract: Deploying AI voice agents beyond English introduces unique challenges: accent handling, language detection, code-switching between languages mid-conversation, and cultural nuances in conversation flow. In this chalk talk, we share architecture patterns for building multilingual voice agents using Amazon Connect Agentic Voice. We cover real-world scenarios from deployments like Spanish and English coexistence, German with regional dialects, and Italian conversational AI. We discuss when speech-to-speech models work natively, when to fall back to TTS pipelines, how to handle polyglot but non-native accent scenarios, and practical approaches to knowledge base localization. Bring your language challenge and we'll design your multilingual architecture on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Describe It, Deploy It: Building AI Agents in Natural Language
sessions.abstract: What if you could describe the customer experience you want in plain English and have an AI agent built for you - complete with tools, guardrails, and conversation flows? In this chalk talk, we explore Amazon Connect's natural language AI agent builder: how business users and developers design, iterate, and deploy agentic self-service by describing intent rather than configuring flows block-by-block. We demo the capability live, then whiteboard the architecture: how to translate natural language into deterministic flows, agentic reasoning chains, and tool configurations. We discuss design patterns that work (and ones that don't). Bring your questions about blending deterministic and agentic AI, setting guardrails that don't strangle creativity, testing agents before they reach real customers, and how this fits alongside Connect's visual flow designer.

sessions.title: AI Agent Teams at Scale
sessions.abstract: When one event impacts hundreds, or even thousands, of customers simultaneously (a cancelled flight, a power outage, a system failure), contact centers cannot scale human agents fast enough. In this hands-on workshop, you orchestrate parallel AI agent teams using Amazon Connect Customer. You configure AI agents that fan out across dozens of affected customers at once: rebooking flights, issuing credits, and scheduling callbacks, all while a single human orchestrator monitors progress, approves exceptions, and intervenes only where needed. Walk away with a working parallel orchestration pattern and the configuration to deploy 1-to-many AI response at scale. This is not 1-to-1 AI coaching. This is 1-to-many crisis orchestration.

sessions.title: Easy Self-Service AI: Design Agents with the Agentic CX Designer
sessions.abstract: Creating AI-powered self-service shouldn't require prompt engineering expertise. In this workshop, build production-ready conversational AI agents using Amazon Connect's agentic CX designer. Experience rapid agent creation with the visual canvas - blending generative and deterministic nodes, accessing external data, passing context throughout the experience, and deploying multi-channel agents from concept to production in hours.

sessions.title: From Reactive to Proactive: Omnichannel AI Outreach with Connect Customer
sessions.abstract: Every organization is building AI agents for inbound, but who's automating outreach? In this workshop, you become a carrier responding to a device safety recall. Instead of posting a notice and waiting for calls, you build a system that identifies affected customers, prioritizes them by risk and value, and deploys an AI agent to reach them by voice before they ever pick up the phone. Walk away with a working proactive outreach engine and the architecture to deploy anticipatory engagement at scale.

sessions.title: Build Production-Ready AI Workflows for Refunds, Disputes, and Fraud
sessions.abstract: Build and deploy a production-ready workflow for back-office processes like refunds, disputes, and fraud investigations. You incorporate prebuilt AI agents in Connect Customer alongside domain-specific custom AI agents into structured workflows, built from natural language descriptions, that process Cases end-to-end. The result: experts freed from repetitive SOP execution to focus on high-judgment actions, exceptions, and approvals. Walk away with a working back-office automation workflow ready to handle real case volume.

sessions.title: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Every organization is building AI agents, but few can answer: "How do you know it works?" and "What happens when it doesn't?" This workshop delivers the complete production lifecycle for agentic AI on Amazon Connect Customer. First, build a testing framework using native Testing & Simulation: functional and integration tests for flows and bots, regression suites and smoke tests for continuous validation — all tied to dashboard-driven observability. Then, automate post-deployment: self-healing loops where breached thresholds trigger pre-approved remediations, canary validation promotes or rolls back changes, and patches auto-remove when metrics recover. Walk away with a reusable testing playbook and a working autonomous improvement loop — delivering up to 90% reduction in manual testing and self-correcting AI agents in production.

sessions.title: Decision Frameworks, Evaluation, and Cost Management with Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path — Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents — and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We'll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog — you'll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and ROI story.

sessions.title: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
sessions.abstract: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework. We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

sessions.title: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
sessions.abstract: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We walk through three memory patterns: episodic (past interactions), semantic (customer knowledge graphs), and procedural (learned resolution paths). We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. Bring your memory challenge and we'll design the persistence layer on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.

sessions.title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
sessions.abstract: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.

sessions.title: EC2 instances from launch to fleet orchestration
sessions.abstract: Amazon EC2 now offers over 1,000 instance types, five purchasing models, and a growing set of fleet and capacity tools. How do you bring it all together? This session is your comprehensive guide to AWS compute today. We cover the full EC2 portfolio from Graviton5 to accelerated instances, walk through On-Demand, Spot, Savings Plans, and Capacity Reservations, and show how EC2 Fleet, Auto Scaling, and Capacity Manager help you run the right instances at the right price. Whether you're new to EC2 or a seasoned practitioner, leave with a clear map of modern compute on AWS.

sessions.title: Unlock your Graviton savings potential using AI and analytics tools
sessions.abstract: How much can you save by migrating to Graviton? In this builder session, explore a real-world scenario and uncover two ways to answer that question. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent can run to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. Deploy both hands-on, identify migration candidates, and see how quickly cost data becomes a migration strategy. Walk away with actionable insights and a deployment kit.

sessions.title: Automate and secure EC2 Image Builder with AI agents
sessions.abstract: EC2 Image Builder pipelines sprawl fast, and frontier agents that run for hours unattended need guardrails. In this builder session, decompose Image Builder operations into reusable agent skills run via Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex. Author AWSTOE components and orchestrate workflows, then harden images and scan for CVEs. Mid-build, a WaitForAction step pauses the pipeline and hands the image to AWS Security Agent to pentest; what it finds decides whether the build ships, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval. Leave with a reusable skill library and governance pattern.

sessions.title: AWS Nitro System deep dive: Security, isolation, and innovation
sessions.abstract: The AWS Nitro System underpins every modern Amazon EC2 instance — purpose-built hardware and firmware delivering security, performance, and continuous innovation. In this deep dive, explore the Nitro architecture from custom silicon and modular design to networking and storage offload. Learn how the sixth-generation Nitro System introduces the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine, bringing formal verification to cloud isolation and extends Nitro-level isolation to containers. Discover how Nitro enables enhanced networking and confidential computing.

sessions.title: Run your largest SAP HANA on AWS: EC2 High Memory deep dive
sessions.abstract: Running SAP HANA at scale requires infrastructure that matches the size and criticality of your Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) workloads. EC2 High Memory instances deliver capacity from 256 GB to 32 TB, backed by the AWS Nitro architecture for consistent performance and hardware-level isolation. In this session, we deep dive into the Nitro design powering these instances and hear how customers are scaling production ERP to 32 TB on AWS. Walk away with architectural guidance and real-world deployment patterns for running your largest HANA workloads in a scale-up configuration.

sessions.title: Delivering next-generation devices on Amazon Braket
sessions.abstract: In this session, we discuss bringing next-generation quantum hardware to Amazon Braket and dive deep on how our combined hardware and software capabilities unlock the best performance of these fault-tolerant devices. We share early results and outline how organizations can begin preparing today for the fault-tolerant era.

sessions.title: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
sessions.abstract: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

sessions.title: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
sessions.abstract: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) is helping teams modernize their HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. In this session, hear how organizations have moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions that apply whether you're running simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.

sessions.title: 50k daily iOS builds with virtualization on Amazon EC2 Mac
sessions.abstract: A leading automotive manufacturer migrated its CI/CD infrastructure from on-premises to AWS to support over 130,000 daily builds (50k + iOS) across 1,300+ microservices. To accelerate iOS mobile app development, the team adopted Amazon EC2 Mac instances with virtualization using OpenAI Tart virtualization toolset, enabling ephemeral macOS VMs that boot in seconds with pre-configured toolchains. This approach reduced average build times from 90 to 35 minutes, a 61% improvement, while eliminating hardware management overhead. The platform now scales to 50,000+ daily iOS builds, serving 3,000+ developers with cost-optimized, reliable, and secure pipelines across hundreds of AWS accounts worldwide.

sessions.title: Beyond the simulator: Quantum chemistry workflows on real hardware
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on experience running quantum computing experiments using the Kvantify SDK; the same workflow used by researchers. In this workshop, participants will set up and execute computational workflows, testing them locally, on a classical simulator via Amazon Braket, and finally on a real quantum processing unit (QPU). Through practical exercises in enzyme engineering and battery development, learners will see how quantum computing accelerates discovery in life sciences and materials science, bridging the gap from simulation to real quantum hardware.

sessions.title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
sessions.abstract: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

sessions.title: Assess your workloads with SELinux compatibility on Amazon Linux 2027
sessions.abstract: AL2027 preview enforces SELinux by default. In this session, deploy an application that hits SELinux denials, learn to read audit logs, diagnose the root cause, and write a custom policy that resolves it. You will leave with the practical skills to adopt AL2027's security defaults.

sessions.title: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
sessions.abstract: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics—latency, IOPS, and throughput—to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We also demonstrate the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

sessions.title: Optimize smarter: EKS performance with APerf and AI-powered analysis
sessions.abstract: Your EKS workload is running, but is it actually efficient? Profile a live application with APerf to see what's consuming CPU cycles: syscall overhead, worker imbalances, inefficient library calls. Issues invisible in dashboards but obvious in a flame graph. APerf Analyzer MCP generates prescriptive guidance, configuration adjustments, and instance recommendations grounded in actual workload behavior. Implement fixes, redeploy, validate. Tasks escalate: fix a worker imbalance, eliminate a blocking call, resolve a writeback burst. Choose Python, Java, or Node.js. A live leaderboard tracks progress—who will finish first?

sessions.title: Optimize a .NET application for Graviton 5 using AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Take a Windows .NET application, run AWS Transform end-to-end (assess, modernize, deploy), and benchmark on Graviton. Compare against the original x86 baseline, inspect what Q got wrong, and tune the result. Covers .NET Framework to modern .NET migration, Lambda packaging on Graviton, and CI integration patterns from production migrations.

sessions.title: Storage performance in EC2 instances: What matters to your workload
sessions.abstract: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. In this chalk talk, we explore why latency-consistent mixed read/write performance drives real application outcomes across database, analytics, and distributed file system workloads. We'll walk through how workload profiles map to different performance dimensions (throughput vs. IOPS vs. latency consistency), how real-world write mixes reveal true storage performance, and how emerging AI workloads are creating demand for an entirely new storage performance profile.

sessions.title: Latest trends: Network/EBS intensive workloads on Amazon EC2 instances
sessions.abstract: EC2 network 'n' and EBS-optimized 'b' instances deliver the highest, most consistent network and EBS performance in the cloud. Join us for a tour of the latest Graviton and Intel instance types in these families, plus the networking and EBS technologies that unlock peak performance for your workloads. Learn how customers leverage these instances for new workloads associated with AI/ML training and inference, and traditional network-intensive workloads such as security & network virtual appliances, and EBS-intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and in-memory databases.

sessions.title: Build your iOS CI/CD pipeline with AI agents on EC2 Mac
sessions.abstract: Build iOS CI/CD pipelines on Amazon EC2 Mac using AI-powered workflows with Kiro CLI and AWS MCP Server. Define infrastructure as declarative specs while AI agents guide deployment, explain concepts, and validate configurations. This hands-on workshop covers EC2 Mac architecture, dedicated hosts, Xcode automation, GitLab setup, and CloudWatch monitoring through interactive AI modules. Learn to collaborate with agents and balance automation with understanding. Gain practical experience in both EC2 Mac operations and modern spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflows for Apple platforms.

sessions.title: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances
sessions.abstract: Container orchestration promises to improve resource utilization, but often we find ourselves with nodes that over-provision CPU, and therefore overspend. This might happen when our workloads have a high memory footprint, or when the number of replicas is driven by resilience targets and not actual load. In this session, we'll learn how easy it is to save cost in these situations without losing performance by taking advantage of EC2 Flex instances (e.g., C8i-flex, M8i-flex, R8i-flex). You'll migrate existing EKS cluster nodes, monitor relevant metrics, and measure the actual cost improvement.

sessions.title: Select and launch the right EC2 instance for your workload and budget
sessions.abstract: With hundreds of EC2 instance types spanning compute, memory, storage, and accelerator families, choosing the right one can be overwhelming. In this session, learn a practical framework for matching your workload characteristics—CPU, memory, network, and storage requirements—to the optimal instance type and size. We cover cost-performance tradeoffs across On-Demand, Spot, and Savings Plans, share real-world selection patterns for common workloads, and demo tools that simplify decision-making. Leave with a repeatable process to right-size from day one.

sessions.title: Build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that runs entirely on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: an ONNX embedding model for vector search, an ONNX re-ranker for retrieval quality, a fine-tuned 4B router for intent classification, and an 8B analyst for structured generation with RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock handles synthetic data generation for fine-tuning and serves as the LLM fallback for edge cases. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

sessions.title: EC2 Flex and T instances: Get modern performance at lower cost
sessions.abstract: Many workloads do not fully use all of the compute resources of a given instance, and we offer Flex and T instances to help cost-optimize for such workloads while getting the latest generation performance. In this session, we will dive deep into both Flex and T instances, which workloads are most suitable for these instances, high-level design, and ways customers can monitor the performance experience with these instances.

sessions.title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, you build a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances — the best of both worlds. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, you deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. You profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, and implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. By the end, you have a hybrid deployment with a live cost dashboard showing 30–45% savings vs. GPU-only baselines.

sessions.title: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
sessions.abstract: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each? In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

sessions.title: Optimize your Amazon EC2 instances: Profile, diagnose, decide
sessions.abstract: Which EC2 instance performs best? It depends on the workload. In this hands-on workshop, learn a repeatable methodology: observe with APerf, find breaking points, diagnose pipeline bottlenecks, and decide by price-performance across AWS Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. Then fix code guided by profiling data.

sessions.title: Accelerating AWS Graviton migrations at scale with AI
sessions.abstract: In this session, we explore how agents accelerate AWS Graviton migrations, improving price/performance for workloads across every phase from migration planning, compatibility validation, to performance testing and optimization. We’ll examine various agentic tools where attendees will learn how to choose the right solution and practical steps to implement the tools in their environments. Participants will leave with actionable strategies to reduce manual overhead and harness AI to unlock Graviton’s benefits at scale.

sessions.title: Optimize AI inference costs: Compare token economics on AWS silicon
sessions.abstract: Most enterprises run their entire AI pipeline on GPU and can overpay. AWS's silicon portfolio (Trainium & Graviton) along with NVIDIA GPU, Intel, and AMD all offer radically different cost-per-token economics for different workloads. This session delivers a decision framework for matching silicon to workload: training and inference on Trainium, RAG pipelines on Graviton, real-time agents on GPU, batch on Intel/AMD. Includes Bedrock vs. self-host crossover analysis, volume thresholds, and the architecture patterns to put the savings into practice.

sessions.title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
sessions.abstract: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. This session explores how customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across six patterns: vanilla AMIs, Firecracker on bare metal, nested virtualization, EKS with Kata/gVisor, containers, and one-instance-per-agent on Nitro. We cover isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-hour, and capacity planning at scale. Attendees leave with a framework for selecting the right pattern based on their scale, security, and maturity.

sessions.title: Security compliance and hardening with EC2 Image Builder
sessions.abstract: Discover how to leverage EC2 Image Builder to create secure, compliant, and hardened AMIs. Learn to automate security baseline implementation, including CIS benchmarks. We'll demonstrate building compliance checks into Image Builder pipelines, integrating vulnerability scanning, and implementing automated testing for regulatory standards.

sessions.title: Building a partner business on Amazon Lightsail
sessions.abstract: Amazon Lightsail is a simple, low-cost cloud platform designed for small and medium business workloads. In this chalk talk, we start with an overview of what Lightsail offers and common use cases partners are delivering today. We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

sessions.title: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
sessions.abstract: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

sessions.title: Democratizing precision time on EC2: make clocks work for you
sessions.abstract: Distributed systems builders have avoided relying on wall clock time for anything critical. Times are changing. Amazon Time Sync now delivers microsecond accuracy on EC2, making clock precision a feature, not a bug, in your system design. We whiteboard how customers in databases, AI, financial services, and media approach design in new ways, and share our open source ClockBound work on the clock error bound as a standard interface for your applications.

sessions.title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
sessions.abstract: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

sessions.title: Accelerating semiconductor design, simulation and verification on AWS
sessions.abstract: EDA workflows demand different compute across frontend, backend, and production phases. This session covers how AWS EC2 instances map to each design phase. Learn how to select instances for throughput-heavy frontend simulation versus memory-intensive backend verification, and hear how ISVs are qualifying tools on AWS Graviton and other CPU processors  to unlock better price-performance for chip design workload.

sessions.title: Compute innovation with the AWS Nitro System
sessions.abstract: The AWS Nitro System has fundamentally changed how we build and deliver EC2 instances, accelerating our pace of compute innovation while improving security and performance for customers. This session explores the Nitro architecture and the latest innovations it enables: multi-host for smaller metal sizes, reduced blast radius, higher performance, how Nitro has helped us in accelerating the pace of innovation, and delivering Flex instances. We'll dive deep into how the Nitro System continues to push the boundaries of what's possible in cloud compute.

sessions.title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
sessions.abstract: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

sessions.title: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
sessions.abstract: Most game studios pick server instances based on vibes. This session replaces that with numbers. We cover tick-rate budgets by genre (128-tick shooters need max frequency; 30-tick survival and 10-tick MMOs don’t), how to instrument Unreal, Unity, and Godot game loops, and how to build bot-driven load tests that tell you exactly how many players fit on an instance. Then we demonstrate it: same open-source game, deployed on M8azn and Graviton, player count ramped until it falls over. You’ll see where high clock speed matters and where you’re paying for headroom you don’t need.

sessions.title: Building crash prediction models with HPC and AI
sessions.abstract: High-fidelity crash simulations generate critical engineering insights but require significant compute time. Learn how Amazon EC2 hpc8a instances can be used to run hundreds of large-scale crash simulations and train surrogate AI models that predict crash outcomes in seconds instead of hours. We’ll also discuss how organizations are migrating CAE workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development.

sessions.title: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
sessions.abstract: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. This chalk talk unpacks how AWS hybrid workflows enabled these outcomes and what enterprises should do now to capture ROI with quantum.

sessions.title: AI agents for HPC operations
sessions.abstract: Managing HPC infrastructure shouldn’t slow down science and engineering. Learn how AI-powered agents with AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) automate workload placement, detect and recover from failures, and simplify day-to-day cluster operations. Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

sessions.title: Bringing better Amazon EC2 price performance to your pipeline with AWS Graviton
sessions.abstract: Which workload should move to AWS Graviton first? And what actually changes in your pipeline? In this code talk, we answer both live. We profile an application portfolio to find strong Arm64 candidates, check dependency and library compatibility, and update a working CI/CD pipeline to build multi-architecture container images for x86 and Arm64, so you see exactly what changes and why. Then we deploy the workload and run a side-by-side load test to compare price performance. You'll leave with a repeatable workload-selection checklist and pipeline patterns you can apply to your own AWS Graviton adoption with minimal disruption.

sessions.title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
sessions.abstract: There are now three ways to migrate Java from x86 to Graviton. AWS Transform Custom runs at scale across hundreds of repos with managed CI/CD and validation. The open-source Java skill runs locally in any agentic IDE, no AWS credentials needed. The Arm MCP server (in Kiro) goes broader, covering non-Java languages and general x86-to-Arm patterns. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and migration timeline. We demo all three on the same codebase, show where each succeeds and where it hands off, and give you a decision framework so you pick the right tool before you start.

sessions.title: Canva's migration to AWS Graviton: from 2% to 54% in 10 months
sessions.abstract: Canva shifted its massive compute fleet from 2% to 23% Graviton adoption in just two months, then scaled to 54% over the following eight months, delivering meaningful cost savings and performance improvements along the way. This session covers the technical blockers the team encountered and overcame and the strategies that made rapid migration possible at enterprise scale. Walk away with practical, battle-tested patterns for planning and executing large-scale Arm migrations, whether you're just getting started or looking to accelerate an existing effort.

sessions.title: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
sessions.abstract: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

sessions.title: Your next Quantum developer might be an AI agent
sessions.abstract: AI is changing who can build quantum applications. See how AI assistants including Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Jupyter AI, and Classiq help developers move from natural-language prompts to optimized quantum workloads on Amazon Braket. Learn how AI generates code, synthesizes hardware-aware circuits, benchmarks on simulators and QPUs, and integrates with HPC resources. Through real examples, you'll see how AI-native workflows reduce complexity, accelerate experimentation, and make quantum development accessible to more builders.

sessions.title: PyTorch optimizations: Faster AI and lower costs with AWS Graviton
sessions.abstract: Explore the latest PyTorch optimizations for Arm-based hardware, from improved kernel performance on AWS Graviton to faster training and inference at lower compute cost. We cover real benchmark results, the open-source contributions driving these improvements, and what it looks like to run modern AI workloads on Arm today. Whether you are tuning a model, contributing upstream, or just curious about what the community has been shipping, come get a grounded view of where things stand and where they are heading.

sessions.title: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
sessions.abstract: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis. Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.

sessions.title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
sessions.abstract: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.

sessions.title: EC2 Spot: Capacity patterns and strategies from the team that runs it
sessions.abstract: In this chalk talk, two engineers from the EC2 Spot team share what they see from the inside: how capacity behaves across regions, instance families, and time of day, including why Graviton-based Spot is consistently available and how seasonal patterns create predictable opportunities. Bring your Spot architecture questions. We'll whiteboard real diversification strategies, walk through anonymized examples from our most successful customers, and discuss what separates workloads that scale effortlessly on Spot from those that struggle.

sessions.title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
sessions.abstract: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.

sessions.title: Auto Scaling meets Capacity Reservations: Patterns that work
sessions.abstract: Capacity Reservations hold your instances. Auto Scaling right-sizes your fleet. Together, they give you both availability and cost efficiency. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to make them work seamlessly. We'll walk through  strategies that keep reservation utilization high during scale-in, mixed-instance policies that balance cost and availability, and fallback patterns for Capacity Blocks transitions. Bring your scaling architecture and we'll work through it on the board.

sessions.title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
sessions.abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. In this chalk talk, learn how to match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Explore the decision framework covering instance types, NICE DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration with Research and Engineering Studio (RES). Whether supporting a VFX render farm's artist desktops, an oil company's subsurface workstations, or an automotive design studio, leave with guidance balancing performance, cost, and simplicity.

sessions.title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
sessions.abstract: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

sessions.title: Everything you've wanted to know about performance on EC2 instances
sessions.abstract: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.

sessions.title: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
sessions.abstract: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like  physics. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for you own projects

sessions.title: Automating macOS at scale: AMI build, TCC, and provisioning on EC2 Mac
sessions.abstract: Automating macOS in the cloud brings challenges Linux and Windows don't. Going from a fresh EC2 Mac instance to a production-ready fleet means clearing non-obvious hurdles: building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder and Packer, pre-approving TCC permissions, bootstrapping Systems Manager, and working with Apple's security model. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the real friction points teams hit: image pipelines, the TCC dialog problem, remote access, MDM enrollment, and fleet provisioning. Bring your toughest macOS automation questions; most of the session is open Q&A.

sessions.title: From DNA to discovery: Build a genomics HPC pipeline on AWS
sessions.abstract: Build and run a real genomics variant-calling Slurm pipeline on AWS PCS using a mixed Graviton + GPU fleet. Cover PCS queue design, Slurm partition strategy, FSx for Lustre, EFA networking, and result aggregation to S3. Walk away with a reproducible, production-grade HPC workflow for life-sciences workloads.

sessions.title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open source models, and Amazon Bedrock.

sessions.title: From zero to HPC: Build production clusters with AWS PCS
sessions.abstract: Master AWS Parallel Computing Service at re:Invent. Build fully managed compute environments with zero setup. This hands-on session covers job submission, resource optimization, and intuitive interfaces to accelerate workflows for researchers and engineers. Scale faster without the complexity.

sessions.title: Orchestrating Physical AI workloads on AWS: Compute and pipeline patterns
sessions.abstract: Physical AI projects — robotics, autonomous systems, digital twins — require complex multi-stage pipelines spanning simulation, training, evaluation, and edge deployment. Each stage demands different compute and orchestration. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architecture patterns combining AWS Batch for parallel simulation, Amazon EKS with Karpenter for heterogeneous GPU/Trainium training, and SageMaker Hyperpod showcasing managed resiliency. We'll compare when to use EKS vs. Batch vs. ParallelCluster, discuss cost optimization with Capacity Blocks and Spot, and solve attendee architectures live on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: The cloud holodeck: Stream NVIDIA Omniverse, scale headless sim on AWS
sessions.abstract: Interactive simulation needs RTX-class GPUs engineers lack; rendering millions of frames needs a fleet nobody wants to babysit. Amazon DCV streams a full NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to any browser, while AWS Batch runs the same scenes headless across GPU fleets for scale. The AWS Visual Asset Management System is the control plane: launching jobs, tracking runs, and versioning outputs. Watch an engineer open a cloud viewport and fan out a thousand-frame jobs live.

sessions.title: Getting the capacity you need: EC2 Launch APIs and Intelligent Auto Scaling deep dive
sessions.abstract: Getting the right compute at the right time is a two-part challenge: launching instances effectively and scaling them intelligently. This deep dive covers both. First, we explore RunInstances—EC2's oldest and most important API—sharing launch best practices, how flexibility helps you get the capacity you need, and how EC2 Fleet incorporates advanced strategies into your calls. Then we go under the hood of EC2 Auto Scaling, and the intelligence that also scales DynamoDB, WorkSpaces, EMR, SageMaker AI, and Aurora. Learn how to use target tracking, predictive scaling, and auto-tuning to automatically and intelligently scale your workloads.

sessions.title: AI-driven optimizations for HPC configurations on AWS
sessions.abstract: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.

sessions.title: Aperf: An all-in-one tool for performance data collection and analysis
sessions.abstract: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. Finally, we'll open the conversation to collect feedback and feature requests from the audience.

sessions.title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
sessions.abstract: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.

sessions.title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
sessions.abstract: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.

sessions.title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
sessions.abstract: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.

sessions.title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
sessions.abstract:
Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose.

Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

sessions.title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
sessions.abstract: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

sessions.title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
sessions.abstract: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.

sessions.title: A DevOps Approach to Recover at Scale from Disaster or Ransomware
sessions.abstract: Recovering your cloud workload completely after a regional event or ransomware attack is not a checklist; it demands a culture of resilience that turns individual craft into reliable recovery.  That culture is built through DevOps. Clear communication, team empowerment, and frequent experimentation and measurement are what separate teams that recover from teams that hope. This session covers the technical requirements for recovering cloud workloads at scale, and the DevOps practices that make those requirements actually work under pressure. You'll leave with practical knowledge to drive full recovery in the face of the worst disasters.

sessions.title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
sessions.abstract: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

sessions.title: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
sessions.abstract: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

sessions.title: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify  merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.

sessions.title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
sessions.abstract: You have enough GPUs in your server to cover your software requirements. But is that all you need to consider? In a world where everyone is fighting for GPUs, picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes an engineering team makes at scale. This session shares lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately. You'll see how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and how to use AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. Leave with a cloud and bare metal architectural pattern and a GPU selection framework covering workload fit and server tradeoffs.

sessions.title: Beyond the Docs: Operating Scoped VPC Endpoints in Real Environments
sessions.abstract: Scoped VPC endpoint policies look simple, until production traffic proves otherwise. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through real-world failures we've encountered while deploying account- and org-scoped endpoint policies and trace the identity flows, auth chains, and hidden dependencies behind them. Together, we'll explore a key lesson: endpoint policies evaluate the request that's actually made, not the request you think you're making. Bring your questions and experiences as we whiteboard the assumptions that lead to outages and learn how to spot them before they impact production.

sessions.title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

sessions.title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
sessions.abstract: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

sessions.title: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
sessions.abstract:
Opening a bank account used to take days A neobank does it in 90 seconds. The secret: five specialized agents — Identity, Document Analysis, Fraud, Compliance Risk, and Customer Experience orchestrated by a supervisor on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. This Talk builds that KYC pipeline live: three API calls, no orchestration boilerplate, agents running across jurisdictions with built-in compliance and audit trails
You'll see real event-driven architecture with Amazon MSK, real Bedrock Guardrails, and exactly what breaks when you scale it. Production KYC, live code — and the cost and abandonment numbers that make it matter.

sessions.title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
sessions.abstract: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of enterprises have rolled back a deployed AI agent, and the organizations that invested in governance roll back more often, not less. 88% of pilots never reach production. The infrastructure that gets an agent from demo to production is where the gap lives. We'll walk through the failure patterns that cause rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.

sessions.title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
sessions.abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

sessions.title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
sessions.abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

sessions.title: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
sessions.abstract: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.

sessions.title: From Fragmented Infra to Golden Path: An Internal Developer Platform on EKS
sessions.abstract: Every team wanted to ship faster, but each was reinventing the same wheels: clusters, pipelines, infrastructure, access. So we built an internal developer platform on Amazon EKS — one golden path that lets product teams go from idea to running service without becoming Kubernetes experts. This is the honest story of that journey. We'll show how we used EKS as the foundation, Crossplane to provision cloud infrastructure through Kubernetes APIs, and Argo CD to drive everything through GitOps. We'll walk through the challenges that nearly derailed us and share what actually moved the needle. You'll leave with a realistic map of the terrain: what worked, what hurt, and what we'd do differently.

sessions.title: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
sessions.abstract: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.

sessions.title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
sessions.abstract: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

sessions.title: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
sessions.abstract: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.

sessions.title: Make your Connect data talk: 10x faster answers with Quick
sessions.abstract: Your Amazon Connect contact center knows why handle time spiked yesterday. The hard part is making it confess. The old way: ask another team, wait for the next report, lose hours. We made it self-serve with Amazon Quick Suite. First we tried the obvious path, exporting Connect's raw records to S3, and spent days fighting data that still came out wrong. Then we pivoted to the Connect analytics data lake: contact records, Contact Lens, and sentiment, accurate, zero ETL. The one catch was cross-account Connect Lake Formation. Now anyone asks Quick in plain language and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster to answer.

sessions.title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.

sessions.title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
sessions.abstract: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.
