sessions.title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
sessions.abstract: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

sessions.title: Practical PKI for On-Prem Devices with IAM Roles Anywhere
sessions.abstract: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. In this session, we'll talk you through multiple ways to set up or use PKI - such as Belgium's eID or a hardware key - to securely access AWS with phishing resistant authentication built using IAM Roles Anywhere. This will include live demos and code samples. By the end of the session we will stop worrying about plain text credential storage because we can use trusted hardware instead.

sessions.title: One-Way Doors: Launching a Regulated Financial Exchange on AWS in 2026
sessions.abstract: "AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (Access Analyzer, Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, and WAF) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late."

sessions.title: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
sessions.abstract: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.

sessions.title: The future of Kubernetes on AWS
sessions.abstract: Kubernetes has become a standard for organizations looking to modernize their application portfolios. AWS developed Amazon EKS to make Kubernetes more accessible to organizations of all sizes, helping them focus on what matters most for their businesses. In this session, join Amazon EKS product leadership to learn about the latest innovations and strategies for building Kubernetes platforms and applications faster, including building and orchestrating agents. Discover how various organizations use Amazon EKS to run their most demanding applications in the cloud, on premises, and at the edge.

sessions.title: Launch a production container app in under 5 minutes
sessions.abstract: Amazon ECS Express Mode reduces container deployment to three required inputs and a single CLI command. In this builders session, deploy a web application with built-in load balancing, autoscaling, TLS, and canary deployments configured automatically. Explore the full service lifecycle from creation through updates to deletion and see how shared ALBs keep costs low across multiple services. Ideal for developers new to Amazon ECS or looking to simplify their deployment workflow. Bring a laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Fundamentals to scale Kubernetes across your organization
sessions.abstract: Ready to get hands-on with Amazon EKS? This modular workshop begins with Kubernetes fundamentals and lets you choose topics that match your interests including generative AI, observability, networking, security, and more. You can learn how to optimize scaling with Karpenter, automate day-to-day operations with EKS Auto Mode, troubleshoot real-world issues, and extend clusters on-premises with EKS Hybrid Nodes. Get hands-on building resilient, production-grade clusters on Amazon EKS following industry best practices and explore the latest Amazon EKS features, choosing only the modules that matter most to you.

sessions.title: Move your app to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and forget the ops
sessions.abstract: Running a production application should not mean owning the infrastructure under it. This lightning talk shows how AWS Elastic Beanstalk assumes ongoing operational responsibility for your applications — deployment, scaling, patching, monitoring, and upgrades — whether you bring source code, a container image, or an existing workload. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.

sessions.title: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
sessions.abstract: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.

sessions.title: Hybrid Kubernetes made simple: EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway for on-prem and edge AI
sessions.abstract: Enterprises are migrating from legacy hypervisors to Kubernetes-native stacks but need hybrid connectivity without complex network changes. In this builder session, attendees set up the newly launched Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway to seamlessly connect on-premises worker nodes to a cloud EKS control plane without modifying existing network infrastructure. They deploy an AI inference workload spanning cloud and edge, configure pod-to-pod communication across environments, implement data residency controls, and validate failover scenarios.

sessions.title: Agentic developer experience with Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Transform your Kubernetes development workflow using generative AI. In this workshop, use Kiro CLI and the EKS MCP Server to automate complex operations, troubleshoot applications through natural language, and deploy micro services on Amazon EKS — all with AI-powered assistance. Work through hands-on labs: explore clusters using natural language, fix connectivity and ingress issues by orchestrating EKS MCP with Terraform MCP, and deploy new application components using AI-guided analysis. Leave with practical skills to integrate AI-powered automation into your existing Kubernetes workflows and dramatically improve developer productivity.

sessions.title: Accelerate declarative resource management with Amazon EKS Capabilities
sessions.abstract: Platform teams struggle to deliver self-service infrastructure that is both fast and governed. Developers want Kubernetes-native provisioning, but adopting new tools while managing existing IaC investments creates friction. In this builders session, explore the latest Amazon EKS Capabilities features including kro Collections, Graph Revisions, and reactive watches for advanced declarative resource management. Then use Kiro to build an agentic workflow that accelerates migration from legacy IaC to Kubernetes-native resource definitions. Leave with working implementations you can bring back to your platform.

sessions.title: Layered security for Amazon EKS: Patterns that scale
sessions.abstract: Kubernetes gives you powerful primitives for running workloads at scale, but its default configuration prioritizes flexibility over security. In this chalk talk, we work through a layered defense strategy for Amazon EKS: hardening the control plane, implementing least-privilege RBAC and pod security standards, securing the software supply chain, enforcing network segmentation, and building runtime threat detection. We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
sessions.abstract: Raise the bar on your software supply chain security with AWS. In this chalk talk, we will discuss DevOps security best-practices, threat detection and incident response for containers, and how to leverage AWS security services including Amazon ECR, Amazon GuardDuty, and Amazon Inspector to protect your Amazon EKS workloads. Discover how you can ensure CVE patching while optimizing storage to accelerate image delivery through seamless integration with open-source tools for publishing and deploying containerized workloads at scale. Learn how to efficently streamline your software supply chain while mitigating risks.

sessions.title: Demystifying the shared security model on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Running containers in production demands security controls at every layer. This chalk talk covers the Amazon ECS shared responsibility model, including IAM policies for task isolation, VPC networking with awsvpc mode, and runtime protections. Explore how Amazon ECS Managed Instances and AWS Fargate automates security patching and enforces instance refresh cycles while maintaining workload availability. Discuss practical patterns for secrets injection, image scanning, and network segmentation. Bring questions about securing your specific container architectures for an open technical discussion.

sessions.title: Right-size and scale Amazon ECS with effective autoscaling patterns
sessions.abstract: Autoscaling containerized workloads means scaling both tasks and the infrastructure underneath them. This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

sessions.title: Connect your Amazon ECS services without the complexity
sessions.abstract: Service-to-service communication in containerized environments introduces routing, discovery, and encryption challenges. This chalk talk explores when to use Service Connect, VPC Lattice, load balancers, or direct service discovery on Amazon ECS and how to combine them as your architecture grows. Understand the trade-offs across latency, cost, and operational overhead so you can match the right pattern to each workload. Bring your architecture questions for an open technical discussion.

sessions.title: Ship software safely with Amazon ECS advanced deployments
sessions.abstract: Rolling update, blue/green, canary, or linear? Amazon ECS gives you deployment strategies with built-in safety controls, no extra tooling required. This chalk talk explores how native Amazon ECS deployment options work and when to use each one. Discuss traffic shifting percentages, validation hooks for pre-traffic testing, and alarm integration for automated rollbacks. Learn how to tune bake time and coordinate multi-service deployments so you can ship changes confidently at any scale. Bring your release pipeline challenges for an open discussion.

sessions.title: Securing and observing Amazon EKS clusters
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on session, explore how to automate the identification, analysis, and mitigation of risks in Amazon EKS clusters. Learn how to implement robust security controls—including role-based access control (RBAC), EKS Pod Identity, and service accounts—to apply least-privilege access and secure workload isolation. Discover how to use AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch to gain deep visibility into EKS cluster activities, enabling real-time monitoring and automated risk detection. You will learn the skills to automate risk management processes, helping your Kubernetes workloads remain resilient against evolving threats.

sessions.title: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Building and scaling inference workloads on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Connect and secure service-to-service networking on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: When your containerized services grow beyond a single cluster, networking becomes the bottleneck. Security groups block health checks, cross-VPC traffic needs custom solutions, and encrypting traffic feels like a full-time job. In this builder's session, configure secure service-to-service communication on Amazon ECS using Service Connect for discovery and encryption, VPC Lattice for cross-account connectivity, and load balancer patterns for external traffic. Implement end-to-end TLS, test failover between services, and observe traffic flows in real time. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Your multi-tenant SaaS application runs on Amazon ECS. Now your customers expect AI-powered features but adding agents to an existing platform introduces new challenges. Including tenant isolation for model access, per-tenant memory and conversation state, cost attribution across shared infrastructure, and agent orchestration at scale. In this workshop, you start with a working SaaS application on Amazon ECS and progressively add agentic capabilities using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement tenant-aware agent routing, configure isolated tool execution with ECS task-level security boundaries, add persistent memory per tenant, and instrument with end-to-end observability. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builder's session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including hardware-level task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

sessions.title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

sessions.title: Build a production multi-tier application on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tier containerized architecture on Amazon ECS from scratch. Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Deploy accelerated workloads with Amazon ECS Managed Instances
sessions.abstract: Amazon ECS Managed Instances let you run workloads on specialized EC2 hardware without managing the infrastructure underneath. In this workshop, deploy accelerated workloads across Graviton and ML accelerators on fully managed compute. Configure capacity providers, select instance types, and optimize costs through multi-task placement and Spot instances. Observe performance using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working configuration you can adapt for your own accelerated workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: From your first Amazon EKS cluster to a self-serve developer platform
sessions.abstract: The best Kubernetes platforms are invisible to the people who use them. Developers provision, deploy, and scale through self-service interfaces without needing Kubernetes expertise, while platform teams reclaim the cycles once spent on cluster operations and lifecycle management. That is the standard now that Amazon EKS is engineered to deliver. Come hear how EKS sees developer experience evolving: Auto Mode removing undifferentiated operational load through managed compute, scaling, and add-ons; EKS Capabilities exposing AWS services as governed, self-serve building blocks; and AI agents taking on operational workflows (upgrades, diagnostics, remediation) that platform teams have owned for years.

sessions.title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.

sessions.title: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale, and this session provides a product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. See how recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications on, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. We'll discuss the range of compute options, from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. You will leave this session knowing how to apply the newest ECS capabilities to your workloads today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds.

sessions.title: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
sessions.abstract: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving you access to the latest GPUs and accelerators. In this session, explore how to launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale based on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, and automatically recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances to serve GPU-backed workloads while optimizing cost and operational agility.

sessions.title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
sessions.abstract: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.

sessions.title: Accelerate application development with Amazon ECS Express Mode
sessions.abstract: What if deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS required just your code and a few configuration choices? Amazon ECS Express Mode makes that possible by handling observability, networking, and security out of the box. In this session, learn how Express Mode accelerates development for individual developers and platform teams without sacrificing control. Discover practical techniques to optimize your workflows, enhance reliability, and reduce operational overhead. Leave with actionable strategies to increase development velocity using the latest Amazon ECS innovations.

sessions.title: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
sessions.abstract: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.

sessions.title: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
sessions.abstract: Teams managing their Kubernetes fleet carry the full weight of the cluster: control plane, node lifecycle, add-on upgrades, and the operational toil. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling analyzes your existing clusters, translates manifests and add-on configurations, and flags what needs to change before you cut over. Learn the patterns for migrating workloads with minimal disruption, from node pools to networking to storage. Discover how teams reach a managed, self-scaling cluster in a fraction of the time manual migration takes.

sessions.title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

sessions.title: Observability-driven scaling: Teaching EKS clusters to right-size themselves
sessions.abstract: Scaling container workloads reactively by waiting for CPU to spike or pods to crash leaves money on the table and risks user-facing latency. This chalk talk explores observability-driven scaling: using CloudWatch Container Insights, KEDA, and custom metrics pipelines to make Amazon EKS clusters anticipate demand before it arrives. We walk through real architectures where teams replaced reactive HPA with predictive scaling informed by business metrics, reduced over-provisioning by 40%, and cut P99 latency during traffic ramps. Bring your scaling headaches and we'll whiteboard solutions together.

sessions.title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
sessions.abstract: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

sessions.title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

sessions.title: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
sessions.abstract: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.

sessions.title: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
sessions.abstract: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

sessions.title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.

sessions.title: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.

sessions.title: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
sessions.abstract: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.

sessions.title: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
sessions.abstract: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. AZ spread off means one zone failure takes your service down. Short health check grace periods kill containers that are still starting. Disabled circuit breakers let bad deploys roll forward across every task. Default dependency timeouts turn one slow call into a cascading outage. Placement constraints pack tasks onto too few hosts. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.

sessions.title: Accelerate platform engineering on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Platform teams struggle to balance developer velocity with operational efficiency. Self-service platforms promise faster delivery, but require orchestrating multiple tools, managing infrastructure complexity, and maintaining governance. In this workshop, you'll build an Internal Developer Platform using Amazon EKS Capabilities, which provides fully managed Argo CD for continuous deployment, ACK for AWS resource management, and kro for Kubernetes resource orchestration. You'll deploy polyglot applications, implement progressive delivery strategies, and automate infrastructure management while leveraging AI to boost productivity. Leave with practical experience in platform engineering patterns to ship faster without sacrificing control. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
sessions.abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

sessions.title: Cloud-native Java on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Learn how to build cloud-native Java applications based on best practices, and discover ways you can optimize application performance for fast startup and efficient resource usage in containerized environments. In this builders’ session, gain hands-on experience as you learn how to reduce memory overhead, lower cold start latency, and achieve sub-second startup times when building Java applications on Amazon EKS. You will also learn how to use Amazon Bedrock to analyze profiling and thread dump data to uncover performance patterns and generate optimization insights.

sessions.title: Optimize analytics workloads on Amazon EKS for performance and cost
sessions.abstract: The analytics landscape is undergoing a shift as global data volumes grow at unprecedented rates. This rapid growth, combined with rising demand for real-time analytics, is driving organizations to modernize and optimize their data processing pipelines and analytics workloads. EKS’s cost-performance and scalability make it the best place to run these workloads.  In this workshop, you will learn hands-on how to optimize EKS for Spark & Kafka workloads using different Karpenter configurations, Spot and Graviton instances, and NVMe volumes. You will also explore observability best practices and granular cost visualization per job. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Inside Amazon EKS: the resilient foundation for critical workloads
sessions.abstract: Real-time financial systems, large-scale AI, and mission-critical platforms run on Kubernetes, and they demand a robust engineering foundation. This session goes under the hood of what makes Amazon EKS the backbone for the most demanding workloads. See how cellular isolation contains blast radius and EKS Provisioned Control Planes eliminate downtime during peak operational periods, backed by an industry-leading SLA as clusters scale into large fleets. Learn how EKS Auto Mode integrates with Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to protect the control plane and running pods during an impaired Availability Zone, keeping critical applications available with no extra configuration.

sessions.title: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
sessions.abstract: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.

sessions.title: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes
sessions.abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore hybrid networking design patterns for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.

sessions.title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
sessions.abstract: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

sessions.title: Breaking down batch inference with Ray Data on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.

sessions.title: Scale financial risk simulations with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.

sessions.title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

sessions.title: Accelerating cost optimization on AWS
sessions.abstract: Finding and implementing cost optimization recommendations sustainably require constant monitoring and action. Join this session to learn how you can accelerate your optimization outcomes while maintaining flexibility in how savings are distributed across your organization. See how you can also measure, share and continuously improve your results.

sessions.title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
sessions.abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.

sessions.title: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk
sessions.abstract: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project.

sessions.title: Stop fighting fires: operations that prevent incidents
sessions.abstract: The cheapest incident is the one that never happens, yet most operations teams stay stuck in reactive firefighting. This session follows a real operational-excellence journey from reactive to preventive operations: using automation and guardrails to remediate configuration drift, enforce standards, and stop problems before they page anyone, with concrete results.

sessions.title: Best practices for agentic-driven operations
sessions.abstract: AI agents are moving from assistants to operators, but how do they actually work within your operational workflows? Understand the architecture of agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root cause across distributed systems, and execute remediation like rollbacks, scaling, and traffic shifts. Learn how agents reason over telemetry, sequence actions, and determine when to escalate. Explore best practices for shaping agent behavior through guardrails, approval gates, and feedback loops as core design elements. Leave with a framework for evaluating where agents should act autonomously versus where human judgment remains essential.

sessions.title: Improving operations with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.

sessions.title: Observability and operations in the AI era (customer)
sessions.abstract: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

sessions.title: Turn security logs into actionable intelligence
sessions.abstract: Security teams drown in logs but struggle to investigate fast. In this hands-on session, turn raw security telemetry from CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and VPC flow logs into actionable intelligence with Amazon CloudWatch. We'll centralize logs in the CloudWatch Unified Data Store, then query across sources to investigate real scenarios: after-hours data access, credential misuse, and exfiltration patterns. You'll build a security dashboard that surfaces who did what, from where, and when. Walk away with reusable queries and dashboards you can deploy in your own accounts, moving from reactive log search to proactive security visibility.

sessions.title: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
sessions.abstract: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.

sessions.title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
sessions.abstract: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you bring open source telemetry into managed backends, query metrics with PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, search logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all three signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. You decide what stays self-managed and what moves to managed, and build the queries and dashboards yourself.

sessions.title: Turn raw telemetry into answers with OpenTelemetry
sessions.abstract: Raw telemetry arrives noisy, unlabeled, and hard to query, so teams waste time cleaning data before they can act. In this hands-on builders session, you set up OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and traces from a live sample application, then use Amazon CloudWatch pipeline processors to enrich and normalize the data in flight. You build the enrichment rules, explore results with natural language query, and leave with a reusable pattern for turning raw signals into analysis-ready telemetry.

sessions.title: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
sessions.abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic and can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behavior without warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you monitor a running agent with metric filters, log queries, and contributor-insight rules to surface cost spikes, failures, and anomalous behavior. You build the detection rules and alarms yourself and leave able to apply them to your own agents.

sessions.title: Automate threat detection and response across your logs
sessions.abstract: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.

sessions.title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.title: Embed FinOps into your CI/CD pipelines
sessions.abstract: Cost overruns from infrastructure changes often go undetected until after deployment, making shift-left cost governance a critical capability for platform and DevOps engineers. This builders' session guides attendees through constructing a working cost estimation gate integrated directly into a CI/CD pipeline. Using AWS CodePipeline, the AWS Pricing Calculator, and CloudFormation change sets, attendees build a pipeline stage that evaluates infrastructure cost impact at pull request time and enforces configurable spend thresholds before deployment proceeds. Bring a laptop to complete hands-on exercises with expert guidance in a small-group setting.

sessions.title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

sessions.title: Orchestrate failover and failback for effective Disaster Recovery
sessions.abstract: Failing over one app is easy — orchestrating failover and failback across interdependent apps is where DR plans break. Real recovery requires dependency-aware orchestration for your entire application stack. In this code talk, we live-code full-stack failover using AWS Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region Switch to define dependency graphs so databases switch before app tiers, validate each step with readiness checks, and safely reverse the sequence for failback. Follow along and leave ready to replace your paper DR plan with coded, repeatable failover that meets your recovery objectives.

sessions.title: Automate patching and compliance with AI-powered visibility
sessions.abstract: Tracking patch compliance across hundreds of accounts is manual, slow, and hard to prove to auditors. In this hands-on builder's session, you automate patching and continuous compliance across Linux and Windows, then let AI do the heavy lifting: generate a multi-account compliance dashboard with spec-driven development and answer compliance questions with natural language instead of hand-building reports. You define patch baselines, maintenance windows, and exception rules, then reason through the trade-offs, rather than running pre-made scripts.

sessions.title: Build resilient apps on AWS: AI-driven recovery at any scale
sessions.abstract: Most teams discover resilience gaps during outages, not before. In this interactive chalk talk, you'll use the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub to map user journeys, define recovery objectives, discover dependencies, and run AI-powered failure mode assessments. You'll implement high availability improvements, deploy multi-region disaster recovery, and run the right automated disaster recovery tests that fit your architecture and use case. Walk away with a repeatable framework you can plug into your own environment next week.

sessions.title: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
sessions.abstract: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that resolves and proactively prevents incidents, optimizes application reliability and performance, and handles on-demand SRE tasks. Its real power is extensibility. In this hands-on workshop, set up an Agent Space, choose your own module, and add skills that encode your team's expertise. Run preventive recommendations across Lambda, databases, containers, analytics, or AI/ML workloads. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

sessions.title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
sessions.abstract: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

sessions.title: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
sessions.abstract: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

sessions.title: Custom SRE agents: From prompt to proactive ops with DevOps agent
sessions.abstract: In this builder session, learn how to create custom SRE agents that turn a simple prompt into automated, environment-specific operational workflows. Using pre-configured tools and integrations, you'll define agents tailored to your priorities, whether that's anomaly detection, performance optimization, cost analysis, or resiliency recommendations. See how agents combine real-time observability data with structured reasoning to surface actionable improvements without manual investigation. Walk away with hands-on experience designing an agent that monitors your operational patterns and proactively recommends next steps, so your team spends less time diagnosing and more time shipping.

sessions.title: Orchestrate multi-layer disaster recovery for critical workloads
sessions.abstract: Your AZ recovery plan and your Region failover plan were probably built by different teams, tested at different times, and have never run together. The result: untested failover paths that turn outages into incidents. Explore how to build a unified recovery framework with Amazon Application Recovery Controller. From zonal autoshift for rapid single-AZ mitigation, to Region switch for cross-Region failover, learn how ARC unifies both layers into a single orchestrated approach. Then discover how to run automated resilience tests that continuously validate your recovery posture before a real event forces the question.

sessions.title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
sessions.abstract: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

sessions.title: Trust but verify: Building the audit loop for AI-driven operations
sessions.abstract: AI agents act fast. Auditors ask questions slowly. Bridge that gap with an observability layer that satisfies both. This session walks through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore traces across multi-agent workflows, Amazon CloudWatch for decision-level visibility and drift detection, escalation thresholds that keep humans in the loop, and patterns for reconstructing agent reasoning after the fact. Walk away with a practical audit loop you can implement for agents running in production.

sessions.title: AI-Powered FinOps: Cloud Cost Optimization in Practice
sessions.abstract: Embed FinOps as an operational discipline using AI-powered cost optimization. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how to shift left on cloud financial management by integrating cost discipline throughout development. Explore AWS services for automated optimizations, rightsizing, and savings plans. Gain experience with AI/ML and container workload cost allocation, multi-cloud reporting, and AI-powered spend analysis. Implement automated strategies using real workload data. Laptop required

sessions.title: Observability patterns for agentic AI in production
sessions.abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic, multi-step, and make autonomous decisions and traditional APM isn't enough. Explore observability patterns for agentic workloads: reasoning chain tracing, token cost attribution, guardrail monitoring, and multi-agent coordination. We'll whiteboard architectures in real time. Bring your toughest production agent monitoring questions and leave with actionable patterns.

sessions.title: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
sessions.abstract: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

sessions.title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
sessions.abstract: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

sessions.title: Building a cost governance framework that scales
sessions.abstract: As your cloud footprint grows, so does the challenge of keeping costs accountable. In this chalk talk, we'll open with common cost governance challenges and then dig into how the AWS FinOps Agent and AWS cost management tools can address them. Together we'll whiteboard approaches for organizing cost data, setting budget guardrails, allocating spend back to the right teams, and building visibility across your organization. Bring your current FinOps challenges and leave with a repeatable governance model for financial sustainability.

sessions.title: Automate savings with AWS Billing and Cost Management services
sessions.abstract: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. Bring your questions and challenges.

sessions.title: Simplify multicloud: manage and monitor VMs in one place
sessions.abstract: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

sessions.title: AIOps strategy: foundations before firefighting
sessions.abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before deciding what they actually want it to handle, investment is racing ahead of maturity. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We map the two halves that teams miss: using AI to run operations and the operational foundations that let AI scale safely, such as cost, security, and organizational readiness. We discuss what to automate, what stays human, and where agents earn autonomy. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity checklist for your team.

sessions.title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
sessions.abstract: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

sessions.title: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
sessions.abstract: Inconsistent tags and no clear picture of what runs where get worse as your AWS footprint grows across accounts. In this code talk, we build the automation that keeps tagging clean at scale. We write a tag policy that enforces the keys and values that matter, wire up an AWS Config rule and remediation runbook that flag and fix non-compliant resources, and query untagged resources across thousands of resources and many accounts. We group assets into applications to keep governance consistent as teams multiply. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root cause.

sessions.title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
sessions.abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

sessions.title: Turn log storage into log intelligence
sessions.abstract: Give your operations teams the full picture without jumping between tools. Learn how to bring logs, metrics, and traces into a unified data store for analytics and improved troubleshooting. Instead of just storing logs and treating logs as text to grep during an outage, use centralization rules that bring telemetry together across accounts and regions, telemetry pipelines that enrich and route data in flight, intelligence tiering that matches storage cost to query value, and AI-assisted log analytics that surface answers instead of waiting for you to ask the right question. This is about making logs work for you — not the other way around. You'll leave with a clear architecture for unified log analytics you can take back to your org and put into production.

sessions.title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS (customer)
sessions.abstract: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

sessions.title: Building AI-powered, app-centric unified observability
sessions.abstract: Your apps run everywhere, but you're still switching tabs to understand what's happening. In this session, we'll show how CloudWatch delivers AI-powered, app-centric infrastructure monitoring where you already work. We'll walk through how unified observability connects application health to underlying infrastructure across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, and how AI surfaces the insights that matter before you go looking. You'll see how CloudWatch shifts from reactive dashboards to proactive, intelligent monitoring that meets you where you are.

sessions.title: Correlate app signals to infra root cause in hybrid environments
sessions.abstract: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

sessions.title: Follow that log from pipeline to intelligence
sessions.abstract: You've got logs flowing from everywhere, but when an issue spans multiple accounts or regions, you're stuck jumping between consoles trying to piece together what happened. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the end-to-end path a log takes from ingestion pipeline to a unified data layer to log analytics. We'll break down where visibility gaps form and why. Learn how you can connect these layers to trace a problem across your entire environment without losing context.

sessions.title: Best practices for building an observability strategy
sessions.abstract: Many teams buy tools before they agree on what they actually need to observe, ending up with multiple dashboards and unnecessary alerts. Learn what to instrument, what deserves an alert, how to set SLOs tied to real user experience, and how to keep the noise down as you grow. We will talk through the operating model decisions that make or break observability, such as who owns the tool, who pays for it, and how on-call actually works. Get a strategy framework and maturity checklist you can bring back to your leadership and engineering teams.

sessions.title: Learnings from resilience testing in AWS
sessions.abstract: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.

sessions.title: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
sessions.abstract: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.

sessions.title: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
sessions.abstract: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.

sessions.title: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself.

sessions.title: Building agentic workflows for augmented observability
sessions.abstract: Drowning in observability data but starving for insights? In this live, interactive coding session, we'll build an AI agent that transforms raw telemetry into actionable intelligence. We'll build a system that correlates metrics, logs and traces from Amazon CloudWatch. Our agent will analyze patterns, create relevant monitoring artifacts, and provide natural language explanations of complex issues. We'll show how to productionize the agent to autonomously respond to operational events, creating a proactive observability workflow. Join us to explore the future of AI-augmented observability.

sessions.title: Scaling operations with MCP, ACP, and A2A
sessions.abstract: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

sessions.title: Optimize AI apps on Amazon Bedrock for cost, latency, and control
sessions.abstract: As AI workloads scale, engineers face complex trade-offs between cost, latency, and response quality. This code talk explores advanced optimization techniques for production AI applications built on Amazon Bedrock, including prompt engineering strategies, model selection criteria, caching architecture, and context window management. Through live coding and real code samples, attendees examine the engineering reasoning behind each design decision, observe direct cost impact using AWS Billing and Cost Management, and explore how to instrument applications to detect performance regressions when optimization changes are applied.

sessions.title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you manage the loop or let AWS handle it? In this code talk, we break down two approaches: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a fully managed agent loop with built-in memory and tool routing, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime for when you need full control. Then we sketch how AWS DevOps Agent's remote MCP support enables headless, tight-loop integration with your custom agents. Bring your architecture challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust agentic pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

sessions.title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
sessions.abstract: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

sessions.title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
sessions.abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

sessions.title: Analyze your telemetry data with natural-language queries
sessions.abstract: During high-severity incidents, dependency on a single engineer who knows the query language creates critical bottlenecks. This code talk explores the architecture and design trade-offs behind a natural-language query workflow that translates plain-language questions into executable queries across metrics, logs, and traces. Live coding demonstrates how to integrate AI-powered query capabilities, correlate telemetry signals from a unified interface, and surface root-cause insights without writing query syntax. You'll see the underlying prompt construction, query translation patterns, and signal correlation strategies that drive reliable observability workflows in production environments.

sessions.title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
sessions.abstract: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.

sessions.title: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
sessions.abstract: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.

sessions.title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
