sessions.abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.

sessions.title: Autonomous DBOps: Agentic AI for maintaining databases
sessions.abstract: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. In this builders' session, learn how to leverage agentic AI solutions implementing LLM-powered autonomous agents to monitor, diagnose, and optimize relational databases in real time. We will demonstrate how AI agents can analyze slow query logs, recommend or apply tuning actions, and trigger intelligent alerts using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Cloudwatch, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Systems Manager. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Optimize your Amazon Aurora resources to reduce costs
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native managed relational database that lets you create, manage, and scale your database resources with ease. In this session, dive deep into Aurora cost components and see how you can use cost-focused features and tooling to optimize costs for your workload without sacrificing performance or scale. Learn how the Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration can help you achieve cost savings for I/O-intensive workloads, and discover how Database Savings Plans can provide additional cost reductions through flexible commitment-based pricing.

sessions.title: HA and DR design patterns for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Oracle
sessions.abstract: Explore high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) design patterns for SQL Server and Oracle databases on Amazon RDS. In this session, learn about the features offered by Amazon RDS for business continuity, including Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and cross-region replication. Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

sessions.title: Safer, simpler, faster upgrades with managed blue/green deployments
sessions.abstract: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. In this chalk talk, you will architect a blue/green database upgrade solution to support major or minor engine version upgrades and perform schema changes with minimal and predictable downtime. Active participation is encouraged as you architect a solution to meet your requirements. In open discussion, learn the trade-offs involved in database management when using blue/green deployments and how to design the most effective upgrade solution to meet your needs.

sessions.title: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

sessions.title: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Most agentic AI architectures stitch together separate stores for vectors and workflow state, adding cost and operational overhead. In this session, explore how Aurora PostgreSQL consolidates these roles into a single database, using pgvector for semantic retrieval, PostgreSQL full-text search for keyword queries, and native state persistence for multi-agent checkpointing. Learn to connect agents directly to Aurora using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, govern every interaction with row-level security and audit trails, and orchestrate resilient, stateful workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and LangGraph without additional infrastructure. Leave with reusable patterns for governed, real-time agentic systems.

sessions.title: Build a digital asset tokenization issuance solution
sessions.abstract: The emergence of digital assets and stablecoins requires bridging traditional message-based finance protocols such as SWIFT and ISO 20022 to programmable settlement rails while preserving institutional security, auditability, and governance. In this session, learn how to build a production-ready end-to-end hybrid settlement architecture on AWS that ingests financial messages, normalizes them into canonical settlement instructions, and executes tokenized asset transfers on-chain. Explore hardware-backed signing with AWS KMS, on-chain signer governance, and three settlement patterns: issuance, redemption, and transfer, with full audit trails, idempotent transaction handling, and EIP-712 typed signing. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Optimize cost & performance in Amazon RDS for SQL Server
sessions.abstract: Cost and performance are top of mind for customers, and these topics go hand in hand. In this chalk talk, learn how to deploy a performant and cost-effective Amazon RDS for SQL Server solution that fits your needs. Explore RDS monitoring tools and native SQL Server features that can be leveraged to pinpoint query inefficiencies, optimize workloads, and right-size your database instances for both cost and peak performance.

sessions.title: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
sessions.abstract: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Leave with actionable best practices drawn from real customer deployments at scale.

sessions.title: Optimizing prediction market and trading infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges, and prediction markets share a critical challenge: managing the tension between resiliency and latency. AWS customers have solved this at scale on low-latency platforms trading digital assets 24/7. In this session, AWS specialists dive deep into architecture patterns and real-world examples addressing each challenge. Leave with best practices for designing resilient, low-latency trading infrastructure using the latest AWS capabilities built for these markets.

sessions.title: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 400+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
sessions.abstract: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 400 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Attendees leave with a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.

sessions.title: Agents on call: Autonomous DB ops on Amazon Aurora with Expedia Group
sessions.abstract: Expedia Group manages thousands of database instances across hundreds of AWS accounts. When incidents strike at this scale, every second counts. In this session, learn how a customer-driven vision for agentic AI evolved into a joint design partnership for autonomous database operations on Amazon Aurora. Discover how agents diagnose incidents across fleet-scale telemetry and deliver actionable recommendations to engineers. This joint initiative demonstrates how AI agents reduce incident response time and serves as a blueprint for teams seeking to automate database operations at scale. Learn how AWS is building the underlying capabilities to make autonomous operations real.

sessions.title: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
sessions.abstract: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

sessions.title: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.

sessions.title: Essentials for migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.abstract: Migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can be a transformative journey, offering significant cost savings and performance benefits. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. In this session, discover the essential things you need to know to ensure a smooth and successful migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL and the optimal architectures to enable such a migration. Learn best practices and pitfalls to avoid from seasoned experts who have helped many customers walk this path.

sessions.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
sessions.abstract: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

sessions.title: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
sessions.abstract: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora DSQL and its architecture
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that uses decades of Amazon innovation and operational excellence. In this session, dive into the design and key innovative technologies that make Aurora DSQL the ideal choice for new applications and applications that require the highest level of resilience. Learn how active-active architecture in Aurora DSQL delivers single- and multi-Region resiliency and virtually unlimited scale

sessions.title: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Semantic search, agents, and image matching with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
sessions.abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building globally distributed applications with DynamoDB global tables
sessions.abstract: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

sessions.title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.abstract: As applications evolve from RAG to agentic workflows, retrieval must support more than top-k semantic matches. In this session, use Aurora PostgreSQL as the core search and context engine for agentic hybrid retrieval. Implement PostgreSQL full-text search for lexical retrieval, pgvector semantic similarity, SQL and metadata filters, fuzzy matching, reciprocal rank fusion, model-based reranking, source attribution, and retrieval diagnostics. Then wire these capabilities into agent tools that decompose complex questions, gather targeted evidence, compare sources, explain ranking signals, and synthesize cited answers. Leave with working code, schema patterns, ranking templates, and techniques for trustworthy retrieval-heavy AI applications.

sessions.title: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

sessions.title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
sessions.abstract: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

sessions.title: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
sessions.abstract: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn about the architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB. Gain a better understanding of when to use DynamoDB and why DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. Leave with a new perspective on how to design your own applications.

sessions.title: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Production agentic AI applications demand strong governance, precise retrieval, and consistent policy enforcement across every agent interaction. In this session, explore a retail shopping scenario where a Strands SDK dispatcher routes shoppers to specialist agents. Aurora powers hybrid search with PostgreSQL full-text search, pgvector for semantic retrieval, and Cohere Rerank for relevance ranking, while managing inventory, orders, customer records, and a queryable JSONB audit ledger. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy orchestrate agents, preserve context, expose tools, and apply Cedar authorization to sensitive actions. Build your own governed agentic AI search application and leave with reusable patterns. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Demystifying Aurora DSQL transactions and concurrency control
sessions.abstract: Join this session to learn about Amazon Aurora DSQL's optimistic concurrency control (OCC). Explore building an application to understand the impact of OCC on your relational workloads, how it differs from traditional databases, and how to achieve the desired semantics in DSQL's OCC model.

sessions.title: Advanced data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Amazon DynamoDB is a popular choice for modern applications because it’s a serverless database that provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Optimizing your usage of DynamoDB requires a different approach to data modeling than traditional relational databases. In this session, explore advanced techniques to help you get the most out of DynamoDB. Learn how to “think in DynamoDB” by learning the DynamoDB foundations and principles for data modeling. Further, learn practical strategies and DynamoDB features to handle difficult use cases in your application.

sessions.title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: This session provides a deep dive into Amazon DynamoDB and shares insights into how DynamoDB is architected and how it’s able to deliver the scalability and response times that customers have come to expect. DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. In this talk we explore the architecture of DynamoDB, and of several specific features. You will understand how we architected DynamoDB to deliver predictable low latency at any scale, and how best to develop your own applications to delight your customers.

sessions.title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB using design puzzles
sessions.abstract: In this session, dive deep into how Amazon DynamoDB works at scale by collaboratively solving a few design puzzles that may seem simple but are actually complex. Learn how to look beyond the obvious solution to find a more effective and scalable one with an understanding of how DynamoDB operates.

sessions.title: Reduce token costs with semantic caching on Amazon ElastiCache
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent AI systems now orchestrate complex workflows requiring frequent foundation model calls. In this session, learn how you can reduce latencies to single-digit milliseconds from single-digit seconds with vector search for Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in agentic AI applications using semantic caching, while also reducing the cost incurred from your foundation models for production workloads. By implementing semantic caching in agentic architectures like RAG-powered assistants and autonomous agents, customers can create performant and cost-effective production-scale agentic AI systems.

sessions.title: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
sessions.abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

sessions.title: Optimize AI workloads with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless
sessions.abstract: Building highly scalable, high-performance AI and data-driven applications requires intelligent caching strategies. In this session, learn how to build with Amazon ElastiCache to scale workloads across caching patterns such as session caching, KV-caching, and more. Dive deep into microsecond latency networking optimizations that enable sub-millisecond response times, and explore common performance pitfalls with practical solutions to keep applications running smoothly.

sessions.title: Advanced data modeling for Amazon ElastiCache
sessions.abstract: This session delves into the intricacies of Amazon ElastiCache data modeling using the purpose-built Valkey data types to optimize application performance and scalability. Explore the use of strings, sets, sorted sets, hashes, bitmaps, and geospatial indexes to model complex relationships and solve use cases such as caching, session store, feature store, real-time analytics, geospatial applications, and rate limiters.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
sessions.abstract: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

sessions.title: Evolve Amazon DynamoDB data models with no application impact
sessions.abstract: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Learn versioning strategies, backward compatibility patterns, and migration approaches for production applications. In this session, architect a solution that covers attribute addition and removal, data type changes, and index modifications while maintaining 24/7 availability. Explore real-world migration scenarios, rollback strategies, and handling distributed application dependencies. The best practices covered in this session are essential for teams managing large-scale DynamoDB applications requiring continuous evolution while serving millions of requests.

sessions.title: Better, faster, cheaper: How Valkey is revolutionizing caching
sessions.abstract: Discover how the powerful combination of open source Valkey and Amazon ElastiCache is transforming the landscape of distributed caching. In this session, explore recent innovations including advanced search capabilities such as full-text search, a memory-efficient dictionary that reduces memory usage by up to 40%, and a multi-threaded architecture that enables instantaneous scaling by up to 230%. Learn about the infrastructure that enables ElastiCache to patch hundreds of thousands of customers while maintaining high availability, even for extreme workloads like Prime Day's trillion requests per minute.

sessions.title: Build governed remediation workflows for Aurora database operations
sessions.abstract: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for slow queries, vacuum issues, index changes, and parameter tuning, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting with a performance troubleshooting recommendation, learn to classify operational risk, validate the proposed change, apply policy-based approval gates, execute with scoped permissions, and capture an auditable trail from insight to action. Explore custom security controls, blast-radius reduction, human-in-the-loop governance, rollback planning, post-change verification across development, staging, and production environments, and integration with signals from your own agents. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Multi-tenant agentic AI with Aurora and DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build a multi-Region, active-active rewards app with Aurora DSQL
sessions.abstract: In this session, get hands-on experience with Amazon Aurora DSQL, a serverless distributed SQL database that delivers active-active high availability. Learn how to build a retail rewards points application with active-active resiliency across multiple Availability Zones and two Regions. Explore how ACID transactions and active-active replication work in Aurora DSQL. Discover best practices for data model and application design and more. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AI-assisted data modeling for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: In this session, learn practical Amazon DynamoDB data modeling through an AI-assisted approach. Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations
sessions.abstract: Frontier agents like Amazon DevOps Agent are strong at broad investigation, correlation, and orchestration, but production database operations require domain-specific execution depth. In this workshop, turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into eval-driven agent skills that DevOps Agent can invoke. Define evals across deterministic scenarios such as lock contention, replica lag diagnosis, long-running transactions blocking vacuum cleanup, connection saturation, and query plan regression. Run evals to surface gaps, then author a skill with pre-flight checks, execution sequence, validation, and rollback. Iterate with eval results, wire the skill into DevOps Agent, and leave with a working skill, harness, and reusable productionization methodology.

sessions.title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Attendees leave with reusable patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

sessions.title: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
sessions.abstract: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Code real-time multi-agent AI systems with Amazon ElastiCache
sessions.abstract: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.

sessions.title: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Amazon DocumentDB and its innovations
sessions.abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a serverless, fully managed, MongoDB API-compatible document database service. In this session, take a deep dive into the most exciting features Amazon DocumentDB offers including serverless, enhanced compression, performance upgrades, and the latest query APIs. Learn how the implementation of these features in your organization can improve resilience, performance, and the effectiveness of your applications.

sessions.title: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
sessions.abstract: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Walk away with a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.

sessions.title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
sessions.abstract: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

sessions.title: Adopt evolving Amazon DynamoDB resiliency design patterns
sessions.abstract: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. Learn how to use the global tables architecture with specific metrics and thresholds that drive effective failover decisions, as well as DR patterns that achieve low RTO and RPO without global tables overhead. Through whiteboard discussion, explore a variety of resilient DynamoDB workload solutions for specific use cases, including incremental export for undoing bad writes, which is faster and less disruptive than a full PITR table restore, approaches to protect against ransomware and data destruction, and cross-account table migration strategies.

sessions.title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
sessions.abstract: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using  Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications. Leave with practical patterns for production-grade agents.

sessions.title: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
sessions.abstract: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Leave with a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.

sessions.title: Deploy and manage blockchain nodes on AWS
sessions.abstract: Self-managing blockchain nodes at scale requires expertise in infrastructure sizing, storage optimization, chain synchronization, snapshot management, and patching, amid rapidly evolving protocols. In this session, explore a reference architecture for deploying self-managed nodes on AWS using Amazon EC2 and AWS Blockchain Node Runners, an open source initiative. The session includes a whiteboard walkthrough of a sample solution, diving deep into each component, addressing key challenges, and exploring AI-driven node deployment with Kiro and how to leverage AWS DevOps Agent for management. Leave equipped to deploy, manage, optimize for data transfer, and scale blockchain workloads on AWS.

sessions.title: Global transactions in Amazon Aurora DSQL
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for global scale. In this session, Marc Brooker, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, dives into the exact algorithms Aurora DSQL uses to achieve faster-than-light consistent reads, strong isolation, durability, and atomicity across regions. The session covers the specific tradeoffs each algorithm makes and what those tradeoffs mean in practice.

sessions.title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

sessions.title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
sessions.abstract: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.

sessions.title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
sessions.abstract: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.

sessions.title: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
sessions.abstract: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. AWS gives you a unified set of tools to plan, build, test, and deploy code—with safety woven into every stage. In this session, learn how to assemble end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using infrastructure as code, then layer in safe-deployment strategies—canary and linear traffic shifting, automated CloudWatch alarm gates, and one-click stage rollbacks—so you can release with confidence and recover in seconds when something goes wrong.

sessions.title: AWS infrastructure as code: A year in review
sessions.abstract: Your infrastructure code deserves the same developer experience as your application code. This session recaps what's new for AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK: early change-set validation, the CloudFormation Language Server for your IDE, Stack Refactoring without downtime, drift-aware change sets, CDK Mixins for composable abstractions, cross-account output references, and the CDK Toolkit Library. See how these capabilities shorten your dev-test cycle and strengthen deployment safety.

sessions.title: Beyond the pilot: How customers scaled Kiro and proved the value
sessions.abstract: Adopting a coding agent is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one. In this panel, engineering leaders from companies that deployed Kiro at scale share what worked: rollout strategies that drove adoption, training approaches that met developers where they were, governance guardrails that satisfied security teams, and the metrics they use to measure productivity impact. Bring your questions—this is an open conversation about the patterns, pitfalls, and payoffs of making AI-assisted development the default across an engineering organization.

sessions.title: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.

sessions.title: Learn new AI development skills with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Discover Kiro, the IDE for structured agentic development. In this builder’s session, explore how to use Kiro as your intelligent partner - helping to understand complex codebases, crystalize detailed requirements, and deliver quality solutions at unprecedented speed. You will iterate with Kiro to finalize your detailed design, before using Kiro to orchestrate AI agents and implement a fully working solution – all while maintaining complete control throughout the development process. You must bring a laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
sessions.abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
sessions.abstract: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

sessions.title: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Deploy without drama: Safe, automated releases on AWS
sessions.abstract: Releasing software shouldn't mean holding your breath. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and AppConfig help you automate safe, hands-off deployments to Amazon EC2, ECS, and Lambda across accounts and Regions. Learn to apply canary and linear traffic-shifting strategies, wire CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback, and use stage-level conditions to gate promotions on integration tests. Whether you're deploying a single service or orchestrating hundreds, leave with patterns for zero-downtime releases you can trust.

sessions.title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
sessions.abstract: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Security Agent, ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.

sessions.title: Ship faster with AWS CloudFormation
sessions.abstract: AWS CloudFormation lets you manage infrastructure as code with increasing confidence and speed. In this chalk talk, we dive into the capabilities that shorten your dev-test cycle and keep deployments safe: catch errors early with change-set validation, author templates faster using the CloudFormation Language Server in your IDE, reorganize stacks without disruption using Stack Refactoring, and prevent accidental overwrites with drift-aware change sets. Bring your templates and your toughest questions—we'll workshop solutions live.

sessions.title: Death, taxes, and runtime deprecations: automate your way out
sessions.abstract: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
sessions.abstract: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

sessions.title: Deploy your applications with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, build and deploy applications using infrastructure as code with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). Create resources using familiar programming languages, apply CDK Mixins to compose reusable behaviors across constructs, and safely reorganize stacks with CDK Refactor. Learn maintenance and operations tips including cross-account output references and programmatic deployments with the CDK Toolkit Library. Get an introduction to building your own constructs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Deploy infrastructure with speed and safety using AWS CloudFormation
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, build and test AWS CloudFormation templates hands-on. Create stacks to deploy and manage resources, then use the CloudFormation Language Server to author with real-time validation in your IDE. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build real-time applications with AWS Amplify
sessions.abstract: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Beyond the IDE: autonomous development with Kiro web and mobile
sessions.abstract: Kiro web and mobile bring agentic development to your browser—every session in an isolated cloud sandbox, no local setup, accessible anywhere you have an internet connection. In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: What's new in full-stack AWS app development
sessions.abstract: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.

sessions.title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
sessions.abstract: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.

sessions.title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
sessions.abstract: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.

sessions.title: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
sessions.abstract: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.

sessions.title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
sessions.abstract: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

sessions.title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
sessions.abstract: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.

sessions.title: How startups ship faster with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Startups live and die by velocity. Small teams, big ambitions, and no time to waste. In this session, hear how fast-moving startups are using Kiro to punch above their weight: turning ideas into working software with spec-driven and agentic development, keeping a lean team focused on product instead of boilerplate, and shipping features that would normally demand far more engineers. We'll describe real patterns startups use to move from concept to production quickly, and share practical takeaways any team can apply. Whether you're a founder, an early engineer, or scaling quickly, learn how agentic development helps small teams build big.

sessions.title: From monolith to the long tail: modernize it all with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Modernization has two faces. There's the big one: the 25-year-old Java or .NET monolith you've been meaning to move off. And, the long tail: hundreds of small apps quietly racking up end-of-life notices for deprecated runtimes, frameworks, and dependencies. This session covers both. See how Transform custom tackles large, complex modernizations—decomposing monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at up to 4x speed. Then see the new continuous modernization capability autonomously scan thousands of repositories against your baselines, prioritize what's drifting, and open remediation pull requests on a schedule. Stop firefighting deprecation emails and start keeping your whole portfolio current.

sessions.title: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
sessions.abstract: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

sessions.title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
sessions.abstract: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

sessions.title: Full stack development on AWS: bring your questions
sessions.abstract: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. This chalk talk is an open Q&A, so bring your real questions and challenges. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.

sessions.title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
sessions.abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

sessions.title: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
sessions.abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning  is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint -  all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

sessions.title: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
sessions.abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.

sessions.title: Make the agent code while you sleep
sessions.abstract: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
sessions.abstract: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
sessions.abstract: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

sessions.title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
sessions.abstract: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

sessions.title: Cloud Migration Journey Tabletop Experience
sessions.abstract: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture.

sessions.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Tabletop Experience
sessions.abstract: Quantum computing is advancing—is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence. Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

sessions.title: 3rd Party Risk Management Tabletop Experience
sessions.abstract: Embark on "Third Party Risk Management," an engaging tabletop designed to challenge and refine your approach to managing external partnerships and vendor relationships. In this immersive experience, leaders are thrust into a high-stakes environment where they must navigate complex scenarios involving third-party risks. This tabletop not only enhances your ability to manage third-party risks effectively but also equips you with practical insights and strategies to safeguard your organization’s interests and strengthen its external partnerships. Join us to elevate your risk management acumen and drive resilient, forward-thinking approaches in an interconnected business landscape.

sessions.title: Agentic AI Governance Tabletop Experience
sessions.abstract: Navigate AI-driven security threats as they escalate in real time. In this immersive executive tabletop, participants allocate a constrained governance budget, then respond to live crisis events scored across six dimensions. Practice navigating high-stakes scenarios including autonomous AI deployment failures, third-party security incidents, and emerging regulatory obligations. Confront real attack techniques, compliance frameworks, and enterprise liability exposure while aligning cross-functional teams under pressure. This experience sharpens governance instincts and crisis fluency—equipping leaders to govern Agentic AI risks, enforce accountability, and make decisive resource allocation calls before a real crisis demands it.

sessions.title: Incident Response Ransomware Tabletop Experience
sessions.abstract: Experience a fast-moving ransomware crisis in this immersive executive tabletop. Navigate a high-stakes scenario where an acquisition of a competitor with poor cyber hygiene triggers a cascading attack. Decide how to contain threats, manage regulatory disclosure timelines, and protect stakeholder trust. Align cross-functional teams—CISO, Legal, CRO, and CEO—while balancing response speed with communication. Confront challenges including vendor lock-in, AI-based detection failures, and global compliance risks like SEC cyber disclosure and GDPR breach notices. Leave with stronger instincts around containment, incident escalation, stakeholder coordination, and business continuity.

sessions.title: AWS AI League: Build agents with AgentCore (Agentic Football)
sessions.abstract: Coordinating agents is where multi agent systems break. They duplicate work, drop handoffs, and burn tokens. In this workshop, build and deploy five autonomous agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Kiro and the Strands Agents SDK, then field them five versus five in live Agentic Football matches. Write the tools your agents call, orchestrate multi turn reasoning across a maze like arena, and solve coordination problems that decide the match. Tune prompts, roles, and tactics between rounds and watch your score climb a live leaderboard. Leave with working code, production ready multi agent patterns, and a shot at the Finale.

sessions.title: AWS AI League Championship Grand Finale: Agentic Football Cup
sessions.abstract:
Experience the ultimate AI showdown from your theater seat as fifty finalists from the AWS AI League season battle head-to-head in real time for the $50,000 championship prize.

This electrifying viewing experience offers ML practitioners, developers, and AI enthusiasts unique insights into agent orchestration, model customization, and multi-agent coordination at scale, as five-versus-five AI agent squads face off live in Agentic Football, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK.

sessions.title: AWS GameDay - Agentic AI & AI Application Monitoring ft. New Relic
sessions.abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative learning exercise to build practical skills in deploying and monitoring AI-powered applications on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll engineer production-ready AI systems and ensure reliability through comprehensive observability. Leverage Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock Agentcore, foundation models, AI agents, prompt engineering, model evaluation, and ML pipeline monitoring as you build and operate AI workloads end-to-end. Face challenges demanding both engineering excellence and operational awareness for AI systems in production! Whether you're an experienced ML engineer or just starting to build with AI, this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with New Relic. Walk-ups welcome.

Face challenges that simulate real-world disasters where every second of downtime counts! Whether you're a seasoned systems architect or new to disaster recovery, this GameDay will put your resilience skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with Clumio by Commvault. Walk-ups welcome.

Build skills in containerization, container orchestration platforms, service mesh, platform APIs, and self-service infrastructure as you construct golden paths that empower development teams. Face scenarios that challenge your ability to balance developer experience with operational governance! sessions.abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative exercise to develop practical skills in application security on AWS. You and your AI-powered security agent are the only things standing between your application and compromise! Whether you're a security engineer, DevOps practitioner, developer, or cloud architect, security is your responsibility, and this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Face off against real-world attack scenarios with multi-stage threat patterns that will test your ability to detect and respond under pressure! Whether you are a seasoned security analyst or just exploring cybersecurity, this GameDay will sharpen your skills. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. sessions.title: AWS AI League: Train with RLVR on SageMaker, deploy in AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Turn a generic model into one that wins on your task, and prove it with data. In this hands-on workshop, you customize a foundation model on Amazon SageMaker AI using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), with no infrastructure to manage. Then you build an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates the model end to end: preparing datasets, triggering training, registering models, evaluating with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploying to a real-time endpoint. Your score posts to a live leaderboard, and you tune between rounds to climb it. You walk away knowing when customization beats a strong prompt.

sessions.title: AWS AI League: Build domain specific AI with Forge
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop you’ll compete head-to-head with other builders to build your own domain specific AI. You’ll tackle real-world challenges as you generate synthetic datasets, experiment with model customization, and fine-tune models to improve accuracy, clarity, and relevance. You’ll learn just how accessible and cost-effective AI customization can be. Whether you’re chasing the championship or simply sharpening your AI expertise, this session delivers practical techniques you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate

sessions.title: AWS wherever you need it: From the cloud to the edge
sessions.abstract: While most workloads can be migrated to the cloud, some remain on-premises or at the edge due to low latency, local data processing, or data residency needs. AWS services like AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories extend AWS infrastructure, services, APIs, and tools wherever you need them, from metro areas to on-premises data centers and the far edge. Explore how these infrastructure services power a broad range of hybrid cloud and edge computing use cases such as financial trading, real-time threat detection, robotic control, and local processing of personally identifiable information (PII). Learn how AWS can help you meet digital sovereignty needs, run generative AI applications with on-premises and edge data, and accelerate migration and modernization with on-premises dependencies.

sessions.title: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
sessions.abstract: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.

sessions.title: AI workloads from cloud to edge: Choosing the right hybrid deployment
sessions.abstract: Organizations are running AI workloads, including training, inference, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, across an expanding set of environments, from AWS Regions to AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. Explore how customers deploy GPU-accelerated AI across the full hybrid spectrum: G7e instances for edge inference, NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances on Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time applications like robotics. Hear how customers navigate these decisions and learn architectural patterns for placing AI workloads where your data lives, without compromising performance or compliance.

sessions.title: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
