In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for manufacturing: Build a cross-domain digital thread
sessions.abstract: Manufacturing data lives in silos — from engineering systems through production lines. In this workshop, build an agentic digital thread: a knowledge-graph-powered AI system that unifies OT and IT data across the product lifecycle and answers cross-domain questions in real time. Using Amazon Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS IoT SiteWise, deploy agents that autonomously traverse connections from product design through production operations — linking engineering changes to equipment assets to quality events — without point-to-point integrations. Leave with a deployable reference architecture adaptable to any manufacturing environment.

sessions.title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
sessions.abstract: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.

sessions.title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
sessions.abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

sessions.title: Build low latency real-time bidding workloads with AWS RTB Fabric
sessions.abstract: With the growth of digital media, including streaming video and retail media, customers that operate advertising platforms need to buy, sell, deliver, and measure millions of ad transactions per second while meeting stringent latency requirements. In this chalk talk, you will learn how to run real-time bidding workloads with your AdTech partners on a dedicated network in the cloud using AWS RTB Fabric. You will learn how to setup, onboard, and integrate AWS RTB Fabric with your supply and demand-side-platforms. Additionally, you will learn about key features including the core network, modules, and pricing model of the service.

sessions.title: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen
sessions.abstract: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production. Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. We design a supervisor agent coordinating specialists across drive-thru, kitchen prep, inventory, and labor scheduling. Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

sessions.title: Designing the AWS Secure Research Environment: Architecture Deep Dive
sessions.abstract: The AWS Secure Research Environment provides a turnkey platform for universities to deploy NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 compliant infrastructure in weeks. This session goes behind the solution's architecture: Landing Zone Accelerator customization, multi-account strategy with Service Catalog vended accounts, preventive SCPs versus detective controls, Network Firewall egress patterns for GovCloud, and automated evidence collection feeding Security Hub. I'll walk through design decisions, what we got wrong, how we iterated, and the open-source CloudFormation templates now available on GitHub for community use.

sessions.title: Build mission-ready software in regulated industries faster with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Federal dev teams struggle to ship fast while meeting compliance requirements. In this workshop, build a real app using Kiro's agentic IDE. Automate testing and docs with hooks, enforce AI behavior with steering rules, and extend capabilities through powers. Ideal for federal devs and architects.

sessions.title: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, learn to build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream and simulate auction scenarios using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. Construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions following the ARTF specification. Orchestrate multi-agent pipelines to simulate adversarial auction environments, test bidding strategies, and evaluate outcomes that feed back into model improvement. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and gain hands-on experience applying your own bidding models—plus a practical understanding of how bidstream agents and agentic workflows connect end to end.

sessions.title: Build a brand knowledge graph for retail and CPG AI
sessions.abstract: Retail and CPG brands invest years building product expertise, from visual styling rules to ingredient pairing and formulation knowledge, that generic AI simply cannot replicate. In this builder session, you'll construct a Graph RAG solution that encodes brand-specific curatorial knowledge into an Amazon Neptune Analytics knowledge graph with multimodal vector embeddings. Using a CPG product catalog, you'll build graph schemas capturing formulation relationships, brand hierarchies, and cross-category pairing rules. Then see how vector similarity search combined with graph traversal enriches retrieval context before grounding Amazon Bedrock LLM responses. Leave with a working deployed architecture adaptable across retail and CPG.

sessions.title: 10 Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
sessions.abstract: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. In this hands-on session, we walk through 10 practical techniques for building cost-optimized video understanding pipelines on AWS. You'll learn how to reduce inference costs, right-size your architecture, and accelerate time to value without sacrificing accuracy. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable. Leave with actionable blueprints you can implement immediately.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for Mission Readiness: Accelerating Federal Operations
sessions.abstract: A federal agency achieved 3x faster document analysis using Agentic AI with autonomous reasoning. This chalk talk explores how AI agents orchestrate mission-critical tasks in high-side environments while meeting IL4/IL5 compliance and zero-trust requirements.

sessions.title: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
sessions.abstract: AI bots now drive more than half of web traffic, consuming content built for human eyes while sending little value back to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both sides of the agent-first internet. First, you'll build a pipeline that transforms any media — images, video, audio — into concise, agent-friendly Markdown summaries using media contextual analysis, interpreting objects, scenes, speech, and meaning while preserving the original for humans. Then you'll monetize that traffic with AWS WAF's new AI traffic monetization capability, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. Leave with a reusable dual-audience, dual-revenue architecture.

sessions.title: Build Agentic Video Streaming Observability Using Kiro and Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Media operations teams struggle to correlate issues across complex live streaming pipelines, In this hands-on session, build an agentic video observability and analytics application using Kiro and Amazon Bedrock that monitors the entire live streaming chain AWS Elemental MediaConnect, MediaLive, MediaPackage, MediaTailor and Amazon CloudFront. Deploy AI agents using Strands Agents SDK and MCP servers to ingest, visualize, and investigate end-to-end QoE/QoS analytics across three layers: origin health, CDN performance, and client-side CMCD telemetry. Leave with a unified dashboard and natural language interface for streaming quality investigation across every pipeline stage.

sessions.title: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
sessions.abstract: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts — true, misleading, or false — each cited to its source at broadcast-compatible latency. We'll unpack the moving parts: a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Bring your own use case and leave with a mapped path from it to the reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.

sessions.title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
sessions.abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

sessions.title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
sessions.abstract: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.

sessions.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
sessions.abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

sessions.title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
sessions.abstract: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

sessions.title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
sessions.abstract: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

sessions.title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
sessions.abstract: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

sessions.title: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production
sessions.abstract: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. Of course, this requires modeling your problem in first-order logic, which demands careful thinking to precisely capture all behaviors of your system. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.

sessions.title: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
sessions.abstract: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rules—financial, legal, regulatory—yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logic—capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.

sessions.title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
sessions.abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

sessions.title: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
sessions.abstract: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.

sessions.title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
sessions.abstract: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose built AI chips to deliver better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference, and leave equipped to write custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

sessions.title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
sessions.abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

sessions.title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
sessions.abstract: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

sessions.title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
sessions.abstract: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

sessions.title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
sessions.abstract: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

sessions.title: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
sessions.abstract: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.

sessions.title: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
sessions.abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.

sessions.title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
sessions.abstract: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

sessions.title: Safer, Better, Agents with Policy
sessions.abstract: In this talk we'll look at how we're applying mathematical logic, especially metric first-order temporal logic, and a powerful technique called autoformalization, to build a firm foundation for safe and reliable AI agents. Don't worry, we'll explain the math and buzzwords, and help you understand the cutting edge of safety and policy for AI agents.

sessions.title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
sessions.abstract: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

sessions.title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
sessions.abstract: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

sessions.title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
sessions.abstract: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

sessions.title: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
sessions.abstract: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.

sessions.title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
sessions.abstract: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

sessions.title: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
sessions.abstract: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.

sessions.title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
sessions.abstract: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

sessions.title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
sessions.abstract: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

sessions.title: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
sessions.abstract: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.

sessions.title: How IT leaders actually pulled off their cloud migrations
sessions.abstract: How did other organizations get their on-premises environments to AWS? In this panel, migration leaders from global organizations share exactly how they did it, including those moving off VMware and other aging infrastructure. You'll hear the real planning decisions, execution strategies, and lessons learned that made their transitions successful. They'll also share where they're headed next with modernization and innovation. Whether you're just getting started or pushing past roadblocks, you'll leave with proven strategies and practical insights to accelerate your own cloud migration.

sessions.title: How Deutsche Bahn made 10 years of cloud modernization pay off in AI
sessions.abstract: You've invested in cloud. Maybe migrated. Maybe modernized. Your board wants AI yesterday, but 88% of companies use AI and only 1% believe they're at maturity. The gap isn't infrastructure. It's whether your organization can move fast enough. In this fireside chat, an AWS executive-in-residence sits down with Deutsche Bahn leadership to unpack how they built that speed: 550+ autonomous teams, AWS migration completed 18 months early, and enterprise-scale agentic AI now in production. You'll leave with: (1) what "AI-ready" requires beyond cloud, (2) a governance model for agents at scale, and (3) a framework for pilot to all-in.

sessions.title: Booking.com's playbook for cloud transformation at global scale
sessions.abstract: Booking.com connects millions of travelers to over 28 million listings across 43 languages. Their cloud transformation had to match that scale. In this session, hear how Booking.com dissolved organizational silos, broke through bottlenecks, and compressed timelines to fundamentally change how they build, operate, and innovate. You'll learn the architectural decisions, migration frameworks, and repeatable patterns that scaled cloud adoption across the enterprise, and how embedding AI from the ground up now powers next-generation customer experiences. Leave with a playbook for turning cloud transformation into continuous, cloud-fluent competitive advantage.

sessions.title: Build your agentic transformation roadmap from portfolio analyses
sessions.abstract: You've decided to pursue agentic AI for modernization, but with hundreds of applications at different maturity levels, knowing where to start is the real challenge. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through a framework for designing a transformation strategy using data-driven findings from AWS Transform's readiness and modernization analyses. We'll dig into how to interpret portfolio-level scores, prioritize applications, sequence work based on business value and technical debt, and build a phased roadmap that connects readiness gaps to concrete actions. Bring your questions and your portfolio challenges.

sessions.title: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
sessions.abstract: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

sessions.title: End-to-end agentic modernization with United Airlines & Bank Hapoalim
sessions.abstract: Legacy applications hosted across mainframe, midrange, and distributed platforms that have resisted previous modernization attempts now have a path that blends determinism and agentic AI to deliver both accuracy and speed. See how United Airlines transformed crew operations while maintaining FAA compliance, and how Bank Hapoalim delivered its mortgage module to production from a 202-million-line estate under a board-mandated deadline while reducing operational risk. Walk through the end-to-end experience, from automated discovery and business-rule extraction with AWS Transform, through forward-engineering microservices with Kiro, to production deployment. Leave with a playbook for modernizing the applications everyone said not to touch.

sessions.title: Using AI to scale legacy app modernization with Experian & Itau
sessions.abstract: A successful modernization approach only matters if it scales beyond the first pilot. Experian and Itaú share how they grew their approach with AWS Transform and Kiro from a single engagement into an enterprise-wide operating model. Experian compresses mainframe analysis from months to days, then standardizes modernization across 550+ workloads and multiple regions with a fully agentic reverse-engineering pipeline. Itaú expanded to 43 business domains, processing nearly 140 million lines of code in a single month. Leave with the operating models that scale modernization from one application to the entire portfolio, unlocking AI-driven capabilities along the way.

sessions.title: Building migration readiness when the timeline is tight
sessions.abstract: Most organizations don't get years to plan a large-scale migration. Licensing changes, compliance requirements, or rising hardware costs can compress your timeline fast. This session covers how to build readiness quickly so your team can move hundreds of workloads with confidence. Learn how to assess your environment, build team capability, and match the right migration pathway to each workload. Hear from a customer who moved hundreds of applications under real pressure with zero critical outages. Walk away with a practical framework for getting your organization ready to move at any speed.

sessions.title: Strategies for optimizing enterprise licenses on AWS
sessions.abstract: Enterprise organizations running commercial software on AWS face licensing decisions that directly impact cost and compliance. This session explores strategies for optimizing Microsoft and other enterprise software licenses across AWS services including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. An AWS licensing expert walks through assessment approaches and optimization levers. Then hear from a customer who ran an AWS Optimization and Licensing Assessment across three workstreams: rightsizing, Availability Zone consolidation, and database modernization, and turned a one-time assessment into an ongoing optimization practice. You'll leave with strategies you can apply to your own licensing environment.

sessions.title: On-premises to AWS readiness: foundational decisions before your migration
sessions.abstract: Successful migrations are shaped by decisions made well before the first workload moves. This session explores how choices in licensing, operating models, technology architecture, and organizational readiness influence migration outcomes, whether moving off VMware, aging infrastructure, or other on-premises environments. Learn how to assess dependencies and business constraints, align stakeholders, and build a plan that avoids common pitfalls and adapts as your environment evolves.

sessions.title: How to assess your environment to migrate & modernize with confidence
sessions.abstract: Without a clear picture of what's running in your environment, teams carry forward outdated assumptions, inherit unplanned tech debt, and miss the fastest path to value. Assessment is the foundational step that sets everything else up for success. Learn how to go hands-on with AWS Transform, an agentic assessment experience that delivers results fast, or work with AWS specialists and partners who leverage this technology alongside decades of migration experience. Use assessment data to make informed decisions, optimize environments, and eliminate redundant licensing.

sessions.title: Skip Refactoring and Simplify Operations with Nutanix on AWS
sessions.abstract: Cloud migrations often stall when rewriting applications takes too long. As projects drag on, organizations are left managing a fragmented, expensive mix of on-premises and cloud silos. Nutanix Cloud Clusters on AWS addresses this friction by establishing a single control plane and a consistent operating model across environments. In this session, learn how to move workloads to AWS bare metal quickly without refactoring. Discover how to eliminate management silos, accelerate migration timelines, and simplify hybrid cloud operations.

sessions.title: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS
sessions.abstract: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows.

sessions.title: From SAP to Agentic AI: Building a unified data strategy on AWS
sessions.abstract: This chalk talk presents a unified architecture spanning SAP Business Data Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services. Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. We introduce the AWS for SAP MCP Server, accessing OData services as AI-ready tools via Model Context Protocol. Live demos showcase AI agents resolving supply chain exceptions, generating Customer 360 insights, and accelerating BW modernization.

sessions.title: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
sessions.abstract: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

sessions.title: Build a data-driven migration plan with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: You're planning a data center exit and need leadership to say yes. That means persuasive data, realistic cost estimates, and a proposal that makes financial sense. In this builders' session, you'll use AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities paired with Discovery Agent data to assess your existing environment, generate cost estimates, and build a compelling business case for migration. You'll work through the end-to-end workflow from discovery and analysis to financial modeling, and leave ready to present a data-driven migration proposal to your stakeholders.

sessions.title: The EBA cloud party: compete to build agentic migration solutions
sessions.abstract: The cloud journey isn't just about migration anymore. It's about building intelligent frameworks that transform how organizations operate. In this gamified Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) workshop, cross-functional teams compete in real time to architect migration and modernization solutions, build agentic AI workflows that automate at scale, and deploy AI-powered applications on AWS. Push boundaries, solve real challenges together, and have fun doing it. Walk away with battle-tested architectures, agentic automation patterns, and a cloud-fluent mindset your team can adopt immediately. Ready to play?

sessions.title: Drive multi-server migrations from discovery to cutover with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Migrating VMware or other on-premises environments to AWS involves dozens of coordinated steps, and most teams spend more time planning handoffs than actually moving workloads. In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience executing a real multi-server migration end to end using agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Modernize legacy batch into real-time with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.abstract: Batch processing has powered critical enterprise workloads for decades, from mainframes running COBOL and PL/I to distributed systems on legacy Java. The trade-off? Overnight batch cycles that business processes can no longer afford. In this session, reimagine batch as event-driven microservices using Domain-Driven Design. AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Your ETL pipelines built on SSIS, Airflow, or custom bash and SQL scripts work, but undocumented dependencies make them nearly impossible to migrate. In this builders' session, you'll use AWS Transform custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. You'll choose from multiple source modules (SSIS packages, Airflow DAGs, or bash/SQL scripts) and work hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized serverless pipeline.

sessions.title: AWS fundamentals for the accidental SQL Server database administrator
sessions.abstract: You became a DBA, and now someone's asking you to be a cloud architect too. With over 240 AWS services, knowing where to start is half the battle. In this chalk talk, we'll map your core DBA tasks to AWS equivalents, covering networking, security, high availability, and disaster recovery for SQL Server. We'll also explore how AI-powered tools like Kiro and AWS Transform can accelerate your ramp-up, from intelligent code generation to modernizing .NET and SQL Server workloads. You'll leave with a clear path to choosing, securing, and cost-optimizing the right services. Come with questions.

sessions.title: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.

sessions.title: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

sessions.title: Your playbook: turn your scattered databases into AI-ready infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Business-critical data scattered across Oracle, SQL Server, and VMware or Nutanix-hosted databases is the number one blocker to deploying agentic AI at scale. In this lightning talk, you'll get a practical playbook for database migration to AWS: real licensing challenges, cost optimization strategies, and modernization pathways that accelerate the path to cloud-native databases using AWS Transform and agentic AI. You'll leave with a clear migration framework that turns fragmented data estates into AI-ready infrastructure, no matter where your databases live today.

sessions.title: Best path forward: Rehost & replatform to containers with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Not every app needs the same migration path, and figuring out which ones to rehost versus containerize is where teams get stuck. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to plan a combined migration and modernization across your application portfolio, then execute a mix of container and rehost migrations deploying to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll work through the full lifecycle. Learn how to order waves and coordinate cutover across a mixed portfolio. Leave with a realistic multi-wave plan you can apply to your own environment. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.abstract: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.title: How to decompose Oracle and SQL Server into purpose-built databases
sessions.abstract: A monolithic traditional RDBMS databases serves transactions, reporting, and search, but serves none of them well. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard how to decompose a proprietary database into purpose-built layers on AWS, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional workloads, Aurora pgvector for semantic search and GenAI (RAG), and Amazon Redshift via zero-ETL for real-time analytics, for a smarter modernization approach. We'll walk through how this pattern eliminates licensing costs, removes ETL pipelines, and turns your operational data into an AI-ready platform. Come ready to whiteboard your decomposition use case.

sessions.title: How British Airways used agentic AI to cut major Java costs by 48%
sessions.abstract: You have hundreds of services stuck on aging infrastructure, and your engineers are spending more time maintaining them than building new experiences. British Airways faced the same challenge with 500 Java services on EC2. Using AWS Transform custom, they built an agentic AI platform that autonomously migrates services to ECS Fargate on Graviton, cutting costs by 48% without touching business logic. They then extended it to improve test coverage and patch security vulnerabilities continuously. In this session, you'll learn how to move from proof-of-concept to a repeatable transformation engine and give your engineers their time back.

sessions.title: How LG U+ cut migration time 50% with AI-powered app refactoring
sessions.abstract: Moving servers to the cloud without modernizing the applications on them just moves your technical debt to a new address. LG U+ needed to modernize applications before they could migrate them, and doing both sequentially would have taken too long. In this session, LG U+ shares how they ran AI-powered modernization and migration in parallel across 87 systems spanning 1,579 virtual servers and 107 physical servers. The result: roughly 20% migration velocity improvement and a 50% reduction in Java migration time through AI-assisted refactoring. You'll learn how to modernize at scale without slowing down the move.

sessions.title: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
sessions.abstract: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their CISO shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) a security- and compliance-integrated dependency mapping approach, and (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.

sessions.title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
sessions.abstract: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.

sessions.title: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
sessions.abstract: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
sessions.abstract: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Transforming legacy core to agentic AI with Nissan & Bread Financial
sessions.abstract: Mainframe applications can't support agentic capabilities. Modernization builds the foundation that can. Discover how Nissan transformed rigid batch vehicle allocation into an AI-driven platform on Amazon Bedrock that responds to real-time demand across thousands of dealerships. Hear how Bread Financial decoupled tightly integrated credit domains into autonomous services, enabling AI agents for credit decisioning and offer personalization. See how both used AWS Transform to extract business rules from decade-old applications and Kiro to forward-engineer production code. Learn how modernized applications enable agentic capabilities that transform how the business competes with real-time insights and autonomous decisions.

sessions.title: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
sessions.abstract: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.

sessions.title: What to do next after your cloud migration
sessions.abstract: Rehosting gets workloads to AWS, but that's just the beginning. This session covers the first 90 days after cutover: stabilizing the environment, building observability so decisions are based on real utilization data instead of pre-migration assumptions, applying auto-scaling and right-sizing adjustments that accelerate ROI, and knowing when a workload is ready to modernize versus when to leave it alone. AWS specialists share the decisions and strategy to turn your freshly migrated environment into one worth the investment.

sessions.title: 5 steps to faster data center exits with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: 70% of applications still sit on-premises, and the longer they stay, the more tech debt compounds. AWS Transform uses agentic AI to compress the entire data center exit journey from assessment through execution. Start with AI-powered discovery that right-sizes thousands of servers, compares cost scenarios, and builds a business case that gets executive buy-in in days. Move into automated wave planning and landing zone deployment. Then see how network architectures convert into production-ready VPCs and workloads rehost to Amazon EC2 at scale. We follow one customer's real timeline from plan to exit and unpack what made it work.

sessions.title: Capital One's WorkSpaces Journey: 320 to 20,000 Desktops in 72hrs
sessions.abstract: Learn how to achieve enterprise-scale cloud desktop deployment from Capital One, who went from 320 manual provisions per day to 20,000 compliant desktops in 72 hours during a major merger integration. Gain production-tested architectural patterns for meeting compliance requirements without slowing delivery. You'll also get a first look at the latest WorkSpaces innovations and our vision for the future of cloud desktops, including how we're expanding what's possible for IT teams managing modern workloads at scale. This session is for those migrating from VDI, scaling an existing fleet, or planning for what's next.

sessions.title: Observability patterns for Microsoft workloads migrating to AWS
sessions.abstract: Migrating Microsoft workloads to AWS requires rethinking your monitoring strategy. Existing observability approaches may not translate seamlessly to the cloud, creating blind spots that lead to costly downtime and degraded end-user experiences. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how to strengthen your observability posture as you migrate .NET applications, SQL Server databases, and Windows services to AWS. We'll cover how to use AWS-native and open-source tooling to monitor workloads across VMs, containers, and serverless, giving you confidence to migrate faster while maintaining operational excellence. Bring your questions.

sessions.title: Architect and optimize your VMware environment on Amazon EVS
sessions.abstract: Dive deep into the architectural decisions that shape a resilient, high-performing VMware environment on Amazon EVS. Explore VCF 9 support, Windows Server license-included entitlements, networking designs, storage configurations tuned for performance and cost, and operational patterns for backup, patching, and disaster recovery. Hear from a customer running production workloads on EVS and leave with actionable architectures tailored to your VMware workloads.

sessions.title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
sessions.abstract: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

sessions.title: Build an AI agent that completes desktop tasks with WorkSpaces
sessions.abstract: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Unlocking SAP Data with AI: From Zero-ETL to Agentic Automation
sessions.abstract: Critical business data remains locked inside SAP ERP and BW systems, limiting real-time insights and AI-driven automation. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to break down data silos using a modern, cost-effective architecture without expensive ETL pipelines. Explore a unified analytics strategy spanning Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services that enables end-to-end SAP data modernization. Then, build with the AWS for SAP MCP Server, enabling agentic AI to orchestrate across SAP, Salesforce, and AWS without writing code.

sessions.title: Modernize SAP business processes with agentic AI on AWS
sessions.abstract: Enterprise processes span SAP for ERP, Salesforce for CRM, and ServiceNow for ITSM, connected by aging, brittle integrations that are slow to change. Agentic AI offers a better path: replacing point-to-point integrations with agents that reason across applications. In this workshop, you modernize an SAP-centric business process by orchestrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents over Model Context Protocol, including the AWS for SAP MCP Server. You implement cross-application use cases spanning finance, supply chain, and operations then leave with a deployable reference architecture for moving from custom integrations to agent-orchestrated workflows.

sessions.title: Build and test HA/DR architectures for Microsoft workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: Can your Windows Server apps, SQL Server databases, and Active Directory survive a system outage? In this builders' session, you'll find out by building and testing HA/DR architectures against simulated failures. Get hands-on with Elastic Disaster Recovery, Systems Manager, S3, AWS Managed Active Directory, and Elastic Beanstalk to construct resilient infrastructure, then measure RTO and RPO in real time as you break things on purpose. You'll leave with a validated resiliency blueprint and the confidence to protect your most critical Microsoft workloads.

sessions.title: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.

sessions.title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
sessions.abstract: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.

sessions.title: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Turn your cloud migration into a security transformation
sessions.abstract: Forward-looking organizations aren't just migrating to AWS. They're using migration as the catalyst to transform their entire security posture. In this workshop, you'll use sandbox accounts to configure centralized governance with AWS Organizations, enforce least-privilege access through IAM Identity Center, and stand up compliance monitoring with AWS Config and Security Hub. You'll do all of this as part of a live migration workflow, landing workloads with a security foundation built for machine-speed operations from day one. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Automate your landing zone and network migration with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Designing landing zones and translating on-premises networks into cloud-native architectures is complex and time-consuming. AWS Transform automates both. In this workshop, you'll see the landing zone agent analyze your requirements and deploy AWS Control Tower, organizational units, service control policies, and workload accounts as infrastructure as code. Then the network agent translates VMware networking components or firewall configurations into VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateways with hub-and-spoke or isolated topologies, ready for deployment in CDK or Terraform modules. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Break free from Oracle licensing and modernize to Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.abstract: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. You'll work through PL/SQL translation, dependency resolution, and validation using AWS Transform's agentic AI to collapse what typically takes weeks into hours of hands-on execution. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Best Practices for .NET modernization with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: As organizations look to reduce tech debt for their .NET applications, builders are looking to accelerate modernization with AI tools. In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop with Visual Studio and an AWS account onboarded to AWS Transform.

sessions.title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Security Agent for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.

sessions.title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
sessions.abstract: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

sessions.title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
sessions.abstract: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

sessions.title: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
sessions.abstract: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.

sessions.title: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress what typically takes months into a single sprint while targeting 30% cost reduction. Through hands-on modules, you'll containerize .NET applications, use AI-powered agents to reduce technical debt, adopt DevOps practices for .NET workloads, and execute end-to-end SQL Server migrations. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full .NET and SQL Server stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Laptop required.

sessions.title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
sessions.abstract: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then apply Amazon Bedrock–powered agents for proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. See how AWS DevOps Agent extends this with autonomous remediation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days.

sessions.title: Create reusable transformation rules for Java modernization at scale
sessions.abstract: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Your network, your rules: Global routing policies with AWS Cloud WAN
sessions.abstract: As global networks scale, they demand deterministic traffic paths—not best-effort routing. In this workshop, gain granular control over traffic flows between Regions, VPCs, and on-premises locations using AWS Cloud WAN routing policies across a multi-Region network. Through hands-on labs, configure route filtering to control reachability, summarize prefixes to reduce routing table complexity, and influence preferred paths with BGP attributes. Leave with practical skills to design scalable, policy-driven connectivity architectures. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
sessions.abstract: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers—and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.

sessions.title: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice
sessions.abstract: Organizations scaling across multiple AWS accounts need AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC, driving up costs and fragmenting access controls. In this session, construct a centralized endpoint architecture in a shared services VPC and expose endpoints to consumers through Amazon VPC Lattice. Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management—eliminating Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

sessions.title: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
sessions.abstract: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services—AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN—but when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Leave with clear guidance and practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

sessions.title: Understand your network: practical network observability on AWS
sessions.abstract: You're collecting Amazon VPC Flow Logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics—but still can't answer "why can't this instance reach the internet?" In this chalk talk, explore practical approaches to network observability on AWS, no deep expertise required. Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. Bring your monitoring questions—we'll discuss real scenarios and help you build observability that works for your team.

sessions.title: More than a heartbeat: Designing health checks that matter
sessions.abstract: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing - not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 - covering how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures - diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard - and we'll design your health strategy together.
