Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

sessions.title: Designing your AWS network for scale: From one VPC to many
sessions.abstract: You started with a single Amazon VPC - and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? Bring your architecture challenges - we'll draw through solutions together on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Private AI agent egress: VPC Lattice meets AgentCore Gateway
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents need to call private MCP servers, internal REST APIs, and OAuth providers — but those backends must never touch the public internet. In this lightning talk, we demo how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway uses managed Amazon VPC Lattice endpoints to route agent traffic privately into your VPC. We'll configure a private MCP server target, show traffic staying on the AWS backbone, and cover key patterns including intermediate domain routing, private certificate workarounds with ALB, and cross-account connectivity. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for secure, zero-public-internet agentic workloads.

sessions.title: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
sessions.abstract: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface — many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and an on-premises router, provision a virtual interface via the CLI and watch BGP establish in real time — then break things on purpose. See how route advertisements propagate, what ECMP and AS path prepending look like from both sides, and how BGP Route Visibility metrics in Amazon CloudWatch diagnose issues as they happen. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, walk away thinking differently about operating Direct Connect.

sessions.title: I didn't know AWS WAF did this
sessions.abstract: Think AWS WAF is just for blocking SQL injection and XSS? Think again. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into creative, real-world use cases - from deploying honeypots and shedding traffic, to stopping account fraud and mitigating DDoS at scale. We'll explore advanced configurations, walk through customer-tested patterns, and whiteboard strategies that make WAF a powerful tool in your security arsenal. Bring your questions and experiences - we're here to break the "WAF does that?" moments together.

sessions.title: Advanced VPC design and new capabilities
sessions.abstract: Amazon VPC is a foundational service on AWS, giving you control over your virtual networking environment. Every year, AWS makes updates to Amazon VPC to help improve functionality, security, and usability. In this session, learn about the latest updates to Amazon VPC and how you can use them to enhance your current architectures.

sessions.title: Enforce encryption in transit using Amazon VPC Encryption Controls
sessions.abstract: Regulated workloads demand encryption in transit, but verifying coverage across VPCs, instances, and endpoints is manual and error-prone. In this session, audit and enforce encryption in transit for Amazon VPC traffic using VPC Encryption Controls. Learn how to enable Monitor Mode to assess current encryption posture, migrate to Nitro instances, activate AWS Transit Gateway encryption for cross-VPC traffic, and switch to Enforce Mode. Analyze encryption status across Amazon EC2, NLB, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon S3 endpoint flows with Amazon VPC Flow Logs. Leave with hands-on experience enforcing encryption for HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP compliance.

sessions.title: Your IPs, your rules: Dynamic edge routing without NAT for AWS BYOIP
sessions.abstract: Some workloads need the public IP the world sees to live directly on the Amazon EC2 instances—no translation in the path. Email gateways rotating sender IPs, VPN concentrators assigning a dedicated address per client, or security appliances terminating traffic on the exact advertised address need the instance to own those public IPs. In this live-coding talk, we build that model end-to-end on AWS: writing CloudFormation for BYOIP pools and Bring Your Own ASN, coding NAT-free ingress routing so traffic arrives untranslated, and configuring BGP peering with Amazon VPC Route Server for high availability. Walk away with a reusable stack.

sessions.title: Bridging clouds: Building global multicloud and hybrid networks on AWS
sessions.abstract: It's no secret, enterprises today run workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers, but stitching together global connectivity without complexity remains a challenge. In this workshop, easily extend AWS connectivity to other clouds and on-premises environments using AWS Interconnect, AWS Direct Connect, and AWS Cloud WAN. Build a global multicloud network, then apply Amazon VPC Lattice to enforce security and handle overlapping IP address spaces without complex NAT configurations. Leave equipped to architect and deploy hybrid network architectures using modern application networking patterns. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Building a private service fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
sessions.abstract: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts - whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities - creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don't cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. Bidirectional sharing doubles the problem. In this session, build a private service fabric—a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

sessions.title: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
sessions.abstract: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone—but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.

sessions.title: Tenant isolation at scale: Network patterns for ISVs on AWS
sessions.abstract: As ISVs scale their SaaS platforms, network architecture becomes a critical decision: balancing tenant isolation, compliance, and operational efficiency. In this chalk talk, examine proven connectivity patterns using AWS PrivateLink, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon VPC Lattice for multi-tenant environments. Explore how to enforce strong tenant boundaries at the network layer, handle cross-account connectivity at scale, and reduce operational complexity as your business grows. Whether building a new multi-tenant platform or evolving an existing one, leave with actionable architecture blueprints ready for production.

sessions.title: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
sessions.abstract: Most enterprises don't run just one website — they run many: corporate sites, regional or sub-brand sites, internal portals, plus full environment tiers (Dev, QA, Staging, Prod) for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately creates configuration drift, inconsistent security posture, and operational overhead that scales with your site count. In this workshop, you'll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many website profiles — whether they represent different brands, business units, or environment tiers — while still allowing targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ. You'll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.

sessions.title: Origin management for multi-region applications with Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: In this session, you'll learn comprehensive origin management with Amazon CloudFront to build secure, resilient content delivery systems. We'll cover automatic failover mechanisms with CloudFront and Route 53, configure granular origin routing with CloudFront Functions, and secure origins using S3 with Origin Access Control (OAC) and VPC private origins for enhanced security. We'll explore integrating on-premises infrastructure through AWS Direct Connect for hybrid architectures, and deploy Origin Shield to further optimize cache performance and reduce origin load.

sessions.title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios - credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse - and we'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

sessions.title: Practical applications of edge compute in Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: Edge compute is a practical way to build faster, smarter applications. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll dive into how Amazon CloudFront empowers developers to run custom logic at the edge using CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge, and the Key Value Store. We’ll explore real-world use cases, architectural patterns, and recent feature launches that unlock powerful personalization, performance optimization, and cost efficiency. Come ready to whiteboard, ask questions, and discover how to push intelligence closer to your users.

sessions.title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it - From code to containment
sessions.abstract: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall — proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

sessions.title: Securing Amazon Bedrock agents with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
sessions.abstract: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement — not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC interface endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF and autonomously remediates threats, generating a plain-English incident summary.

sessions.title: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
sessions.abstract: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds - and origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.

sessions.title: What's new in Amazon Route 53: DNS innovations for 2026
sessions.abstract: Explore the latest innovations in Amazon Route 53, AWS's fully managed DNS service. This session covers 2026 launches including Route 53 Global Resolver for secure anycast DNS resolution from anywhere without VPNs, DNS Views sharing across accounts, and expanded DNS Firewall threat protection through partnerships. In this session, we also cover Profiles enhancements for simplified multi-VPC DNS management with granular IAM controls, and expanded domain registration support. Learn how these capabilities help you secure DNS resolution, simplify hybrid and multi-account architectures, and strengthen your DNS security posture at scale.

sessions.title: Network security architecture: Deployment patterns for firewalls
sessions.abstract: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. Join this chalk talk to discuss deployment patterns for AWS Network Firewall and Gateway Load Balancer with third-party firewalls for ingress and egress inspection.

sessions.title: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
sessions.abstract: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations—yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Elastic Load Balancing for modern workloads
sessions.abstract: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, GWLB transparent inspection architecture, and deployment patterns. Topics include performance optimization, troubleshooting methodologies, QUIC support, and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Walk away with practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance—whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS.

sessions.title: Connectivity strategies across AWS Partitions
sessions.abstract: Organizations increasingly operate across AWS commercial, GovCloud, Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions to satisfy regulatory, data residency, and national security requirements—but connecting them introduces networking challenges that go well beyond standard multi-Region design. In this session, learn cross-partition connectivity patterns using AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and application-layer proxies alongside DNS resolution strategies, compliance boundary enforcement, and operational trade-offs. We walk through architectural blueprints for securely linking partitions while preserving the isolation guarantees they exist to enforce, and share lessons learned from customers navigating ITAR, GDPR, and national sovereignty mandates at scale.

sessions.title: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

sessions.title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
sessions.abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, scale horizontally across availability zones, and enforce security controls with AWS WAF - including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

sessions.title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
sessions.abstract: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic - and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

sessions.title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
sessions.abstract: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers - AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Leave with battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

sessions.title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
sessions.abstract: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response - across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

sessions.title: Parse, verify, cut over: Accelerating CDN migrations to Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: CDN migrations rarely fail on feature gaps - they fail on semantics: cache keys that fragment silently, TTL precedence that behaves differently under load, and edge logic that resists one-to-one translation. In this session, dive deep into the engineering discipline behind large-scale migrations to Amazon CloudFront. Learn how AWS-built migration tooling converts third-party CDN configurations into CloudFront infrastructure as code and produces coverage reports that scope the work automation can't do. Then go beyond conversion into parity verification with traffic replay and cache hit ratio baselining, progressive DNS cutover with engineered rollback, and cache warming that protects day-one performance. Also learn how AWS Partners provide hands-on-keyboard migration support at scale.

sessions.title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
sessions.abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors - but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

sessions.title: Owning atoms to bits: How AWS accelerates network innovation at scale
sessions.abstract: At AWS, we design everything within our infrastructure networks—from buildings to fiber, routers to protocols. This atoms-to-bits ownership lets us move at breakneck speed: the moment we spot an opportunity to improve customer performance or resilience, we drive it into production. In this talk, Senior Principal Engineers cover how they applied this pattern to develop the random graph fabrics reshaping data center topologies and highly available systems for machine learning at planet scale. Learn what it takes to continually refresh, upgrade, and re-architect live infrastructure without ever interrupting a single customer workload.

sessions.title: Connect everything, everywhere: AWS global connectivity
sessions.abstract: Point solutions don't scale globally—and stitching together and managing dozens of them creates blind spots. In this session, discover what's new in AWS Cloud WAN and AWS Direct Connect: simplified hybrid connectivity, smarter segmentation, and real-time visibility across global traffic. See how AWS Cloud WAN's policy engine and AWS Direct Connect's latest capabilities combine to deliver seamless connectivity from anywhere to anywhere. Walk away with patterns to build a borderless, resilient global network.

sessions.title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
sessions.abstract: Your application works perfectly in the lab—but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

sessions.title: Managing and Monitoring AWS Direct Connect at Scale: Customer Lessons
sessions.abstract: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints — spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Leave with actionable strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.

sessions.title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
sessions.abstract: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.

sessions.title: Rewriting the AWS SDK for Python: Async from the ground up
sessions.abstract: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio hacks, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this talk is for you. We're rewriting the AWS SDK for Python with async built in from day one. We'll share the engineering challenges - why async-native is harder than "just add await" - and then show you the result: clean concurrent calls, bidirectional streaming with Bedrock and Transcribe, and a migration path that doesn't require rewriting your application overnight.

sessions.title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
sessions.abstract: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.

sessions.title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
sessions.abstract: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

sessions.title: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
sessions.abstract: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI Catalog to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.

sessions.title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
sessions.abstract: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.

sessions.title: Build multi-agent workflows with Strands Agents SDK on AWS
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build a multi-agent system using the Strands Agents open source SDK. You will create specialized agents with distinct roles, connect them via MCP for tool access, implement agent-to-agent delegation patterns, and add memory for stateful conversations. Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.

sessions.title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.

sessions.title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
sessions.abstract: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

sessions.title: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
sessions.abstract: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.

sessions.title: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
sessions.abstract:
"The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with autonomous relevance tuning and persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today.
OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents."

sessions.title: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
sessions.abstract: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.

sessions.title: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.

sessions.title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
sessions.abstract: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

sessions.title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
sessions.abstract: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

sessions.title: Performance tuning for streaming ingestion with Apache Iceberg
sessions.abstract: Unlock real-time streaming into Apache Iceberg with advanced performance tuning. Learn how to optimize ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink for fraud detection, IoT monitoring, and real-time analytics. This session covers throughput optimization through partitioning, parallelism, write distribution, batching, and checkpoint tuning. Discover techniques to reduce small file issues with compaction, minimize write amplification with deduplication, and maintain low-latency ingestion at scale, turning raw streaming data into actionable insights with efficiency and reliability.

sessions.title: Expedite model loading times in Kubernetes using kro & ACK
sessions.abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the Storage ? Network ? CPU ? PCIe ? GPU path. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines. We compare Mountpoint S3 CSI, EFS, FSx for Lustre, and SOCI for lazy-loading container images, showing how each accelerates data delivery to GPU memory. Combined with Kubernetes DRA for topology-aware GPU + storage placement, platform teams compose reusable inference stacks consumed with a single CR.

sessions.title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

sessions.title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
sessions.abstract: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

sessions.title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
sessions.abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This chalk talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll diagram context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

sessions.title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
sessions.abstract: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

sessions.title: Building Your AI Practice: From Business Model to Partner Revenue
sessions.abstract: Enterprises expect agentic outcomes. That changes how solutions are built and deployed. Traditional delivery practices are evolving to agentic delivery, outcome-based models, and scalable IP transacted through AWS Marketplace. Partners moving first are delivering measurable business outcomes faster and building new revenue alongside their customers. In this session, learn the three-stage practice-building path. See how Forward Deployed Engineering gives partners a new engagement architecture and faster delivery: pod-based, and time-boxed. See where AWS co-investment programs and AI-specific enrollment paths de-risk each stage of practice growth. Walk away with example GTM models and a concrete action plan.

sessions.title: Go-Live to ROI: How Partners Turn Customer Outcomes into Revenue
sessions.abstract: The partners thriving in the AI era aren't the ones who just deploy — they're the ones who prove impact. Since launching the Business Value Realization (BVR) motion at the AWS Partner Summit in New York in June, partners across every tier and geo are moving fast: documenting outcomes, unlocking milestone-based funding, and turning deployments into recurring revenue. Explore how consulting, managed services, and technology partners use the BVR framework to quantify ROI, earn the BVR Competency, strengthen C-suite relationships, and build customer success practices that generate net-new revenue beyond go-live.

sessions.title: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
sessions.abstract: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

sessions.title: Speed Wins: Compress Migration Timelines from Pipeline to Production
sessions.abstract: Enterprises face a wall of technical debt standing between them and the AI opportunity. In this session, learn how AWS Transform helps compressing the entire partner lifecycle — from intelligent prospecting and AI-powered co-sell through to automated delivery and simplified funding — and why first-movers will own disproportionate share of a the opportunity.

sessions.title: AI-Powered Profitability: How Partners Are Winning with AWS
sessions.abstract: AI is reshaping partner economics. Hear from AWS VP Julia Chen about how to build a profitable AI-first business. This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. You'll leave with insights about where to invest and pathways for growth.

sessions.title: Agentic Process Transformation at Enterprise Scale
sessions.abstract: Your customers don't need another automation tool, they need the leap forward they're actually looking for with AI. Agentic Process Transformation (APT) is the framework partners use to help customers move past isolated task automation and into enterprise-wide process reinvention: redesigning entire processes from the ground up to grow revenue and improve the bottom line at a scale automation alone can't reach. We'll share how to spot these transformation opportunities and the architectural patterns that turn them into production solutions. Leave with a concrete strategy for helping your customers make that leap today.

sessions.title: Agentic AI Meets the Line-of-Business Buyer
sessions.abstract: Budget authority is migrating from CIOs to line-of-business leaders - CFOs, Chief Medical Officers, Heads of Manufacturing - who buy outcomes, not infrastructure. At the same time, agentic AI is making it possible to automate entire business processes end-to-end, not just assist them. The partners who win are the ones who can connect these two shifts: framing autonomous agents as measurable business outcomes (revenue acceleration, cost compression, speed-to-market) in the language LOB leaders understand.

sessions.title: Scaling ISV Revenue: Accelerating Co-Sell with AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: AWS Marketplace has become the fastest path for ISVs to scale co-sell, but unlocking its full potential means going beyond procurement and using it as the backbone of how you sell. This session unpacks how high-performing ISVs combine ISV Accelerate with AWS Marketplace to accelerate co-sell. Three points separate top performers: (1) structuring AWS seller alignment to generate Marketplace-routed pipeline, (2) using private offers and channel-partner workflows to compress enterprise deal cycles by 30-40%, and (3) mining Marketplace buyer signals to drive expansion and proactive renewal. Walk away with a focused playbook for turning Marketplace into a scalable revenue motion.

sessions.title: Agentic-Led Modernization: First Movers' Winning Formula with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Continuous modernization isn't optional — it's the engine of speed and competitive advantage. In this session, hear what early-adopter AWS Partners discovered building on AWS Transform, how composability lets them embed their own IP while harnessing AWS's customer reach, funding, and brand, and where the roadmap

sessions.title: Delivering Measurable Customer Business Outcomes
sessions.abstract: AWS's Business Value Realization (BVR) motion helps AWS Partners deliver measurable customer outcomes after deployment, building long-term relationships anchored in proven impact. This session breaks down the end-to-end process of defining, quantifying, and tracking business outcomes — from building a compelling case for change to KPI measurement and change management that drives adoption. Learn the common pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact that resonates at the C-suite rather than just the project team. Leave with a repeatable approach ready to apply to your next engagement.

sessions.title: The Agentic MSP: How AI Compounds Customer Outcomes at Every Layer
sessions.abstract: The most profitable Managed Services Providers aren't just using AI internally. They're creating a compounding cycle: automate your own operations with Agentic AI, deliver measurably better outcomes to customers, then help those customers adopt AI themselves so the results multiply. This session shows how the AWS Managed Services Provider Program rewards that progression, from foundational automation through outcome-based delivery powered by AI agents. Leave with your own assessment and a concrete plan to reach the next level.

sessions.title: Multi-Tenant Agentic Platforms: A Scalable Reference Architecture
sessions.abstract: SaaS is going AI-native. ISVs must orchestrate third-party agents at scale. This session presents a multi-tenant architecture covering MCP, A2A, and AgentCore for orchestration, entitlement-based monetization, secure token exchange, agent lifecycle via Agent Registry, and cross-tenant observability.

sessions.title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
sessions.abstract: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for SAP: From Migration to Production with MCP, Kiro and Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Partners are turning SAP modernization from a years long crawl into an agent powered sprint. Using AWS built MCP servers and Kiro, they accelerate S/4HANA migrations, then keep those agents running in production on Bedrock AgentCore for issue triage, integration mapping, and master data governance. One story: migrate faster, operate smarter. You differentiate by layering your own IP, industry templates, and delivery methodology on top. Live demos. Architecture patterns. Lessons from partners already in production. Walk out with a blueprint for building agentic SAP solutions and the confidence that this partner opportunity is real, now.

sessions.title: Agentic Transformation Needs Evaluation: Agent Quality Framework for ISVs
sessions.abstract: ISVs shipping production agents at scale need to answer: is this good enough for customers? Agentic transformation doesn't end at build; quality evaluation is the missing layer. In this builders' session, you implement an open-source evaluation framework hands-on: define test criteria for your agent, run it in a sandbox on Bedrock, calibrate an automated judge against human labels, and track failure rates in CI. For multi-agent systems, attribute failures to the agent that caused them, not where they surfaced. Leave with a working Python CLI installed as your production quality gate.

sessions.title: Build Custom Transformation Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
sessions.abstract: Every organisation's modernization journey is unique — we whiteboard how to build, deploy, and share custom transformation agents using the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit — from orchestrator architectures and MCP patterns to one-command Bedrock AgentCore deployment. Bring your challenges.

sessions.title: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
sessions.abstract: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

sessions.title: From Manual to Autonomous: AI-Driven AWS Partner Ops with Quick & MCP
sessions.abstract: 38% of partners cite SA access as their #1 GenAI need; 42% cite technical complexity as the implementation barrier. Expertise locked in SMEs doesn't scale, the answer is architectural. This session shows how Amazon Quick, the Partner Central MCP Server, and Marketplace AI Listing Experience  automate end-to-end partner operations — co-sell, technical validation, MP listings optimized via SEO/GEO, Express Private Offers, and demand generation. We cover MCP protocol integration, agent orchestration across Partner Central and Marketplace, cross-system auth, and extensibility patterns. Leave ready to build your own MCP-based workflows automating specialist-knowledge access and pipeline at scale.

sessions.title: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
sessions.abstract: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants. But what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their team with consutling agents? In this code talk, learn how a team of consulting agents prompts a human consultant to conduct structured discovery asking the right questions, validate assumptions, build out business requirements, delivers agent designs and AWS architectures, calculates financial models with ROI, and exports a Statement of Work. All done in real-time, not weeks, whilst running a single workshop with your client.

sessions.title: From Intention to Production: Loop Engineering with the FDE Kit
sessions.abstract: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

sessions.title: Agentic AI Governance for Regulated Industries
sessions.abstract: As agentic AI expands into regulated industries, autonomous decisions must meet compliance before production. This session gives partners a governance framework spanning technical and non-technical requirements — not just architecture. We demo a working multi-agent system and share the code.

sessions.title: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
sessions.abstract: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

sessions.title: AWS Marketplace checkout, your website, your brand
sessions.abstract: When a buyer on your website is ready to purchase, AWS Marketplace gives them a procurement path their company has already approved. AWS Marketplace Storefront brings that path onto your own domain, so you keep your brand, your journey, and your sales team's visibility. In this chalk talk we'll build one live: catalog selection, buyer routing, embedding on your domain, and wiring requests into your CRM.

sessions.title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

sessions.title: Building a Zero Trust for Agentic AI Practice: A Partner Framework
sessions.abstract: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

sessions.title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
sessions.abstract: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

sessions.title: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

sessions.title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
sessions.abstract: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

sessions.title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
sessions.abstract: Organizations planning post-quantum migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the PQC Readiness Maturity Model: five levels from discovery to quantum-ready, each with measurable milestones. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

sessions.title: Track Cross-Domain Attack Vectors with AWS Security Hub Extended
sessions.abstract: In this 20-minute lightning talk, see how AWS Security Hub Extended correlates signals across endpoint, identity, email, data, browser, and AI domains into a single attack narrative. We show how cross-domain correlation surfaces attack vectors invisible to any single tool, and how customers deploy preconfigured detection patterns for immediate value.

sessions.title: Multi-cloud security with AWS security services
sessions.abstract: In this 20-minute session, we walk through the multi-cloud security capabilities available across AWS security services today. From detecting threats across cloud providers to managing vulnerabilities and enforcing consistent posture regardless of where workloads run, see how AWS gives security teams unified visibility and response across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments.

sessions.title: How to plan a post-quantum migration strategy
sessions.abstract: Post-quantum migrations can succeed when both the technical and organizational paths are clear. This session delivers a governance-first framework for CISOs and senior technology leaders to drive an organization-wide post-quantum migration. You'll learn how to build executive alignment, establish migration governance, set priorities across business units, and create accountability structures that scale. Learn how AWS is deploying PQ algorithms across our services and how the shared responsibility model applies to this transition. Walk away with a leadership playbook to position your organization ahead of NIST and CNSA 2.0 regulatory timelines.

sessions.title: Journey to Post Quantum (PQ) Authentication in AWS
sessions.abstract: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

sessions.title: AWS detection and response innovations: security at machine speed
sessions.abstract: Discover how the latest AWS detection and response capabilities can help secure your environment more effectively - and faster than ever. We'll cover enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and how AI-powered security operations can close the gap between finding a risk and resolving it. Walk away with actionable insights for integrating AWS security services to strengthen and simplify security across your multicloud environment.

sessions.title: AI governance: from foundations to agentic speed
sessions.abstract: As organizations move from experimental AI to production agentic workloads, governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. In this session, learn how to build a governance foundation for AI using AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to govern autonomous agents operating at machine speed. See how to implement preventive and detective controls for Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence collection, and map controls to frameworks like ISO 42001. Leave with a practical approach to govern AI workloads from first model invocation to fully autonomous agents.

sessions.title: Network Security Innovations for Agentic Workloads
sessions.abstract: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.

sessions.title: From Commit to Secure: Catch Vulnerabilities at Machine Speed with AWS Security Agent
sessions.abstract: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven, but supply chain incidents show registries are targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar: OIDC-based temporary credentials, artifact signing with AWS Signer, dependency governance using CodeArtifact package groups, scanning with Amazon Inspector, and detection with GuardDuty and Security Hub. Walk away with a defense-in-depth blueprint you can scale across your environment.

sessions.title: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
sessions.abstract: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.

sessions.title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
sessions.abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.

sessions.title: One security view across every cloud: AI-driven prioritization at scale
sessions.abstract: Security operations are shifting from manual triage to AI-driven prioritization. AWS Security Hub leads that shift with new AI capabilities that surface actionable insights, reduce noise, and help security teams focus on what matters across their entire environment. In this session, we cover how Security Hub's expanded multicloud support enables unified visibility and compliance monitoring across your cloud environments from a single pane of glass. See how these advances can help you move faster with less effort.

sessions.title: Build a KMS key lifecycle dashboard with usage and cost insights
sessions.abstract: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.

sessions.title: AWS Network Firewall implementation made simple with Infrastructure as Code
sessions.abstract: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

sessions.title: Building Production-Ready Agents Securely: Lessons from AWS at Scale
sessions.abstract: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

sessions.title: Closing the Loop: Using Frontier Agents for Continuous Governance
sessions.abstract: Build a Well-Architected workload with three AI agents working design-to-runtime for always-on AI governance. In this builders' session, combine Security Agent (now part of Continuum) for pre-deployment checks, DevOps Agent for triage and root-cause analysis, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration via MCP tools. You'll scan for OWASP Top 10 issues, run pen tests, and use ready-to-merge fix PRs. You'll author a skill encoding your runbooks, catch a privilege escalation bug that manual review missed, witness DevOps Agent diagnose an incident, and ship a complete loop: design, code review, adversarial tests, CI/CD gates, monitoring, AI-driven RCA, mapped to a Well-Architected pillar.

sessions.title: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
sessions.abstract: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with explicit proxy-based egress controls
sessions.abstract: Dive deep into a new AWS Network Firewall deployment mode that enables explicit forward proxy functionality for outbound HTTP/S traffic. Unlike transparent firewall inspection, an explicit proxy allows you to authenticate traffic sources and apply granular application-layer filtering on outbound connections. In this builders session, you'll deploy this new capability, configure your workloads to route traffic through it, and write rules that control which outbound connections are permitted from your environment. You leave with hands-on experience setting up and operating the explicit proxy functionality and an understanding of how it complements transparent inspection for a more complete egress security posture.

sessions.title: Advanced AWS Network Security: Defending Against Emerging Threats
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, master AWS network security techniques using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Gain practical experience configuring URL category filtering to detect unauthorized AI service usage, and explore recent feature improvements for container workload protection and advanced DNS-layer defenses. Through real-world scenarios, you'll implement IDS/IPS filtering, east-west traffic controls, and domain-based policies using fully managed AWS services. Leave equipped to build resilient network defenses that address both traditional and emerging threats.

sessions.title: Crypto Escape Room: Race to migrate to quantum resistance
sessions.abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is on and here's a chance to test your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a visible countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, data-at-rest re-encryption, code signing rotation, certificate lifecycle automation, or secrets key rotation. Teams unlock "quantum resistance badges" as they complete steps using AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Certificate Manager, and AWS Secrets Manager. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence you can execute under pressure.

sessions.title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
sessions.abstract: What if your customers' data needs to stay invisible even to you? Cryptographic computing makes computation on encrypted data without decrypting it possible. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) has become practical for ML inference. In this session, learn what FHE is, why it now works at scale on AWS, and how to get started. We will walk through two examples: encrypted ML inference on medical images and financial transactions, and encrypted ETL that aggregates records without exposing individual values. Leave with a deployment blueprint built for regulated industries.

sessions.title: Preventing unintended access: a practical guide to data perimeter controls
sessions.abstract: Are you looking to prevent unintended access to your data and mitigate data exposure risks? This hands-on session demonstrates how data perimeter controls implemented through service control policies (SCPs), resource control policies (RCPs), and VPC endpoint policies help keep corporate data within organizational boundaries. You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.

sessions.title: Shift left on IAM: enable developers to self-serve roles and policies
sessions.abstract: What if developers could create IAM roles and policies for faster deployment without being gated by security teams? In this workshop, you embed IAM governance directly into your CI/CD pipeline so developers can self-serve roles and policies safely, regardless of IaC tool. You build permissions boundaries that define safe zones, use IAM Access Analyzer to catch overly broad policies before deployment, and set up AWS Organizations tag policies to enforce required tags for attribute-based access control. You leave with a working pipeline that enforces security and tag compliance on every IAM change you ship.

sessions.title: Securing AI Coding Agents: Defence in Depth Across the Development Lifecycle
sessions.abstract: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defence-in-depth framework spanning five phases - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defence at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, and CodePipeline. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

sessions.title: Investigating AI Threats: Extending IR to the Generative AI Layer
sessions.abstract: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

sessions.title: Assume Breach, Prove Recovery: A ransomware resilience workshop
sessions.abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using cross-region vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and clean room validation are non-negotiable.

sessions.title: Not all bots are bad: Building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
sessions.abstract: Today's edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and bad actors — and treating them all the same costs you either security or revenue. This session shows how to turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it intelligently: legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic gets diverted into deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get differentiated treatment that opens the door to new monetization models — all without touching your origin logic. You'll leave with a practical blueprint for classification-driven traffic control, deception-based threat response, and monitoring patterns you can put into production right away.

sessions.title: What's new in Application Security: Securing applications at machine speed
sessions.abstract: AI is accelerating your release cadence. AWS application security capabilities help engineering teams ship secure applications faster, including AI-powered workloads. In this session, learn how AI-driven services enforce organizational guardrails before code is written, perform threat modeling, review code for vulnerabilities, generate fixes automatically, and enable on-demand penetration testing. See how to codify these into paved pathways that give developers room to build with AI while maintaining consistent security standards. Leave with a clear plan for embedding AWS application security into your platform, from design through continuous validation.

sessions.title: Securing multi-agent orchestration
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent systems create new attack surfaces at every point agents communicate: prompt injection propagating across agent boundaries, agent impersonation, unauthorized tool use, and data exfiltration through inter-agent channels. Join us to explore defense-in-depth for multi-agent orchestration using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AWS Step Functions, and Amazon EventBridge. We whiteboard patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing per-agent tool-use policies, detecting anomalous behavior, and implementing kill switches. Leave with a mental model for production-grade multi-agent security.

sessions.title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
sessions.abstract: When a cloud-native energy company needed to build security operations from scratch, they faced a choice: hire a SOC team or find a smarter way to triage threats. In this talk, the AWS Customer Incident Response Team walks through how customers go from manual CloudTrail analysis to AI-assisted triage, and why that matters now that adversaries are using AI to accelerate their own attacks.

sessions.title: Security Leverage at AI Velocity: The Operating Model Shift
sessions.abstract: AI investment is no longer just an engineering decision. It's a security decision. AI velocity and security velocity compound together to produce enterprise value. The same velocity AI gives your developers is now available to your adversaries. The asymmetry that protected enterprises for decades is shifting. This session covers the operating model shift that compounds enterprise value rather than erodes it. We show how engineers paired with frontier agents, carrying application context across design, code, and pen testing, produce security leverage for your organization.

sessions.title: Next-gen threat detection: GuardDuty advanced security capabilities
sessions.abstract: Amazon GuardDuty leverages AI and machine learning at scale to detect threats across your AWS environment. In this session, explore the latest advances in GuardDuty's detection capabilities, including new AI-driven models, expanded coverage areas, and deeper integration with your security workflows. Learn how these enhancements help you detect sophisticated threats faster, reduce investigation time, and stay ahead of evolving attack techniques.

sessions.title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
sessions.abstract: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities.
