In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.

sessions.title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
sessions.abstract: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.

sessions.title: Threat Technique Catalog for AWS: Practical Controls for Real TTPs
sessions.abstract: AWS CIRT responds to security events across organizations of all sizes. Across events, patterns and trends emerge. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn that pattern into an advantage: take what threat actors are actually doing and build it into actionable detections and mitigations in security operations.

sessions.title: AI-Assisted Incident Response: Preparing for AI-Assisted Offensive
sessions.abstract: When a cloud-native energy company needed to build security operations from scratch, they faced a choice: hire a SOC team or find a smarter way to triage threats. In this talk, the customer's CISO and AWS CIRT walk through how they went from manual CloudTrail analysis to AI-assisted triage, and why that matters now that adversaries are using AI to accelerate their own attacks.

sessions.title: LOTA: Detecting and preventing advanced lateral movement
sessions.abstract: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

sessions.title: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
sessions.abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

sessions.title: Automated memory forensics at scale with generative AI
sessions.abstract: In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.

sessions.title: Good Fences Make Good Neighbours: A Network perimeter approach to data perimeters
sessions.abstract: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.

sessions.title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
sessions.abstract: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You'll deploy an AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then layer four controls: Bedrock Guardrails for input validation & content filtering, AgentCore Policy enforcing Cedar-based tool authorization (role-based access, parameter constraints), CloudWatch anomaly detection for behavioral observability, and Step Functions automated response for operational control. Then you'll test your system with five scenarios that exercise each layer independently and verify the controls work as designed.

sessions.title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
sessions.abstract: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

sessions.title: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
sessions.abstract: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.

sessions.title: Zero trust for non-muman identities: IAM for autonomous agents
sessions.abstract: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.

sessions.title: Simplify your key management: Choosing between AWS KMS and CloudHSM
sessions.abstract: You're running AWS CloudHSM, but do you still need to? AWS Key Management Service (KMS) capabilities now cover many workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, at lower cost and operational overhead. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through the decision together. Using a framework from real customer migrations, we'll whiteboard your use case, identify what's keeping you on CloudHSM, and map a migration path to KMS where it fits. Leave with concrete next steps to simplify your cryptographic infrastructure.

sessions.title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
sessions.abstract: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for Security: How AWS CIRT reduced triage time to minutes
sessions.abstract: When a security event hits a customer account, every minute counts. Learn how AWS CIRT built an agentic AI system using Amazon Kiro that performs investigation workflows autonomously: ingesting case data, baselining environments, analyzing indicators, and producing triage assessments. We cover architecture decisions for AI agents with live AWS API access, evaluation frameworks measuring accuracy against expert answer keys, and guardrails keeping humans in the loop. Leave with patterns for applying agentic AI to operational workflows where accuracy is non-negotiable.

sessions.title: Shared Judgment: Security Culture for the Agentic Era
sessions.abstract: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, answering messages. They communicate on your behalf — and surface every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security has long operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents collapse the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

sessions.title: Centralized governance for multicloud environments
sessions.abstract: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on three separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with drift no one catches, compliance evidence assembled by hand, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model: AWS Config multicloud support to record and evaluate configuration items from Azure alongside AWS, Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability, and AWS Security Hub to aggregate findings into one compliance surface. You'll walk through a deployable architecture defined in infrastructure as code that gives one analyst a unified view across three clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.

sessions.title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
sessions.abstract: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. In this session, learn how to defend both paths using AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall. See how WAF authenticates callers, enforces rate limits, and blocks prompt-injection payloads before they reach your agent, while Network Firewall applies managed threat-intelligence categories to drop egress traffic to malicious destinations without maintaining custom deny lists. Walk away with a deployable defense-in-depth boundary pattern for your agentic AI workloads.

sessions.title: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
sessions.abstract: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.

sessions.title: A Day in the Life of a SPIFFE SVID
sessions.abstract: Across AWS, on-prem, and other clouds, workloads need verifiable identity without long-lived secrets. Meet SPIFFE. In this chalk talk, we show you how to issue SPIFFE SVIDs and how they flow into AWS. Follow this SVID through SPIRE attestation, cross-cloud federation, exchange for STS credentials via IAM Roles Anywhere or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and presentation to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity for AI agent tool access. Leave with a decision framework for adopting SPIFFE workload identity on AWS.

sessions.title: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
sessions.abstract: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers like Amazon Cognito, Okta, Ping, or Microsoft Entra with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns in Cedar, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema, policy templates, and sample policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.

sessions.title: Quantum-Proof Your IoT Fleet: Migrate Devices to Post-Quantum Cryptography OTA
sessions.abstract: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

sessions.title: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
sessions.abstract: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.

sessions.title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
sessions.abstract: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them to connect across trust boundaries. AWS now offers a path to eliminate them in both directions. STS outbound identity federation lets your AWS workloads exchange their IAM identity for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds, AI model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic Claude, and SaaS platforms like Snowflake. In the other direction, workloads running outside AWS can use IAM Roles Anywhere to obtain temporary AWS credentials, eliminating the need for long-lived access keys. In this session, we cover trust configuration, claim matching, and scoping patterns for both directions, iving you a complete blueprint for removing static credentials from your architecture

sessions.title: Innovation in Identity Security: How We Protect the Cloud & Help You Do It Too
sessions.abstract: Learn how AWS approaches identity as the foundation of cloud security - both protecting AWS infrastructure and enabling customers to operate securely at scale. Explore how AWS innovates in access management and develops prescriptive, service-specific guidance helping organizations adopt services confidently, drives secure-by-default authorization across 300+ services, and ensures IAM policies work predictably. Millennium Partners will share how they use AWS guidance and threat modeling to evaluate new services, strengthen their security posture, and give developers freedom to innovate faster.

sessions.title: Closing the compliance loop when agents change your infrastructure
sessions.abstract: AI agents and automated pipelines now change your infrastructure faster than any review can keep up, and not every change comes through CloudFormation. In this workshop, you'll close the compliance loop end to end: author a CloudFormation Hook that enforces encryption and tagging before deployment, then extend the same logic into an AWS Config custom rule with CloudFormation Guard so out-of-band changes get caught continuously. You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.

sessions.title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
sessions.abstract: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

sessions.title: How Coupang cut security costs protecting billions of requests
sessions.abstract: Your traffic doesn't look like it did two years ago. AI-driven workloads, unpredictable spikes, and relentless growth mean your firewall infrastructure has to keep up or become the bottleneck. Coupang knows this firsthand: millions of e-commerce transactions daily across a massive AWS footprint, with complexity and cost rising in lockstep. In this session, hear how they rearchitected around AWS Network Firewall to scale automatically with their business, strengthened their security posture, and cut costs in the process. Walk away with their architecture patterns, the operational decisions that made it work, and new centralized firewall management capabilities you can apply to your own environment immediately.

sessions.title: Control What Goes Out: Egress Security for AI Workloads
sessions.abstract: Most AWS workloads rely on two fundamental outbound mechanisms—DNS queries and network connections—both of which can be abused for data exfiltration. Learn how to lock down both. We'll cover DNS Firewall enhancements to secure the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how integrating DNSFW with NFW delivers advanced, unified DNS security. We'll also explore URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protections to containerized and AI workloads—helping you achieve compliance and simplified operations at scale.

sessions.title: Architecting Firewalls on AWS: A Layered Defense Strategy
sessions.abstract: Automated traffic now exceeds half the web. L7 attacks are getting smarter. A single firewall isn't enough. This chalk talk explores how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together for layered protection. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including TGW-attached firewall patterns. We dig into trade-offs: centralized vs. distributed inspection, cost vs. latency, and when each service carries the load alone vs. when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams. We'll whiteboard protection that scales with your environment.

sessions.title: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
sessions.abstract: Organizations go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You also explore the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned from real scenarios.

sessions.title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
sessions.abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.

sessions.title: Unify cross-cloud identity with AWS Identity Center and OIDC
sessions.abstract: Organizations running workloads across AWS and GCP face a common challenge: securing cross-cloud access without long-lived credentials or bespoke plumbing. In this session, learn how REA Group standardizes on OpenID Connect to solve both human and machine cross-cloud identity. Explore how AWS Identity Center consolidates workforce access, while Workload Identity Federation replaces Vault-based models with short-lived OIDC tokens for AWS roles, CI/CD pipelines, and Kubernetes workloads. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for building a unified identity mesh across clouds without static keys or centralized bottlenecks.

sessions.title: AWS GameDay - Winning the DDoS Game
sessions.abstract: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!

sessions.title: Red Team CTF: When Auth and Guardrails Aren't Enough
sessions.abstract: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

sessions.title: Ship Permissions Faster: IAM Policy Tools in Your CI/CD Pipeline
sessions.abstract: Build a complete permissions pipeline that identifies IAM policy issues at code review. In this session, we build the pipeline stages: validate policies at pull request time with Access Analyzer, simulate critical access paths before deployment, preview Service Control Policies (SCP) impact against real CloudTrail data, and automatically triage Access Denied errors in production using IAM's new debugging API and autofix recommendations. We'll write commit gates that block overly permissive policies, integration tests that ensure operational permissions, and auto-triage that turns production denials into automated remediation commits.

sessions.title: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: detect and respond in real time
sessions.abstract: In this builder session, you start with a deployed web application containing known OWASP vulnerabilities and race to find and fix them before attackers do. Using AWS Security Agent, you review application designs, reproduce vulnerabilities, and push fixes through a CI/CD pipeline. Simultaneously, Amazon GuardDuty detects active exploitation attempts targeting those same weaknesses — and you respond in real time by isolating compromised resources and hardening configurations. Experience the full closed-loop workflow: Inspector identifies the vulnerability, GuardDuty catches the exploit, and Security Agent generates the remediation.

sessions.title: Navigating the Inter-workings of an Agentic SOC & Threat Hunting Analyst
sessions.abstract: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.

sessions.title: Implement governance guardrails for autonomous AI agents at scale
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, but unconstrained permissions can lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you will build a defense-in-depth governance framework for agentic workloads. You will create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Bedrock Guardrails via IAM policy-based enforcement, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and implement Cedar-based deterministic enforcement in AgentCore. You will leave with a deployable pattern that constrains agent behavior without blocking legitimate actions.

sessions.title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
sessions.abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.

sessions.title: Threat Detection and IR in AgentCore Workloads
sessions.abstract: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

sessions.title: The AWS Security Incident Response Challenge: Defend the Cake!
sessions.abstract: Our Magic Unicorn Cake recipe is under threat from the notorious Grumpy Cats, and you're the AWS Security Engineer who must stop them. This workshop mirrors real security incidents - unauthorized access, suspicious API activity, data exfiltration - wrapped in a fun, immersive scenario. Defend digital delicacies from crafty cyber-cats by implementing threat detection, defensive configurations, monitoring, and incident response. Every technique translates directly to scenarios observed by the AWS Customer Incident Response Team. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Processing PII without exposing it: KYC with Nitro Enclaves
sessions.abstract: Know Your Customer (KYC) pipelines must screen personally identifiable informaiton (PII) against sanctions lists and politically exposed person (PEP) databases while proving to regulators that data was never exposed to unauthorized systems. Traditional Spark pipelines may give executors access to decrypted PII, creating compliance risk. In this workshop, learn how to combine AWS Nitro Enclaves with Amazon EMR on EKS to process PII at scale without exposing plaintext to the compute layer. You'll configure KMS key policies with PCR0 attestation, deploy enclave sidecars as Kubernetes DaemonSets, and run Spark jobs where only screening decisions leave the enclave boundary.

sessions.title: Crossing the kill chain: IR when attackers pivot between clouds.
sessions.abstract: When a threat actor compromises credentials in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool can follow. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the detection and response patterns for cross-cloud lateral movement using Security Hub, Inspector, and multicloud telemetry sources.

sessions.title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
sessions.abstract: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this hands-on workshop, build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets with AWS Secrets Manager, scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

sessions.title: OAuth delegation patterns design for AI agents with Amazon BedRock AgentCore Identity
sessions.abstract: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, but how do you delegate the right access without over-permissioning? In this chalk talk, we explore authorization delegation patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with code examples. We cover every relevant OAuth grant flow: authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. Explore how each pattern maps to real agent scenarios and leave with a decision framework for your architecture.

sessions.title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
sessions.abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.

sessions.title: Resilient workforce access: Multi-region identity architecture on AWS
sessions.abstract: Resilient identity architectures cannot be built around a single point of failure. In this session, we architect layered workforce access resilience across four tiers: IAM Identity Center multi-region replication for external IdP customers, ADFS direct IAM federation as an emergency path for Active Directory environments, regional STS endpoints to remove hidden dependencies, and break-glass IAM users as a last resort. Learn which layers your environment needs, how to sequence failover across them, and how to validate resilience without disrupting production.

sessions.title: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
sessions.abstract: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

sessions.title: A deep dive on IAM policy evaluation
sessions.abstract: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising.  We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.

sessions.title: From Proofs to Production: Neurosymbolic AI and Provable Security
sessions.abstract: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.

sessions.title: From Design to Deployment: Embedding Security into Every Phase of the SDLC
sessions.abstract: AWS Continuum embeds security expertise at every stage of the software development lifecycle: AWS Continuum for threat modeling for architecture documents, AWS Continuum for code scanning for pull requests and full repositories, and AWS Continuum for penetration testing for deployed applications. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into how AWS Continuum coordinates multiple analysis passes with built-in safety guardrails and multi-step validation to deliver high-confidence findings. Bring your questions about integrating security into CI/CD pipelines and scaling AppSec across multiple teams.

sessions.title: Threat Modeling the Agentic SDLC: From User Story to Deployment
sessions.abstract: Agentic development is accelerating, but how do you threat model a workflow where AI makes decisions autonomously? In this Code Talk, walk through an end-to-end process: from threat modeling a user story with AWS Continuum for threat modeling (capabilities are delivered through AWS Security Agent), through the developer workflow, to deployment. See how ThreatForest - an agentic tool built on the Strands framework - autonomously generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and how to build a reusable mitigations catalogue that scales across your organization. Leave with working patterns and hard-won lessons from real-world implementations, including where traditional threat modeling assumptions break down for agentic systems.

sessions.title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
sessions.abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

sessions.title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
sessions.abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to why your AI economics are wrong
sessions.abstract: Most AI business cases use ROI frameworks built for deterministic systems, measuring cost avoidance while missing the metrics that predict success. The gap between pilot and production economics is 10-50x, and most finance teams still model AI as capital expense rather than variable. This session names the three assumptions that guarantee your AI business case is wrong, and the costs that blindside CFOs in production. It presents the financial model Amazon uses internally to forecast AI operating expenditure. You leave knowing which line items to remove from your next business case, and which to add that nobody tracks yet.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the end of the inference constraint
sessions.abstract: Almost every AI decision leaders make today is quietly shaped by one fact: inference is scarce. The cost of intelligence is collapsing, and within a couple of years that constraint is gone. The mistake is assuming the constraints go with it. They do not, they move. When capability is no longer gated by cost, the bottleneck becomes what you run, how you orchestrate it, and whether you can trust what comes back. This session maps that shift, and how to tell which parts of your AI strategy are permanent and which are artifacts of a constraint about to lift.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to advanced team models in an agentic world
sessions.abstract: You built multi-skilled teams for cloud. That shape does not absorb agents. Cheaper execution does not remove work, it relocates it into judgment, verification, and spotting confidently wrong answers. The question we want answered is not about reporting lines, it is "does this new world include me?" The twenty-year senior, the junior who cannot get in, the manager of a smaller team: each needs a different answer. Four operating models return, from today's anti-pattern to the hourglass, with a first-person account of what works inside Amazon and what doesn't. The answer is yes, but the entry requirement has changed.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
sessions.abstract: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
sessions.abstract: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to why your AI governance can't keep up
sessions.abstract: Your AI ships faster than the people allowed to approve it. Approval becomes the place good ideas go to wait. That does not stop the work, it hides it. Governance built to reduce risk now manufactures the risk you cannot see. A separate AI review board adds a queue. Those getting it right kept it inside existing enterprise risk, turning "something bad might happen" into control questions an executive can sign. AI now helps assess AI risk. You leave with questions for your risk function, and a way to match how fast you decide to how fast you build.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
sessions.abstract: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
sessions.abstract: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
sessions.abstract: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to what your board must now about AI (and shouldn't)
sessions.abstract: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
sessions.abstract: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the hardest investment decision in AI
sessions.abstract: Fund the platform or fund the use case? Demand proof before investing or invest to generate the proof? Scale the winner or explore the next opportunity? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and they require the CIO and CFO to act together. Two former operators share how the best CIO-CFO pairs align on what to fund, what to kill, and what "good enough evidence" looks like when certainty isn't available. You leave with the approach that replaces "requestor and approver" with co-ownership, and the questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption when authority cannot
sessions.abstract: Amazon engineers have shipped 500 production MCP servers, with 3,600 more in development. None of it was mandated. Kiro's MCP interface, Claude code in secure environments, and the agentic tooling that spread alongside them moved through the org because Amazon invested in the unglamorous half of adoption: Technical Field Communities, Security Guardians, structured upskilling cadences, and explicit accounting for experimental debt alongside technical debt. This session shows what scales AI adoption when authority cannot, names the new debts every agentic team is quietly accruing, and gives executives the three structures worth funding before the next mandate fails.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
sessions.abstract: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the million-robot question
sessions.abstract: Amazon coordinates more than a million robots with one AI model, improving fleet travel time by roughly 10% and getting better. And still, we keep humans in the loop. Why? Because in the physical world the bottleneck is not capability, it is consequence. A wrong answer can be rolled back. A wrong action cannot. Drawing on the largest robotic fleet on Earth and customer deployments where AI acts on physical assets, this session gives leaders a framework for deploying AI where mistakes have mass, and the questions to ask before AI acts in the real world. This is AI's future.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
sessions.abstract: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

sessions.title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
sessions.abstract: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.

sessions.title: Choosing the right AWS storage service
sessions.abstract: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.

sessions.title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.

sessions.title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
sessions.abstract: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

sessions.title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
sessions.abstract: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.

sessions.title: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
sessions.abstract: Data unavailability is costly, and the threats driving it are only growing in frequency and severity. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. You'll see how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery for availability to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.

sessions.title: Building Apache Iceberg data lakes with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.

sessions.title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

sessions.title: Accelerate data migrations with AWS DataSync at any scale
sessions.abstract: Long migration windows, limited visibility, and complex source environments can slow your data migrations to AWS, whether you are transferring data from on-premises file servers, Hadoop clusters, or multicloud object storage. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts show you how AWS DataSync Enhanced mode's parallel pipeline simultaneously lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies your data to dramatically reduce those timelines. You will learn how to configure for maximum throughput, design endpoint connectivity for secure and efficient data movement, and use richer metrics and monitoring to gain full visibility into your transfer pipeline.

sessions.title: Shared file storage for containers, serverless, and Lambda
sessions.abstract: Containers spin up and disappear. Your application state needs to outlive them. Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and Amazon S3 Files give your containerized and serverless workloads durable, shared file storage. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads on Fargate, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.

sessions.title: Accelerating AI inference with Amazon EBS
sessions.abstract: As organizations optimize AI workflows to keep GPUs highly utilized, Amazon EBS plays a distinct role in the AI pipeline where key business data is close to compute. In this session, learn how EBS minimizes pre-staging time for model weights with low latency, accelerates data preparation and checkpoints on high-performance EBS volumes, and reduces response times by serving vector embeddings at sub-millisecond latencies during inferencing, all while delivering elasticity and configurability in storage and performance. Leave with architecture patterns, volume configurations, and a framework for extending your storage architecture with EBS for AI/ML workloads.

sessions.title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

sessions.title: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
sessions.abstract: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.

sessions.title: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
sessions.abstract: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.

sessions.title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
sessions.abstract: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.

sessions.title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
sessions.abstract: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

sessions.title: Optimize performance and cost of Amazon EBS at massive scale
sessions.abstract: Managing production workloads across multiple regions while weighing cost and risk requires optimal strategy. With block storage, operating at scale can mean different things, including delivering high IOPS or I/O bandwidth to applications, managing and monitoring millions of volumes, or protecting petabytes of data with stringent RPO and RTO requirements. In this talk, learn best practices for scaling and managing your Amazon EBS environment, including automation, monitoring at scale, and cost-optimization techniques using cloud-native tools to meet your business needs.

sessions.title: Gaining insights with S3 Metadata and annotations
sessions.abstract: Learn how S3 annotations let you attach rich, structured context (JSON, XML, YAML, or plain text) directly to your objects without re-uploading them. In this session, you will configure annotations on a live dataset, build an enrichment pipeline that attaches AI-generated summaries on ingest, query annotation payloads at scale through S3 Metadata's Apache Iceberg table in Athena, and wire an AI agent that discovers and retrieves objects using annotation-based search. You leave with patterns for zero-read agentic discovery and metadata architectures that scale to billions of objects.

sessions.title: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.

sessions.title: Build a fully managed data lake with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Data lakes have evolved from raw Parquet files with Hive-style partitioning to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables. In this hands-on workshop, you'll understand that evolution, then build a working analytics data lake with Amazon S3 Tables in under two hours. You'll create an S3 table bucket, ingest real-world data, migrate data into the bucket, and query it with Amazon Athena. You'll also learn how to connect third-party tools like DuckDB for interactive exploration. Along the way we’ll cover the benefits of fully managed Iceberg tables and when to use Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation for open data architectures.

sessions.title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
sessions.abstract: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

sessions.title: Accelerate database protection, recovery, and testing with Amazon EBS
sessions.abstract: Protecting your data and troubleshooting issues are essential for running production self-managed databases on AWS. This builders’ session tackles both. Get hands-on with EBS Snapshot Lock for immutable backups, Recycle Bin for accidental deletion recovery, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for automated, application-consistent snapshots. Learn Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization for predictable restore throughput and use EBS Volume Clones to create virtually instant point-in-time copies without impacting production. You will leave with a practical playbook to improve your database resilience. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

sessions.title: Build an AI-powered AWS Backup analyst with multi-agent orchestration
sessions.abstract: Few teams have the capacity to continuously audit their backup posture across accounts and regions. AI agents can do that work and recommend fixes while keeping you in control. In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and deploy a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval to AgentCore Gateway. Leave with a scalable pattern you can run in your own environment.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
sessions.abstract: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.title: Build and optimize data transfers with AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
sessions.abstract: When you're moving petabytes from on-premises file servers and multicloud object stores into AWS, transfer speed and operational visibility are equally critical. In this builders session, you'll configure AWS DataSync Enhanced mode to move data from diverse source environments into AWS using its parallel pipeline for high-throughput transfers. Enhanced mode generates detailed task reports and transfer logs as it works. You'll then use Amazon Bedrock to analyze that data, surfacing performance bottlenecks and generating optimization recommendations. Walk away with reusable patterns for fast data movement and AI-powered transfer visibility.

sessions.title: Simplify secure file sharing with Transfer Family no-code web apps
sessions.abstract: Traditional file transfer solutions often require complex client software, custom scripts, or technical expertise, creating barriers for business users who need to share data. Learn how AWS Transfer Family web apps enable secure, browser-based file transfers that automatically trigger data processing workflows. We'll show you how to build automated pipelines that process files upon upload while maintaining enterprise-grade security through AWS IAM Identity Center for your workforce or Amazon Cognito for external users. Discover how to streamline file ingestion, kick off validations, and orchestrate downstream processing, starting with a simple drag-and-drop interface for your end users.

sessions.title: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
sessions.abstract: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.title: Improving your database agility with Amazon FSx
sessions.abstract: Customers self-manage databases on AWS to maintain full control over architecture, functionality, availability, and performance. Amazon FSx provides the high-performance, highly available storage they need to do this at scale. This workshop will whiteboard production architectures for self-managed databases on Linux and Windows using Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, NetApp ONTAP, and Windows File Server. Learn how to architect for high performance and high availability, implement zero-copy snapshots and clones for rapid database refresh, and accelerate backup and recovery. Whether you run Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL, bring your architecture questions.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
sessions.abstract: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
sessions.abstract: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.

sessions.title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
sessions.abstract: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.

sessions.title: AWS Backup: Centralized data protection for your cloud environment
sessions.abstract: Managing data protection across a growing cloud environment requires a centralized strategy. AWS Backup was designed around this principle, giving more than 150,000 organizations a fully managed service to automate backup operations, enforce protection policies at scale, and safeguard 20+ AWS services from a single console. From human error to infrastructure failures to targeted attacks, AWS Backup helps ensure you can recover the right data, at the right time, with confidence. In this session, learn how AWS Backup works, how you can use it to protect mission-critical workloads, and hear directly from customers about their implementation strategies and operational outcomes.

sessions.title: Secure data transfers at scale with AWS DataSync and Transfer Family
sessions.abstract: Organizations moving data to AWS need transfers that are fast, secure, and manageable at petabyte scale. In this session, learn how AWS DataSync and AWS Transfer Family help you accelerate migrations, automate ongoing data movement, and enable secure file exchanges with external partners. We'll cover best practices for maximizing throughput, designing transfer architectures for performance and cost efficiency, and integrating secure workflows across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. Hear directly from a customer about how they used these services to solve large-scale data movement challenges in production.

sessions.title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
sessions.abstract: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.

sessions.title: Designing cost-efficient Iceberg data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

sessions.title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
sessions.abstract: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

sessions.title: A practical guide to Amazon S3 data protection
sessions.abstract: Learn step-by-step methods to protect your critical Amazon S3 data against accidental deletion, ransomware, and corruption, even at billion-object and petabyte scale. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.

sessions.title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
sessions.abstract: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We cover S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata journal tables for storage analytics at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

sessions.title: "Optimize performance and cost for archival data with Amazon S3  "
sessions.abstract: Not all data needs frequent access, but it still needs the right retrieval strategy when called upon. In this chalk talk, learn how to design a cost-effective archival storage strategy using Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes. We cover how to analyze access patterns to identify archival candidates, automate data movement with S3 Lifecycle policies and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and design restore workflows using S3 Batch Operations and S3 Event Notifications. Whether you're retaining compliance data for years or staging cold datasets for periodic analytics, leave with a practical framework for balancing retrieval performance against long-term storage costs.

sessions.title: Optimize HPC with storage for throughput and IOPS
sessions.abstract: High-performance computing workloads demand storage that keeps pace with thousands of compute nodes processing data in parallel. Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput without the operational burden of managing a parallel file system. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS adds high IOPS with consistent low-latency response for latency-sensitive workloads. Explore how to select the right deployment type based on your workload profile, leverage native S3 integration for data pipelines, and right-size performance independently from capacity. Bring your questions about CFD (computational fluid dynamics), genomics, semiconductor design, weather modeling, and other compute-intensive workloads.

sessions.title: Migrating petabytes at scale: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
sessions.abstract: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes.
