Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.

sessions.title: From CSV to Iceberg: Understanding open data formats on Amazon S3
sessions.abstract: Building a data lake on Amazon S3 and need to decide between Parquet, Hive, and Iceberg – or understand how your team already did? In this session we develop the mental model for storing structured data on Amazon S3 and trace how it evolved. Understand formats from CSV to Parquet that accelerate analytic queries, walk through the evolution of table and partition schemas that organize data at scale, and learn how open table formats like Apache Iceberg bring database-like capabilities to your data lake. Leave with a clear picture of each and how Amazon S3 Tables bring it all together as a fully managed experience.

sessions.title: Accelerate database protection and testing with EBS Snapshots and clones
sessions.abstract: Teams that rely on backups alone risk slow dev cycles, compliance gaps, and prolonged recovery times. Learn how Amazon EBS Snapshots and Volume Clones solve these challenges together. See how Snapshots deliver incremental, cross-region data protection with automated lifecycle policies for compliance, while Volume Clones create instant local copies for development and testing. We'll compare cost, performance, and architectural tradeoffs. You'll leave with a decision framework for when to snapshot, when to clone, and how to combine both in production architectures.

sessions.title: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
sessions.abstract: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but mutli-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.

sessions.title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
sessions.abstract: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.

sessions.title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
sessions.abstract: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

sessions.title: Break free from on-premises NAS: Migrating to AWS
sessions.abstract: Learn how Amazon FSx storage simplifies the migration of on premises workloads to the cloud while keeping the compatibility and performance your apps depend on. With fully managed, block and file storage that eliminates operational overhead, see real-world migration patterns for user file shares, high-performance applications, enterprise databases like Oracle, SAP, and SQL Server, and VMware migration with AWS Transform and FSx for ONTAP. Discover how organizations are reducing costs and accelerating innovation.
services: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

sessions.title: Best practices for cost optimization with AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: AWS Backup protects workloads across more than 20 AWS services, and each resource type brings its own cost profile. In this chalk talk, learn practical approaches to managing your data protection TCO by tailoring your AWS Backup strategy to each workload. We'll dig into full versus incremental backups, lifecycle policies, cold storage tiering for S3 and other resource types, and backing up direclty to logically-air-gapped-vault to protect data from ransomware without maintaining multiple copies. Then we'll cover how to build cost observability using AWS Backup reporting and monitoring to track and optimize spend.

sessions.title: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.

sessions.title: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.

sessions.title: Advanced S3 performance engineering: From multipart to resilience
sessions.abstract: Master advanced Amazon S3 performance optimization techniques across storage classes, including S3 Standard for general purpose storage and S3 Express One Zone for the highest performance needs. This expert-level workshop focuses on implementing sophisticated data transfer patterns using multipart uploads and Transfer Manager. Design and deploy resilient applications with advanced retry strategies and robust error handling mechanisms. Through technical exercises, build high-performance solutions for large-scale data transfers across different S3 storage classes. Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.title: Deploying mission-critical applications with Amazon EBS
sessions.abstract: Millions of users run their performance-intensive enterprise applications and databases on AWS. In this workshop, explore the step-by-step process of deploying a high-performance application on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS for optimized availability, resiliency, and cost performance. Discover how to select the ideal Amazon EC2 instance types and Amazon EBS volume types for various workloads. Learn about on-demand storage flexibility and performance using Elastic Volumes. Monitor and improve the operational performance and resource optimization of Amazon EBS using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Build resilience and fault tolerance using AWS Fault Injection Service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
sessions.abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll build ransomware recovery capabilities using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults, restore testing, and Backup Audit Manager. Working through a simulated account compromise scenario, you'll implement protection across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and predictable availability. Configure vault isolation policies, validate backup integrity, orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised, and walk away with a tested recovery playbook. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
sessions.abstract: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
sessions.abstract: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.

sessions.title: Optimizing containerized applications with shared file storage
sessions.abstract: Containerized workloads can face unpredictable latency spikes, throughput bottlenecks, and runaway costs as they scale. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through techniques for identifying these issues and solving them in production environments. Bring your use cases, performance questions, and architecture challenges as we tune Amazon EFS, Amazon S3 Files, and Amazon FSx for real-world EKS and ECS deployments. We'll cover IO profiling, throughput vs. latency tradeoffs, cost-optimization strategies, multi-attach EFS configurations, FSx volume sizing, and POSIX-compatible pipeline design on S3 Files. You'll leave with practical insights you can apply to your environment immediately.

sessions.title: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.

sessions.title: AWS Backup clean room recovery: Comprehensive resilience framework
sessions.abstract: Having an isolated vault is only half the battle. When a cyber event hits, you need confidence your backups are clean and recoverable. In this chalk talk, learn how to design an Isolated Recovery Environment using AWS Backup that validates and restores data in a secure space separate from production: reducing blast radius, breaking the kill chain, and proving recoverability on demand. We'll cover immutable air-gapped copies, automated restore testing with malware scanning, and Multi-party approval to control recovery access during account compromise. Leave with a framework for building recovery confidence into your backup strategy.

sessions.title: AWS Backup at scale: centralizing enterprise data protection
sessions.abstract: Protecting a single workload is straightforward. But when every team owns their own accounts, organizations need a centralized approach to enforce consistent data protection across all of them. We'll dig into how to build backup architectures that scale across your entire AWS estate, covering Organizations backup policies to enforce protection standards across accounts, cross-account and cross-region copy strategies, and Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring and audit evidence. Whether you're onboarding new accounts or tightening controls on existing ones, we'll walk through patterns for centralized data protection you can prove.

sessions.title: AWS Transfer Family: From SFTP to Agentic AI Workflows
sessions.abstract: Learn how to build enterprise-grade file transfer solutions using AWS Transfer Family and extend them into agentic AI workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through building secure SFTP servers, integrating with enterprise identity providers like Okta and Azure AD, and automating file processing using Terraform. We'll explore how event-driven architectures handle malware scanning with GuardDuty, and how AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore take over downstream tasks like data extraction and fraud detection. Bring your questions. You'll walk away with practical patterns for evolving traditional managed file transfer into intelligent, agentic processing pipelines.

sessions.title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
sessions.abstract: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

sessions.title: Advanced security patterns on Amazon S3
sessions.abstract: Amazon S3 security settings and access controls suit virtually any workload, but as data estates grow to millions of buckets across organizational boundaries, standard policy approaches hit limits. In this chalk talk, equip yourself with proven patterns for managing access at scale: optimizing policy evaluation with access points and access grants, scaling beyond IAM policy limits with cross-account structures, implementing attribute-based controls that adapt as teams and datasets grow, and securing your data lake perimeter with resource control policies. Join the S3 security team for a structured discussion of the patterns that solve the hardest multi-account access problems at scale.

sessions.title: Building your first event-driven application
sessions.abstract: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Building interactive web applications on AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: Web applications need fast responses, server-side rendering, and real-time updates, but managing origin servers, CDN configurations, and scaling infrastructure pulls you away from building features. In this builders' session, deploy a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll configure routing and static asset delivery, implement server-side rendering with consistent low latency, and add real-time interactivity. Walk away with a working application and deployment patterns for production web workloads. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Building lightning-fast web apps
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this lightning talk, hear how a customer built a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. They cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical takeaways for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
sessions.abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

sessions.title: How AI-native startups run untrusted agent code on Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.abstract: AI agents increasingly generate and execute untrusted code that needs a safe, isolated place to run. A growing set of AI-native startups and ISVs are converging on one pattern: one MicroVM per agent session, spun up on demand, torn down when the work is done. In this session, see how [Customer] built production agent sandboxes on Lambda MicroVMs, walking through the full lifecycle that delivers hardware-level isolation per session. See how they scale to thousands of concurrent sandboxes and the operational tradeoffs they navigated to get there.

sessions.title: AWS Serverless developer experience
sessions.abstract: The AWS Serverless Developer Experience (SDE) workshop is a hands-on workshop that immerses developers in building serverless solutions. It covers composing serverless applications, event-driven architecture principles, serverless observability, open-source tools, and deployment automation, and is available in Python, Typescript, Java, or .NET runtime. The workshop aims to accelerate your serverless maturity through a real-world use case, challenging you to understand the “why” behind the design decisions, and their implementation, as you complete the solution and apply Serverless best practices.

sessions.title: Building serverless applications with Terraform
sessions.abstract: Master the integration of serverless technology with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform on AWS. In this hands-on workshop, learn to efficiently define, deploy, and maintain serverless architectures—from Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints to DynamoDB tables and EventBridge rules. Whether you're new to Terraform or looking to apply it to serverless workloads, you'll gain practical experience writing reusable modules, managing state, and automating deployments across environments. Walk away with patterns you can immediately apply to your own serverless projects. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
sessions.abstract: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building event-driven architectures
sessions.abstract: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: What's new in AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: The serverless landscape moves fast, and the months leading up to re:Invent bring a wave of new capabilities for building event-driven applications. This hands-on workshop is your chance to explore the latest releases the moment they land. Build with the newest serverless features, work through the technical trade-offs that matter in real systems, and leave with production-ready patterns you can apply the moment you're back at your desk. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.abstract: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, set up observability for sandboxed executions, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Building Serverless distributed data processing workloads
sessions.abstract: Processing large-scale data shouldn't require provisioning clusters or managing batch infrastructure. In this builders' session, design and deploy a distributed data processing pipeline using AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. Working in small groups, you'll implement fan-out patterns that process thousands of objects in parallel, handle partial failures gracefully, and optimize for cost and throughput. Learn when Distributed Map is the right choice versus other parallelization strategies, and walk away with a reusable pipeline template. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
sessions.abstract: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
sessions.abstract: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
sessions.abstract: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

sessions.title: Building Serverless applications at AI speed
sessions.abstract: Manually wiring up Lambda functions, API Gateway routes, and IaC templates for every new service is repetitive work that AI handles well. In this builders' session, use Kiro to go from natural language specifications to a deployed serverless application. You'll configure MCP tool servers to give the AI agent access to AWS APIs, author steering documents that produce consistent output, and iterate on generated infrastructure until it passes validation. Walk away with techniques for getting reliable, production-ready code from AI-assisted workflows. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Automating Serverless migrations at scale with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Runtime deprecations pile up. API migrations stall. Legacy code sits untouched because manual upgrades across hundreds of functions take weeks your team doesn't have. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to assess, plan, and execute Lambda runtime upgrades and API migrations at scale. Working hands-on, you'll run the full agentic loop: codebase assessment, transformation planning, incremental code changes committed to Git, and self-validating test execution. You'll scale transformations across hundreds of functions in parallel using AWS Batch and Fargate. Walk away with patterns for automated, large-scale modernization. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Same code, any compute: Portable architecture on AWS
sessions.abstract: Your business logic shouldn't be coupled to a compute service. In this session, apply Hexagonal Architecture and 12-factor patterns to design workloads where compute is a deployment decision, not an architectural one. Through live code, see the same logic packaged as a Lambda function, a Fargate task, and an EKS pod using AWS Lambda Web Adapter and runtime-neutral handler patterns. You'll learn where portability pays off, where it adds unnecessary abstraction, and how to evaluate the trade-offs between pay-per-request, always-on containers, and orchestrated clusters for your workloads.

sessions.title: Serverless streaming data processing with AWS Lambda and Apache Kafka
sessions.abstract: Build a serverless streaming data pipeline in 60 minutes. In this builders' session, you design and deploy a real-time location tracking app that ingests events from Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK), processes them with AWS Lambda, and pushes live updates to a dashboard through AWS AppSync—no consumer fleet to manage, no scaling logic to write. Experiment with Lambda event source mapping for Kafka, applying recent improvements in filtering, batching, and error handling. You must bring your laptop to participate.
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)

sessions.title: Build self-healing Serverless applications with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. In this builders' session, work with a deployed serverless application and use AWS DevOps Agent to resolve real-world failures autonomously. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Orchestrating agentic workflows: Step Functions & durable functions
sessions.abstract: AI agents need orchestration that handles long-running tasks, human approvals, and recovery from partial failures. In this chalk talk, compare AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for agentic workloads, and learn when to choose code-first, replay-based recovery versus visual state-machine semantics. We’ll whiteboard how durable functions checkpoint progress and resume after failures, how Step Functions handle branching and parallel tool calls, and where Lambda MicroVMs fit for sandboxing agent-generated code execution. Bring your architecture questions—we’ll design hybrid patterns that combine both orchestrators based on your workload shape.

sessions.title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
sessions.abstract: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

sessions.title: Distributed transactions with Step Functions and durable functions
sessions.abstract: Distributed transactions across microservices break in ways monoliths never did: partial failures, inconsistent state, rollbacks that don't roll back. In this builders' session, build a payment processing using saga pattern that orchestrates multiple serverless microservices using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions. You'll implement compensation mechanisms that handle partial failures, compare orchestration approaches for short-lived versus long-running transactions, and monitor transaction flows across distributed services. Walk away with working saga patterns and the observability setup to troubleshoot them in production. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
sessions.abstract: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

sessions.title: Build interactive web apps with AWS Lambda
sessions.abstract: Web applications need persistent connections, session state, and native HTTP handling - capabilities that don't map obviously to Lambda's request-response model. In this session, see how to run web frameworks like Express, Hono, and Next.js directly on Lambda using runtime adapters that preserve the framework's native patterns. If you're running containerized web apps today, we walk through practical migration paths that move your existing framework code to Lambda with minimal changes.

sessions.title: Guardrails for AI-henerated Serverless infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

sessions.title: Testing serverless and event-driven applications
sessions.abstract: You're shipping faster with serverless, but your testing strategy hasn't kept up. Local mocks drift from cloud behavior. Integration tests require full deployments. Contract changes between services break downstream consumers silently. In this chalk talk, whiteboard testing approaches that match how serverless developers actually work: unit testing business logic in isolation, integration testing service interactions without deploying everything, and contract testing event schemas between producers and consumers. We cover local versus cloud testing tradeoffs, when each makes sense, and chaos engineering techniques like injecting message delays, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery to catch failures before your users do.

sessions.title: Operating Lambda at scale: Choosing the right execution model
sessions.abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

sessions.title: Serverless Java in 2026
sessions.abstract: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM native AOT deliver sub-second startup, and Lambda Managed Instances give steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

sessions.title: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
sessions.abstract: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

sessions.title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
sessions.abstract: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

sessions.title: Operating Serverless at scale: What changes at 1000+ functions
sessions.abstract: What works at 10 Lambda functions may not work at 1,000. Deployments that took seconds now take hours. A single misconfigured function triggers account-level throttling. Observability drowns in noise. In this chalk talk, we discuss what changes at scale: deployment strategies that roll out code safely across hundreds of functions, account structure and concurrency management to prevent blast radius problems, observability approaches that surface signal without drowning in cardinality, and platform engineering patterns that let application teams ship independently. We share what large-scale Serverless operators do differently and where the common pitfalls are.

sessions.title: Building Serverless AI agents
sessions.abstract: AI agents need more than an LLM and a prompt. Production agents require tool execution with least-privilege isolation, orchestration that recovers from partial failures, and observability that tracks token spend alongside function duration. In this chalk talk, we discuss architectural patterns for Serverless AI agents: model routing across providers and cost tiers, fault-tolerant orchestration with Step Functions and Lambda durable functions, isolated code execution using MicroVMs, and state management for long-running multi-step workflows. We whiteboard the decisions that matter for your workload shape and where each pattern introduces complexity you may not need.

sessions.title: Modernizing multi-tenant workloads with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.abstract: Many organizations run untrusted or tenant-specific code on shared container clusters with complex isolation logic they built themselves. Namespace hacks, sidecar proxies, and custom scheduling rules all add operational weight without delivering hardware-level guarantees. Lambda MicroVMs offer a modernization path: replace self-managed isolation infrastructure with VM-level sandboxes that persist filesystem state across invocations and scale to zero between tasks. In this session, we cover migration patterns from container-based multi-tenant architectures to MicroVMs, the security model that replaces your custom isolation layer, stateful session management, and integration with orchestration services. We discuss what migrates cleanly and what needs redesign.

sessions.title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
sessions.abstract: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session, we cover what actually changes: function design patterns for agent consumption, orchestration choices for non-deterministic workflows, cost governance when an agent loop calls 200 functions in a single reasoning chain, and observability that tracks token spend alongside invocation metrics. We also cover what doesn't change, and where existing Serverless patterns hold up without modification.

sessions.title: What's new with Amazon API Gateway
sessions.abstract: Your next API consumer might not be a person. AI agents, MCP servers, and coding assistants are calling APIs programmatically, and they need machine-readable schemas, predictable error contracts, and discoverable endpoints. In this session, we cover what's new with Amazon API Gateway: recent launches, direct service integrations that eliminate Lambda glue code, declarative event wiring, and patterns from real customer deployments. We also discuss how to design APIs that serve both human developers and autonomous agents without maintaining separate interfaces.

sessions.title: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
sessions.abstract: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

sessions.title: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
sessions.abstract: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. Implement an MCP server with versioned tools, wire it to AgentCore Gateway for discovery and invocation, then expose an entire Step Functions workflow, human-in-the-loop gates and all, as a single callable tool. Add scoped agent identity, watch an unauthorized call get blocked, then an authorized one go through. Walk away with a repeatable playbook for turning existing APIs into agent-ready tools.

sessions.title: A day in the life of a Serverless builder
sessions.abstract: In this code talk, follow a Serverless application from first line of code to production deployment, all live. Start with an AI coding agent generating infrastructure and function scaffolding, iterate locally with hot reload, deploy in one command, then debug a failing request by tracing it across Lambda, EventBridge, and DynamoDB using native OpenTelemetry. Along the way, see how recent Serverless launches change the workflow: faster deploys, built-in observability, and simplified local testing. No slides, no diagrams. Just a terminal, an editor, and the workflow a Serverless developer uses in 2026.

sessions.title: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
sessions.abstract: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.

sessions.title: Building and scaling low latency web apps with AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this code talk, build a full-stack web application entirely on AWS serverless services, live in code: API endpoints, business logic, data persistence, and authentication. We walk through architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and show how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with patterns you can apply to your own projects.

sessions.title: Serverless compute built for the web
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, see how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. We cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Orchestrating agentic applications with Lambda durable functions
sessions.abstract: AI agents are powerful, but production workloads need more than an LLM and a prompt. They require deterministic routing, audit trails, compensation logic, and human oversight. In this workshop, build agentic orchestration using AWS Lambda durable functions and MCP tools. Learn to design workflows that checkpoint progress, recover from failures automatically, and pause for human-in-the-loop approval—all without managing additional infrastructure. You'll implement tool-calling patterns, handle multi-step reasoning with retries, and deploy agents that are observable, testable, and production-ready. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, discover how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services—from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration
sessions.abstract: AI workflows need state such as conversation history, intermediate results, and human approvals, but managing it shouldn't require a database and custom recovery logic. In this builders' session, build a stateful AI workflow that checkpoints progress, recovers from failures automatically, and pauses for external callbacks. Working hands-on with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-step reasoning chains with retry semantics, compare orchestration approaches for different workflow shapes, and deploy a working agent pipeline. Walk away with patterns for choosing the right orchestration tool for your workload. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: AWS Technical Essentials
sessions.abstract: AWS Technical Essentials gives you the foundation to start building on AWS with confidence. In this bootcamp, navigate the AWS Management Console, configure IAM security controls, deploy compute workloads across EC2, Lambda, and containers, set up databases with RDS and DynamoDB, manage storage with S3, explore networking services, and monitor resources with CloudWatch. Hands-on labs reinforce each topic, so you leave ready to design available, scalable, and cost-effective solutions.

sessions.title: Become an AWS AI Business Strategist
sessions.abstract: Turning an AI idea into enterprise reality requires more than technical knowledge. In this bootcamp, you apply the Discover, Design, Deliver framework to diagnose business problems, assess organizational readiness, and scope AI pilots with clear success criteria. You navigate responsible AI tradeoffs, lead change management across cross-functional teams, evaluate agentic AI architectures for autonomy versus control, and build phased scaling strategies from proof of concept through production deployment.

sessions.title: The Amplification Effect: How AI Sharpens the Builder
sessions.abstract: Replacement anxiety dominates the AI conversation, but builders who use AI as a daily collaborator are discovering the opposite: AI amplifies human capability. This breakout session presents a practical framework for using AI tooling as a skills accelerator. We'll show how builders who integrate AI into daily workflows develop stronger critical thinking, faster adaptability, and deeper domain reasoning. Drawing from real-world examples, you'll learn how the act of collaborating with AI and refining its direction builds the exact human capabilities organizations need most. Walk away with a progression model from proficiency to mastery and techniques to start sharpening your skills immediately.

sessions.title: How T&C Empowers Partners to Build AI-Ready Teams and Drive Customer Impact?
sessions.abstract: Join this session to discover how AWS Training and Certification empowers partners to transform their workforce through strategic AI skills development. A partner shares their firsthand journey of designing AI learning pathways, implementing gamification that drove engagement at scale, and building sustainable certification programs tied to measurable business outcomes. You'll see how T&C enables this transformation, from foundational cloud fluency through advanced GenAI and Agentic AI readiness and leave with a concrete action plan to accelerate AI readiness across your teams.

sessions.title: AWS Certification & Proficiency Path: How to be Proficient in the Age of AI Agents?
sessions.abstract: Skills decay at unprecedented speed as AI reshapes what proficiency means. Certifications still validate expertise, but practitioners now need to demonstrate they can design, build, and optimize AI-powered systems alongside traditional cloud architecture. This lightning talk explains how AWS Training and Certification developed exam content, hands-on labs, and simulation-based assessments for agentic AI domains. You will also see how our team validated new competency frameworks, mapped learning paths to job roles, and built assessment experiences that measure real-world readiness rather than knowledge recall alone.

sessions.title: Lab Maker: From Prompt to Personalized Lab in Minutes
sessions.abstract: Lab Maker on AWS Skill Builder generates personalized hands-on labs from natural language prompts, allowing you to learn and experiment in the Console without incurring costs or risking production environments. During this session, we will generate a custom lab in real time before saving and sharing it with a team, demonstrating the full creation-to-collaboration workflow. We will then push Lab Maker further by generating a lab for a recently launched AWS service and uploading real organizational constraints to show how the tool adapts to your specific environment. You will leave this session with the knowledge and confidence to create your own labs.

sessions.title: Spec-Driven AI Development with Kiro
sessions.abstract: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) brings structure, traceability, and human oversight to every phase of high-velocity, Agentic-AI powered software delivery. In this bootcamp, apply AI-DLC in Kiro to build a production application through Feature Specs, control agent behavior with steering files and execution modes, extend capabilities with MCP servers and Kiro Powers, and automate workflows with hooks. Leave with a governed, repeatable process for shipping quality software with AI assistance.

sessions.title: Automate Penetration Tests with AWS Security Agent
sessions.abstract: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.

sessions.title: AI Powered Business Intelligence with Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Amazon Quick brings AI-powered analytics, automation, and research into a single workspace. In this bootcamp, build interactive dashboards and visualizations with Quick Sight, organize team knowledge resources in Spaces with appropriate permissions, create custom Chat Agents to surface insights conversationally, automate repetitive workflows with Quick Flows, and conduct multi-source research with proper validation. The three hands-on labs give you practical experience to apply these skills immediately in your organization

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Govern AI agents by hacking one first
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. Exploit a live AI agent with a prompt injection attack that approves a fraudulent transaction, then defend it. Fix it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to block prompt attacks and PII leaks. Verify it: prove your controls are in place with AWS Config conformance packs and find ungoverned AI resources with Resource Explorer. Observe it: trace agent decisions and guardrail interventions in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave ready to assess a customer's AI agents for governance gaps, protect them, and prove the controls work. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Agentic AI workflows for business users on Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. Walk through a hands-on business scenario using Amazon Quick, the agentic AI workspace that connects to your tools and learns your workflows. Create knowledge spaces, run deep-research agents, connect external APIs, automate multi-step processes with Flows, and build a custom AI agent in a browser. Leave able to help customers put agentic AI to work across their teams and business applications. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Build the AgentCore agent your demo pretends to be
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. A good prompt gets you a chatbot. Everything else on AgentCore turns it into an agent. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add persistent memory so it stops forgetting, tools through Gateway to reach real data, and Cedar policies that enforce boundaries, plus production traces, quality evaluations, and AI-driven optimization with A/B testing. Leave with hands-on experience on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and ready to show customers what separates a chatbot from an agent worth paying for. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified AI Practitioner
sessions.abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified AI Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Generative AI knowledge unlocks doors here. Enter a narrative-driven 3D world, choose your avatar, and tackle progressively harder puzzles tied to AWS Certified AI Practitioner exam domains. Each locked room blends exam-style questions with hands-on labs covering foundation models, responsible AI, prompt engineering, and agentic workflows. Collaborate with teammates, solve challenges under time pressure, and race to escape before your peers to top the leaderboard.

sessions.title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
sessions.abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Step into a 3D virtual world, choose your avatar, and race other players through rooms locked behind AWS Cloud Practitioner exam-style challenges. Each room combines interactive puzzles with hands-on labs that reinforce foundational cloud concepts like Compute, Storage, Networking, Security, and pricing models. Solve challenges collaboratively or compete solo, unlock rooms, and escape first to claim the leaderboard.

sessions.title: Automate Investigations to Resolve Application Failures with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

sessions.title: Build an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
sessions.abstract: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.

sessions.title: From our Agents to yours: Build, Optimize and Certify
sessions.abstract: AWS builds its certification exams, from foundational cloud to agentic AI, using production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this session, we show how we built our reasoning agents with AWS Well-Architected practices to solve real operational challenges: climbing latency, spiraling token costs, and non-deterministic failures. You’ll leave with concrete patterns to apply on AWS, plus a clear path to validate those skills through AWS Certification

sessions.title: Organize Enterprise Knowledge and Secure Data with Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Amazon Quick transforms how teams access insights and automate decisions. In this SimuLearn session, you design Spaces in Quick to organize enterprise knowledge, configure custom Chat Agents with specialized instructions and curated knowledge bases, and integrate Quick with enterprise systems using Actions and connectors backed by Amazon S3 or Amazon DynamoDB. You then apply row-level and column-level security controls to protect sensitive data and explore Quick Research for comprehensive multi-source analysis and reporting.

sessions.title: Go from Code to Deployed Agent with AgentCore CLI
sessions.abstract: Go from zero to a deployed, observable AI agent in under an hour. Use the AgentCore CLI to scaffold a Strands agent with a custom tool, test it locally against the Runtime contract, then deploy to AgentCore Runtime via CDK. Invoke the agent to demonstrate session isolation, inspect automatic CloudWatch logs and X-Ray traces, and confirm the framework-agnostic contract by replacing the agent with a plain Python function.

sessions.title: Evaluate Enterprise AI Agents with an Eval-First Approach (Workshop Studio)
sessions.abstract: A successful agent demo does not guarantee production readiness because agents can behave inconsistently across question types and multi-turn sessions. In this spotlight lab, you build two custom evaluators for an agent: THELMA, which scores single-turn RAG quality across seven dimensions including hallucination detection via groundedness scoring, and Mind the Goal, which computes Goal Success Rate across entire conversations and attributes failures to root causes. You register both as native AgentCore evaluators, run batch evaluations, and use diagnostic outputs to pinpoint exactly what to optimize first.

sessions.title: Agentic AI Powered DevOps and Security Engineering with AWS Frontier Agents
sessions.abstract: Application failures and security vulnerabilities demand fast answers to reduce downtime. In this bootcamp, learn how to setup AWS DevOps Agent and automate investigation failures through logs, metrics, and code changes, then generate remediation plans. Learn how to use AWS Security Agent to configure domain-scoped penetration tests, monitor real-time execution, and interpret severity-rated findings. Gain hands-on experience with two agents that compress hours of investigation into minutes.

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI workflows fail in ways that don't show up until production: a human misses the deadline, an external system says no, a sub-workflow loses state mid-flight. Fix it. Combine Step Functions, Lambda durable functions, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore into a three-layer stack that routes decisions, checkpoints execution, and reasons through uncertainty. Run real scenarios through the Simulator Panel and trace every layer live. Leave ready to build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
sessions.abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate by playing this 3D virtual escape room game. Enter a 3D virtual environment, select your avatar, and navigate rooms locked behind AWS Solutions Architect Associate challenges and design your way out. Build VPCs, select storage and database services, configure high availability, and implement fault-tolerant architectures while solving exam-aligned puzzles and completing hands-on labs. Each room builds on the previous, testing progressively deeper architectural knowledge. Collaborate with peers or compete solo and escape first to claim the leaderboard.

sessions.title: Validate your hands-on AWS skills & earn a Microcredential
sessions.abstract:
In this session, you will be given time to attempt a microcredential exam of your choice on AWS Skill Builder. These timed, hands-on exams test your skills in a live, provisioned AWS environment and test on popular topics. 

The product and developer team will be onsite to walk you through the UI and introduce the exam. Please note - this is an individual exam, and you will not be provided any hints or guidance outside of what is provided in the typical test environment. This exam is free to take on AWS Skill Builder. 

Attendees are required to bring their own device to complete the exam. Those who pass will be issued a microcredential badge on Credly.

sessions.title: Enhance Production Applications with AI-Assisted Development in Kiro
sessions.abstract: Enhancing production apps requires balancing delivery velocity with code safety. Kiro gives you both. In this hands-on lab, add features to enhance a live application using AI-assisted development on Kiro. Define coding standards with steering files and specs, generate UI components from natural language prompts, automate quality checks with agent hooks, install powers for domain expertise, and delegate backend analysis to custom subagents. Deploy your changes confidently to production environments.

sessions.title: Build Reliable AI Agents on AWS with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: When your data changes frequently, RAG helps your agent access the latest information at query time. Fine-tuning an LLM with domain data brings precision in how the agent responds and executes. In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

sessions.title: Modernize .NET Applications with AWS Transform and Kiro
sessions.abstract: Legacy .NET Framework applications tied to Windows limit your deployment options and increase operational costs. In this lab, you use AWS Transform for .NET in Interactive Mode to automatically port a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor application. You review the AWS Transform generated assessment report and migration plan, accept the automated transformation, then use Kiro to identify and fix the residual runtime issue that remains after the port.

sessions.title: Context-Aware Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory
sessions.abstract: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.

sessions.title: Orchestrate AI Agents with AgentCore Runtime
sessions.abstract: You need more than one agent to reason across inventory, shipments, forecasts, and suppliers at the same time. In this lab, you deploy a multi-agent supply chain system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. You load data into DynamoDB, build container images with CodeBuild, and deploy specialist agents plus a supervisor orchestrator powered by Amazon Nova models. The orchestrator classifies questions, routes them to the right specialists in parallel, and synthesizes their responses into one coherent answer.

sessions.title: Build Wealth Advisor Agents with Full-Stack Agent Architecture
sessions.abstract: In this SimuLearn session, you leverage the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform ito build production-grade wealth management advisor. You create Memory resources for client personalization, configure a Gateway with MCP tool targets for account and market data, deploy specialist agents and a supervisor to Runtime, and authenticate users through Cognito. The result is a multi-agent advisor that recognizes each client, remembers their goals, and produces auditable financial guidance through governed tools.

sessions.title: Spec-to-Agent Fitness App Deployment with Kiro and Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.abstract: In a simulated scenario, Fitness trainers waste 30 minutes daily on manual data entry and cannot spot trends across clients. In this SimuLearn session, you build FitTrack AI using Kiro's spec-driven workflows and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You design flexible schemas, create agent tools for client management and natural language analytics, deploy the agent on ECS Fargate, configure Bedrock Guardrails for health safety, and implement anomaly detection using database change streams.

sessions.title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
sessions.abstract: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.

sessions.title: Building Advanced Agentic AI Systems on AWS
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent systems unlock powerful workflows, but production demands more than chaining agents together. This bootcamp covers advanced patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement agent-as-tool communication, share memory across agents, optimize context windows for cost and performance, and secure deployments with policy-based access control and VPC integration. Configure distributed tracing, build evaluation frameworks, and design deployment strategies that take your agentic systems from prototype to production-ready state.

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Ship an AI agent without crossing your fingers
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI agents work great in demos but break in production. Replace luck with observability. Prototype a role-based agent with the Strands SDK. Evaluate it with custom evaluators for quality and compliance. Deploy it to production on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Observe it with OpenTelemetry tracing and CloudWatch dashboards. Detect drift by evaluating production traffic at scale. Leave ready to take a customer's AI agent from prototype to production-grade. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build Self-Service AI Experiences with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents
sessions.abstract: Customers expect instant answers about their orders, accounts, and open cases. In this hands-on lab, build a self-service AI agent in Amazon Connect that autonomously resolves customer requests by looking up profiles, searching and creating cases through MCP tools, and retrieving FAQ answers from a knowledge base. Configure AI Guardrails for content safety and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context for human agents.

sessions.title: Integrate Agents with MCP Servers and Tools using AgentCore Gateway
sessions.abstract: Your agent may handle basic conversations well, but to take real-world actions it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this hands-on lab, use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tools with JWT authorization. Register tool targets, connect to a pre-deployed nutrition coach agent, and validate how it dynamically discovers and invokes new capabilities at runtime without redeployment.

sessions.title: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
sessions.abstract: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.

sessions.title: Ship AI Agents Faster with AgentCore Harness
sessions.abstract: Building a production-ready AI agent meant writing orchestration code, packaging containers, and managing deployment pipelines. AgentCore Harness eliminates all of that. In this hands-on lab, you declare what your agent does through configuration and let AgentCore handle the execution loop. You create a harness agent, iteratively add tools, attach AWS Skills, swap models mid-session to suit your output requirements, and publish versioned endpoints for safe rollout to your customers.

sessions.title: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
sessions.abstract: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.

sessions.title: Spec-to-App Development with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. In this SimuLearn session, you build a city event management application by guiding Kiro through its spec-driven workflow: generating EARS-format user stories, reviewing architecture decisions, and executing a sequenced task list that produces a working MVP. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.

sessions.title: Streamline Claims Processing with Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Claims adjusters spend hours retrieving policy data, applying business rules, and drafting decision letters manually. In this SimuLearn session, you use Amazon Quick Automate to orchestrate the entire claims process. You configure REST API and MCP connectors, build a multi-step workflow with Custom Agent steps, and chain together policy retrieval, rules validation, and AI-powered letter generation. The workflow handles missing data gracefully and stores audit-ready decision letters in S3.

sessions.title: Network Security for AI Agents on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: AI agents decide at runtime which endpoints to call, and that decision can bypass your security review. In this SimuLearn session, you deploy an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in VPC mode and route its outbound traffic through AWS Network Firewall. You configure a default-deny policy with an approved-domain allow list, then prove it works: an approved call succeeds while an unapproved call gets dropped. The firewall log becomes your audit evidence.

sessions.title: AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC)
sessions.abstract: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) reimagines how teams plan, build, and ship software with AI as a first-class participant. In this bootcamp, learn the three phases (Inception, Construction, Operation) , apply the Intent-Unit-Bolt framework to decompose requirements into AI-executable work items, then use Kiro IDE's Spec-Driven Development to generate domain models, application code, tests, and infrastructure. You leave with a working application built entirely through the AI-DLC methodology.

sessions.title: Agentic Modernization with AWS Transform (Workshop Studio)
sessions.abstract: AWS Transform orchestrates AI agents that analyze, refactor, and convert legacy applications without manual line-by-line rewrites. In this bootcamp, set modernization objectives, let AI agents decompose and transform .NET Framework code to cross-platform .NET on Linux, then migrate a SQL Server database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Practice agentic assessment, wave planning, code transformation, and schema conversion end to end.

sessions.title: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
sessions.abstract: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.

sessions.title: AWS Partner: Your agent can wait. Go fix the app it depends on.
sessions.abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. An agent is only as reliable as the services it calls. Before you fix anything, you need to know exactly what's broken. In this workshop you stress-test that claim — probing a service for gaps that break autonomous invocation, reading the findings against your own predictions, and making the call on what gets fixed first. Leave with a ranked fix list and a method that transfers to any service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Resolve and Prevent Production Incidents with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: AWS DevOps Agent investigates production incidents end-to-end: tracing failures to the responsible change, guiding the fix, and verifying recovery. Once the service is stable, the agent converts root cause findings into automated prevention rules that enforce mandatory review gates on the same class of risk in future deployments. In this SimuLearn session, experience the full investigate, resolve, and prevent lifecycle as one continuous workflow in a single session.

new.title: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
new.abstract: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

new.title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
new.abstract: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.
