new.title: Building a cost governance framework that scales
new.abstract: As your cloud footprint grows, so does the challenge of keeping costs accountable. In this chalk talk, we'll open with common cost governance challenges and then dig into how the AWS FinOps Agent and AWS cost management tools can address them. Together we'll whiteboard approaches for organizing cost data, setting budget guardrails, allocating spend back to the right teams, and building visibility across your organization. Bring your current FinOps challenges and leave with a repeatable governance model for financial sustainability.

new.title: Automate savings with AWS Billing and Cost Management services
new.abstract: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. Bring your questions and challenges.

new.title: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
new.abstract: Inconsistent tags and no clear picture of what runs where get worse as your AWS footprint grows across accounts. In this code talk, we build the automation that keeps tagging clean at scale. We write a tag policy that enforces the keys and values that matter, wire up an AWS Config rule and remediation runbook that flag and fix non-compliant resources, and query untagged resources across thousands of resources and many accounts. We group assets into applications to keep governance consistent as teams multiply. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root cause.

new.title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
new.abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

new.title: Turn log storage into log intelligence
new.abstract: Give your operations teams the full picture without jumping between tools. Learn how to bring logs, metrics, and traces into a unified data store for analytics and improved troubleshooting. Instead of just storing logs and treating logs as text to grep during an outage, use centralization rules that bring telemetry together across accounts and regions, telemetry pipelines that enrich and route data in flight, intelligence tiering that matches storage cost to query value, and AI-assisted log analytics that surface answers instead of waiting for you to ask the right question. This is about making logs work for you — not the other way around. You'll leave with a clear architecture for unified log analytics you can take back to your org and put into production.

new.title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS (customer)
new.abstract: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

new.title: Building AI-powered, app-centric unified observability
new.abstract: Your apps run everywhere, but you're still switching tabs to understand what's happening. In this session, we'll show how CloudWatch delivers AI-powered, app-centric infrastructure monitoring where you already work. We'll walk through how unified observability connects application health to underlying infrastructure across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, and how AI surfaces the insights that matter before you go looking. You'll see how CloudWatch shifts from reactive dashboards to proactive, intelligent monitoring that meets you where you are.

new.title: Correlate app signals to infra root cause in hybrid environments
new.abstract: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

new.title: Follow that log from pipeline to intelligence
new.abstract: You've got logs flowing from everywhere, but when an issue spans multiple accounts or regions, you're stuck jumping between consoles trying to piece together what happened. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the end-to-end path a log takes from ingestion pipeline to a unified data layer to log analytics. We'll break down where visibility gaps form and why. Learn how you can connect these layers to trace a problem across your entire environment without losing context.

new.title: Best practices for building an observability strategy
new.abstract: Many teams buy tools before they agree on what they actually need to observe, ending up with multiple dashboards and unnecessary alerts. Learn what to instrument, what deserves an alert, how to set SLOs tied to real user experience, and how to keep the noise down as you grow. We will talk through the operating model decisions that make or break observability, such as who owns the tool, who pays for it, and how on-call actually works. Get a strategy framework and maturity checklist you can bring back to your leadership and engineering teams.

new.title: Learnings from resilience testing in AWS
new.abstract: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.

new.title: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
new.abstract: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.

new.title: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
new.abstract: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.

new.title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
new.abstract: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

new.title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
new.abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

new.title: Analyze your telemetry data with natural-language queries
new.abstract: During high-severity incidents, dependency on a single engineer who knows the query language creates critical bottlenecks. This code talk explores the architecture and design trade-offs behind a natural-language query workflow that translates plain-language questions into executable queries across metrics, logs, and traces. Live coding demonstrates how to integrate AI-powered query capabilities, correlate telemetry signals from a unified interface, and surface root-cause insights without writing query syntax. You'll see the underlying prompt construction, query translation patterns, and signal correlation strategies that drive reliable observability workflows in production environments.

new.title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
new.abstract: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.

new.title: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
new.abstract: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.

new.title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
new.abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.

new.title: Capital One's WorkSpaces Journey: 320 to 20,000 Desktops in 72hrs
new.abstract: Learn how to achieve enterprise-scale cloud desktop deployment from Capital One, who went from 320 manual provisions per day to 20,000 compliant desktops in 72 hours during a major merger integration. Gain production-tested architectural patterns for meeting compliance requirements without slowing delivery. You'll also get a first look at the latest WorkSpaces innovations and our vision for the future of cloud desktops, including how we're expanding what's possible for IT teams managing modern workloads at scale. This session is for those migrating from VDI, scaling an existing fleet, or planning for what's next.

new.title: Create reusable transformation rules for Java modernization at scale
new.abstract: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.

new.title: How A Customer Met Surge Hiring in Hours, Not Weeks
new.abstract: You expanded fast, but your hiring didn't keep up. What started as seasonal growth has become a scramble of manual screening, scheduling delays, and fragile workarounds that can't keep pace with your brand — forcing the impossible choice between speed and quality. Hear how Universal Studios replaced weeks-long hiring with Amazon Connect Talent, putting AI teammates to work running science-backed candidate assessments and AI-led interviews that take candidates from application to same-day offer — evaluated on the substance of their answers. Built on AWS with Amazon's proven hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent ensures recruiters stay in control of every decision.

new.title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
new.abstract: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

new.title: How Bayer designed 50K proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
new.abstract: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.

new.title: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
new.abstract: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

new.title: AWS Marketplace checkout, your website, your brand
new.abstract: When a buyer on your website is ready to purchase, AWS Marketplace gives them a procurement path their company has already approved. AWS Marketplace Storefront brings that path onto your own domain, so you keep your brand, your journey, and your sales team's visibility. In this chalk talk we'll build one live: catalog selection, buyer routing, embedding on your domain, and wiring requests into your CRM.

new.title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
new.abstract: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

new.title: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
new.abstract: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

new.title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
new.abstract: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

new.title: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
new.abstract: Organizations go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You also explore the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned from real scenarios.

new.title: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
new.abstract: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.

new.title: The agent fabric: shipping your software into the agentic economy
new.abstract: Your customers' AI agents won't stop at your product boundary. They expect your data, workflows, and agents to be reachable. If you're not, someone else will be. This workshop teaches the agent fabric pattern for making software products interoperable in the agentic economy: cross-organization agent discovery, cross-account identity, and the A2A protocol. Register specialist agents in AWS Agent Registry so a customer's coordinator can discover your capabilities, build that coordinator with the Strands Agents SDK, and wire cross-account trust and observability with AgentCore Identity and Observability. Leave with the pattern for shipping your product into the agentic economy.

new.title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
new.abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.

new.title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
new.abstract: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

new.title: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
new.abstract: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework. We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

new.title: Accelerate application development with Amazon ECS Express Mode
new.abstract: What if deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS required just your code and a few configuration choices? Amazon ECS Express Mode makes that possible by handling observability, networking, and security out of the box. In this session, learn how Express Mode accelerates development for individual developers and platform teams without sacrificing control. Discover practical techniques to optimize your workflows, enhance reliability, and reduce operational overhead. Leave with actionable strategies to increase development velocity using the latest Amazon ECS innovations.

new.title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
new.abstract: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

new.title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
new.abstract: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.

new.title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
new.abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.

new.title: Orchestrate multi-layer disaster recovery for critical workloads
new.abstract: Your AZ recovery plan and your Region failover plan were probably built by different teams, tested at different times, and have never run together. The result: untested failover paths that turn outages into incidents. Explore how to build a unified recovery framework with Amazon Application Recovery Controller. From zonal autoshift for rapid single-AZ mitigation, to Region switch for cross-Region failover, learn how ARC unifies both layers into a single orchestrated approach. Then discover how to run automated resilience tests that continuously validate your recovery posture before a real event forces the question.

new.title: Simplify multicloud: manage and monitor VMs in one place
new.abstract: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

new.title: AIOps strategy: foundations before firefighting
new.abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before deciding what they actually want it to handle, investment is racing ahead of maturity. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We map the two halves that teams miss: using AI to run operations and the operational foundations that let AI scale safely, such as cost, security, and organizational readiness. We discuss what to automate, what stays human, and where agents earn autonomy. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity checklist for your team.

new.title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
new.abstract: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

new.title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
new.abstract: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you manage the loop or let AWS handle it? In this code talk, we break down two approaches: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a fully managed agent loop with built-in memory and tool routing, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime for when you need full control. Then we sketch how AWS DevOps Agent's remote MCP support enables headless, tight-loop integration with your custom agents. Bring your architecture challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust agentic pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

new.title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
new.abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

new.title: Agentic AI Jam - brought to you by Nvidia [REPEAT of GHJ308]
new.abstract: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Are you ready to build and deploy agentic AI solutions on AWS? We provide hands-on environments where you can architect intelligent and production-ready agents. How do you orchestrate multi-step agent reasoning with tool use? How can you design agents that plan, act, and self-correct autonomously? Whether you are new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this Jam is your chance to demonstrate your skills and learn new ones. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to accelerate your agentic AI expertise. Team up, compete with others, climb the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. With expert guidance every step of the way, all you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

new.title: AWS Jam: All-in Builder Showdown [REPEAT of GHJ311]
new.abstract: Join the 2026 All-In Builder Showdown featuring hands-on environments where you will tackle Agentic AI, Intelligent DevOps automation, and AI-powered cloud security. Build autonomous agents that reason and act, automate deployments with AI-driven pipelines, and architect self-healing security defenses. Whether you are new to AWS or an experienced Cloud Ninja, this is your chance to shine and learn. Our challenges span all skill levels, with helpful clues and AWS expert support throughout. Team up in groups of four, complete challenges, and climb the leaderboard for prizes based on speed and accuracy. Connect with fellow builders, expand your AWS expertise, and master these essential cloud domains. Register now and go all in!

new.title: GPU orchestration at scale using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
new.abstract: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions from the cloud to the edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unsharable integers. In this L400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision an EKS cluster with NVIDIA L4 nodes, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time. Leave with a reproducible pattern for maximizing GPU utilization across competing workloads without over-provisioning.

new.title: How Citizens Bank reimagined CX with Amazon Connect and generative AI
new.abstract: Citizens Financial Group is transforming its customer service ecosystem using Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, and generative AI. In this session, learn how Citizens migrated legacy IVR and contact center infrastructure to Amazon Connect, deployed conversational AI across voice and digital channels, and integrated generative AI-powered agent assist and real-time conversation intelligence. We cover the solution architecture spanning Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge, along with measurable outcomes in containment rates, handle time, and routing accuracy. Attendees will gain a practical blueprint for enterprise-scale customer experience transformation in financial services.

new.title: How Ramp tracks and governs AI spend down to the team, model, and API key
new.abstract: When AI token spend spans multiple providers and dozens of teams, knowing who spent what, on which model, and whether it's COGS or OpEx requires its own pipeline. We'll cover ingesting usage data from third-party AI APIs, processing with Temporal workers, persisting on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, running on Amazon ECS Fargate, and surfacing anomalies before they hit your invoice. See how Ramp attributes spend by provider, model, team, and API key, and attributes cost down to the request-level when teams connect their router, gateway, or internal data. Learn how Ramp separates COGS from OpEx for accurate unit economics, then closes the loop with governance.

new.title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
new.abstract: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers - AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Leave with battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

new.title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
new.abstract: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response - across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

new.title: Parse, verify, cut over: Accelerating CDN migrations to Amazon CloudFront
new.abstract: CDN migrations rarely fail on feature gaps - they fail on semantics: cache keys that fragment silently, TTL precedence that behaves differently under load, and edge logic that resists one-to-one translation. In this session, dive deep into the engineering discipline behind large-scale migrations to Amazon CloudFront. Learn how AWS-built migration tooling converts third-party CDN configurations into CloudFront infrastructure as code and produces coverage reports that scope the work automation can't do. Then go beyond conversion into parity verification with traffic replay and cache hit ratio baselining, progressive DNS cutover with engineered rollback, and cache warming that protects day-one performance. Also learn how AWS Partners provide hands-on-keyboard migration support at scale.

new.title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
new.abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors - but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

new.title: Unify cross-cloud identity with AWS Identity Center and OIDC
new.abstract: Organizations running workloads across AWS and GCP face a common challenge: securing cross-cloud access without long-lived credentials or bespoke plumbing. In this session, learn how REA Group standardizes on OpenID Connect to solve both human and machine cross-cloud identity. Explore how AWS Identity Center consolidates workforce access, while Workload Identity Federation replaces Vault-based models with short-lived OIDC tokens for AWS roles, CI/CD pipelines, and Kubernetes workloads. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for building a unified identity mesh across clouds without static keys or centralized bottlenecks.

new.title: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
new.abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning  is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint -  all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

new.title: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
new.abstract: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.

new.title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
new.abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters, leveraging native OIDC providers from GKE and Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, and federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

new.title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
new.abstract: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

new.title: How Adobe unified multicloud observability with open source
new.abstract:
Adobe operates production services across AWS and Azure, but 20+ monitoring tools and per-cloud dashboards turned every cross-cloud incident into a translation problem before debugging could begin. In this session, hear how Adobe standardized on OpenTelemetry and consolidated to four open-source technologies (Cortex,
Grafana Tempo, FluentBit, and Grafana) with AWS as the operational hub processing 1M+ trace samples per second. The result was a single pane of glass for every engineer regardless of where workloads run, and multi-million dollar savings through telemetry compression. Walk away with a proven, vendor-independent playbook for multicloud observability built on open source and open standards.

new.title: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Specifications
new.abstract: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization — but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. In this chalk talk, we start from the foundational layers of compute, storage, and networking and build outward through data, security, observability, and AI. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability — and in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most. Along the way, we challenge common myths: that managed services equal lock-in, that Kubernetes equals portable, and that open source alone guarantees freedom. Through interactive whiteboarding, we'll design portable architecture patterns together — examining real trade-offs, open specifications like Apache Iceberg, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and MCP, and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.

new.title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
new.abstract: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

new.title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
new.abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

new.title: From Event Streams to Enterprise AI with Cloudera Anywhere Cloud
new.abstract: Distributed edge assets, remote sensors, and transactional systems often leave operational data isolated from enterprise AI platforms. This session demonstrates how global organizations break down these operational boundaries using Cloudera Anywhere Cloud. Discover an event-driven architectural blueprint that standardizes real-time streaming, unifies hybrid pipelines, and routes live activity directly into downstream analytics and AI agents. Learn how a single operational standard across hybrid environments simplifies data sovereignty and enables real-time enterprise automation.

new.title: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI
new.abstract:
Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it.
What you'll learn
⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots
⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve
⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments
⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps

new.title: Hands-On Workshop: Build & Deploy AI Agents with Cloudera Agent Studio
new.abstract: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera Agent Studio. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will build multi-agent workflows without code, develop agentic chatbots for data access, learn Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration with AWS tools including Amazon Bedrock and PuppyGraph, and explore the latest Cloudera AI and Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments.

new.title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike
new.abstract: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments.

new.title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS
new.abstract: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps.

new.title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect
new.abstract: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation.

new.title: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery
new.abstract: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare.

new.title: Own Your Harness: Control Cost & Risk in Enterprise-Wide AI Adoption
new.abstract: The fastest way to lose control of AI is to let agents multiply without a harness. This talk walks through Presidio's journey from scattered pilots to enterprise-wide adoption, built on a custom orchestration layer that treats cost, identity, and policy as first-class concerns. Attendees will get an inside look at the architectural decisions, guardrails, and economic models that let us scale AI use predictably across the business. If you're weighing governance (cost and risk) against velocity, this is the playbook you want from day one.

new.title: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy
new.abstract: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at Resolve AI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions.

new.title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps
new.abstract: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment.

new.title: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI
new.abstract: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice.

new.title: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk
new.abstract: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project.

new.title: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS
new.abstract: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself.

new.title: Architecting for digital sovereignty: Choosing your AWS hybrid cloud infrastructure
new.abstract: Digital sovereignty requirements vary widely across government, defense, healthcare, and financial services. In this session, we use real-world case studies to compare architectural differences across AWS Dedicated Local Zones, AWS Outposts within the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and AWS Regions. We examine how data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and cryptographic key management differ across these options. We then demonstrate how to configure account access, data residency controls, and network ingress/egress policies for strict versus moderate requirements, including how to detect and prevent non-permitted data flows between hybrid infrastructure, the parent Region, and on-premises environments.

new.title: Applying the Well-Architected Framework to AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
new.abstract: AWS Outposts and Local Zones bring cloud closer to your users and data but introduce architectural decisions that do not exist in a purely cloud-native model. How do you design for resilience when infrastructure sits in your facility? What does security and cost optimization look like across hybrid topologies? In this chalk talk, we walk through the Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. We will draw out real-world patterns, discuss trade-offs, and build a practical mental model for well-architected hybrid solutions.

new.title: Deployment strategies for highly available edge applications
new.abstract: Organizations need to be able to deploy critical applications that are highly available and fault-tolerant at the edge. These workloads are often some of the most demanding in terms of durability and availability requirements. Deploying workloads on AWS hybrid cloud and edge computing services like AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts requires planning for networking, compute, storage, and other failure modes. In this chalk talk, dive deep into each of these services, review use cases, and examine reference architectures. Learn design considerations, deployment patterns, and best practices for high availability and disaster recovery.

new.title: Computing‑Power‑Cooling Synergy: Building the Future of Global Data Infrastructure
new.abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads is driving new demands for large-scale data center infrastructure, with challenges in power supply, high-density cooling, and system integration. In this session, we will share real-world deployment practices and introduce end-to-end infrastructure solutions, including highly reliable UPS power systems, liquid cooling technologies, and turnkey integrated solutions. We will explore how computing, power, and cooling synergy can optimize data center efficiency, improve deployment agility, and accelerate the development of AI-ready infrastructure.

new.title: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
new.abstract: Buying and selling media has long been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. Built on AWS, this converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.

new.title: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
new.abstract: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built the AI Media Center on AWS, a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish at the speed of live. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.

new.title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
new.abstract: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months—and extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Strands that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion-model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.

new.title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
new.abstract: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. We discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.

new.title: Skip Refactoring and Simplify Operations with Nutanix on AWS
new.abstract: Cloud migrations often stall when rewriting applications takes too long. As projects drag on, organizations are left managing a fragmented, expensive mix of on-premises and cloud silos. Nutanix Cloud Clusters on AWS addresses this friction by establishing a single control plane and a consistent operating model across environments. In this session, learn how to move workloads to AWS bare metal quickly without refactoring. Discover how to eliminate management silos, accelerate migration timelines, and simplify hybrid cloud operations.

new.title: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS
new.abstract: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows.

new.title: How Coupang cut security costs protecting billions of requests
new.abstract: Your traffic doesn't look like it did two years ago. AI-driven workloads, unpredictable spikes, and relentless growth mean your firewall infrastructure has to keep up or become the bottleneck. Coupang knows this firsthand: millions of e-commerce transactions daily across a massive AWS footprint, with complexity and cost rising in lockstep. In this session, hear how they rearchitected around AWS Network Firewall to scale automatically with their business, strengthened their security posture, and cut costs in the process. Walk away with their architecture patterns, the operational decisions that made it work, and new centralized firewall management capabilities you can apply to your own environment immediately.

new.title: Control What Goes Out: Egress Security for AI Workloads
new.abstract: Most AWS workloads rely on two fundamental outbound mechanisms—DNS queries and network connections—both of which can be abused for data exfiltration. Learn how to lock down both. We'll cover DNS Firewall enhancements to secure the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how integrating DNSFW with NFW delivers advanced, unified DNS security. We'll also explore URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protections to containerized and AI workloads—helping you achieve compliance and simplified operations at scale.

new.title: Architecting Firewalls on AWS: A Layered Defense Strategy
new.abstract: Automated traffic now exceeds half the web. L7 attacks are getting smarter. A single firewall isn't enough. This chalk talk explores how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together for layered protection. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including TGW-attached firewall patterns. We dig into trade-offs: centralized vs. distributed inspection, cost vs. latency, and when each service carries the load alone vs. when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams. We'll whiteboard protection that scales with your environment.

new.title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
new.abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.

new.title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
new.abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

new.title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
new.abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

removed.title: Amazon Bio Discovery: Architecting Beyond Antibody Design
removed.abstract: Amazon Bio Discovery is a new AI-powered application where scientists design antibody therapies using biological foundation models, AI agents, and integrated lab testing. Drug development, however, doesn't stop at validation. This chalk talk walks through Bio Discovery's capabilities, then architects a downstream pipeline connecting validated candidates to AWS HealthOmics for sequence characterization and liability screening, and Amazon QuickSuite for natural language querying of experiment outcomes and portfolio visualization. Whether evaluating Bio Discovery or already using it, this session provides architectural patterns for extending AI-powered discovery into full development pipelines.

removed.title: Amazon Connect Health: Integrating Agentic AI into Clinical Workflows
removed.abstract: In this session, you'll learn how EHR companies and providers can integrate Amazon Connect Health's point-of-care SDK-patient insights, ambient documentation, and medical coding-into clinical workflows, with a deployable reference implementation.

removed.title: Compliance-as-Code: IL2–IL6 Authorization in Weeks, Not Years
removed.abstract: The traditional Authority to Operate (ATO) process delays mission-critical software by years due to complex FedRAMP and DoD requirements. This session introduces Game Warden, Second Front's PaaS built on AWS-GovCloud that uses a "compliance-as-code" approach to accelerate approvals and deployments at all FedRAMP levels and DoD's Impact Levels 2, 4, 5, 6 and JWICs. Attendees will discover how a modernized shared responsibility model accelerates deployment from years to weeks. Whether you are a commercial provider or a government leader, learn to maintain CI/CD agility while satisfying rigorous zero-trust mandates to deliver software at the speed of relevance.

This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI workflows fail in ways that don't show up until production: a human misses the deadline, an external system says no, a sub-workflow loses state mid-flight. Fix it. Combine Step Functions, Lambda durable functions, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore into a three-layer stack that routes decisions, checkpoints execution, and reasons through uncertainty. Run real scenarios through the Simulator Panel and trace every layer live. Leave ready to build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption. You must bring your laptop to participate.
removed.take: Partner-only bootcamps get reshuffled constantly as re:Invent firms up its AgentCore curriculum, and this one reads like it got merged into a broader agentic-workflow bootcamp rather than killed outright. Durable functions for Lambda and AgentCore are both young enough that the demo content (the "Simulator Panel") probably needed another round of internal testing before AWS lets partners loose on laptops with it. Nothing sinister here, just the usual pre-launch churn of a session built around services that are still hardening.
removed.title: AWS Partner: Build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption

removed.abstract: AWS Firewall Manager helps how organizations deploy WAF, Shield Advanced, and Network Firewall across multi-account environments. This session covers best practices for defense-in-depth using Firewall Manager policies. We'll show how to best leverage Firewall Manager, whether you're rolling out AWS WAF, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, or AWS Network Firewall to hundreds of accounts. You'll leave this session with an actionable deployment blueprint.
removed.take: Notice the services list doesn't even match the abstract—ACM, KMS, and Secrets Manager are along for the ride while the actual content is Firewall Manager, WAF, Shield Advanced, and Network Firewall. That kind of metadata drift usually means the session got reworked or folded into a bigger Firewall Manager/network security talk and someone forgot to update the catalog entry before it was pulled entirely. Builders' sessions are also notoriously capacity-constrained and speaker-dependent, so a dropped facilitator or a scheduling collision is the boring but likely culprit. No black helicopters required, just conference-catalog entropy.
removed.title: Managing Firewall Policies at Scale

removed.abstract: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.
removed.take: Structured-outputs-as-a-security-boundary was always a spicy claim for a 300-level slot, and "attack them with real injection payloads" live on stage is exactly the kind of demo that gets quietly reconsidered after a dry run. Most likely explanation: the grammar-enforcement feature or its Claude/open-weight parity shifted enough between now and re:Invent that the talk's provider-differences section needed a rewrite, or it got folded into a broader agentic-security session. Nothing here smells like a launch embargo so much as a speaker or content scope issue.
removed.title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock

removed.abstract: Debugging distributed serverless applications used to mean stitching together X-Ray traces, CloudWatch logs, and custom metrics from multiple extensions. Lambda now emits OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs natively, no layers or extensions required. In this chalk talk, we cover setup and configuration, end-to-end tracing with API Gateway vended logs, and distributed tracing across Step Functions, EventBridge, and SQS. We also discuss observability for agentic workloads: tracking token consumption, tool call success rates, and workflow checkpoint state. Bring your observability questions, especially around cost at scale: sampling, filtering, and cardinality management.
removed.take: SVS334 has the smell of a session that got too big for its own abstract—native OTel, vended logs, Step Functions, EventBridge, SQS, and agentic-workload tracing is at least three chalk talks wearing a trenchcoat. My money's on a content merge, likely folded into a broader agentic-observability or Lambda launch session once the native OTel feature's GA messaging solidified. Chalk talks with this much service sprawl often get split or absorbed when the actual product scope firms up closer to re:Invent, and "token consumption tracking" reads like a feature that wasn't quite ready to be talked about in public yet.
removed.title: Serverless observability: Native OpenTelemetry and vended logs
